[project]
name = "mcp-hangar"
version = "2.31.0"
description = "Policy enforcement plane for MCP: every tool call ends in a verdict. Self-hosted, MIT."
readme = "README.md"
license = {text = "MIT"}
requires-python = ">=3.11"
authors = [
    {name = "Marcin Pyrka", email = "marcin@mcp-hangar.io"}
]
keywords = ["mcp", "model-context-protocol", "llm", "ai", "security", "policy-enforcement", "tool-poisoning"]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 5 - Production/Stable",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries",
    "Topic :: System :: Systems Administration",
]
dependencies = [
    # Pinned EXACTLY, not merely bounded. This pin is a contract with the SDK, and
    # what it protects against is a wrong wire, not an ImportError.
    #
    # Why exact: `_sdk_compat` shims SDK internals (`_lowlevel_server`,
    # `add_request_handler`, `MCPError`, `HANDSHAKE_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS`), the front
    # door installs its own `tools/list` and `tools/call` handlers, and the relay
    # registers `tasks/*` methods the SDK deliberately does not carry in
    # `SPEC_CLIENT_METHODS`. Any of those can change between two SDK releases
    # without a failing import, and 2.3.0 proved it: it stopped running the
    # `tools/list` handler before dispatch and asked `get_tool_input_schema`
    # instead, so every `Mcp-Param-*` check on a projected tool was silently
    # skipped (#1791) -- a deny that did not deny.
    #
    # How to move it: run the weekly canary against the candidate (#1793), then
    # the full integration tier, the relay smoke (`task-relay-smoke.yml`, by
    # dispatch) and the conformance workflow. A failure there is the pin doing its
    # job. Move `mcp` and `mcp-types` together to the same version, and raise the
    # floors in `scripts/check_dependency_floors.py` that the move implies.
    #
    # The v1 line on `main` solves the same class of problem with `>=1.28.1,<2`
    # (#561): both branches must be unable to follow the SDK somewhere their
    # code does not run. Do not widen either to match the other.
    "mcp==2.3.0",
    "mcp-types==2.3.0",  # v2 split protocol-types dist (imported directly as mcp_types); paired with mcp
    "structlog>=24.0.0",
    # Mirrors the floor `mcp==2.3.0` declares; we inherit it rather than choose it.
    # Declared at the same value so the metadata cannot claim an install that the
    # resolver can never produce (see scripts/check_dependency_floors.py).
    "pydantic>=2.12.0",
    # Capped below 1.0: httpx 1.0 drops `httpx.AsyncClient`, which this code
    # uses everywhere. Unbounded, `pip install --pre mcp-hangar` -- the install
    # the v2-preview docs recommend -- resolves httpx to 1.0.dev3 and the
    # gateway dies at startup. Same class as the `mcp` cap (#561): a dependency
    # allowed to walk into a major this code does not run on.
    "httpx>=0.25.0,<1",
    "prometheus-client>=0.19.0",
    # Security floors: pip leaves an already-installed version alone while it
    # satisfies the constraint, so a floor is what an existing environment keeps.
    # pyjwt 2.13.0 fixes CVE-2026-48522/48523/48524/48525/48526 and CVE-2026-32597;
    # 48524 and 48525 are pre-auth DoS on the JWKS path (`get_signing_key_from_jwt`).
    # 2.14.0 fixes PYSEC-2026-4140 and 4142..4152 (4145: an HMAC/asymmetric
    # allow-list accepts a non-canonical PEM public key as the HMAC secret);
    # 2.15.0 fixes PYSEC-2026-4141.
    # `[crypto]` because JWKS RS256/ES256 needs it; it arrived only via `mcp` before.
    "pyjwt[crypto]>=2.15.0",
    # 50.0.0 fixes CVE-2026-69247; 49.0.0 fixes CVE-2026-69248/69249.
    "cryptography>=50.0.0",
    # not imported directly; arrives via mcp/httpx/starlette. 4.14.2 fixes
    # GHSA-82r6-8w77-94w6 (TLSStream IDNA 2003 host name encoding) and
    # GHSA-5p39-cfhj-2xmp (process-pool workers blocked on undrained stderr).
    "anyio>=4.14.2",
    "pyyaml>=6.0",
    "docker>=7.1.0",
    "aiosqlite>=0.19.0",
    "typer>=0.12.0",
    "rich>=13.0.0",
    "questionary>=2.0.0",
    # not imported directly; declared to raise the floor inherited via mcp/starlette
    # (mcp alone asks for >=0.0.9). 0.0.31 fixes CVE-2026-53537..53540.
    "python-multipart>=0.0.31",
    "protobuf>=6.33.5",
    "jcs>=0.2.1",
    "click>=8.3.3",  # security floor: PYSEC-2026-2132 (click.edit() command injection); transitive via typer
    # not imported directly; uvicorn needs a WebSocket library to upgrade a
    # connection, and without one `/api/ws/events` answers 404 (#1676). Only the
    # Dockerfile installed it before. 16.0 is the first release with Python 3.14
    # wheels, above uvicorn[standard]'s own >=13.0 and every known advisory (<9.1).
    "websockets>=16.0",
]
[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = [
    "pytest>=9.0.3",  # security floor: CVE-2025-71176 (tmpdir handling)
    "pytest-cov>=4.1.0",
    "pytest-asyncio>=1.3.0",  # first release that admits pytest 9 (the pytest floor above)
    "pytest-timeout>=2.2.0",
    "pytest-benchmark>=5.1.0",
    # Parallel runs: CI passes `-n auto --dist loadfile` (see ci-core.yml).
    "pytest-xdist>=3.6.0",
    # Pinned, not a floor: this is the version CI lints with. A floor would let
    # every machine resolve a different ruff, which is how a rule that fires
    # locally stays invisible in CI. Dependabot bumps it (uv ecosystem), and CI
    # follows automatically because it installs from here.
    "ruff==0.17.0",
    "import-linter==2.15",
    "mypy>=1.8.0",
    "hypothesis>=6.90.0",
    "jsonschema>=4.20.0",
    # The discovery security check's HTTP client (security_validator.py). In a
    # deployment the kubernetes extra brings it; without it here the check is
    # skipped in every test run and its tests can only skip (#1756). Security
    # floor: the deps-floor-audit job refuses anything older than 3.14.4.
    "aiohttp>=3.14.4",
]
# The kubernetes discovery source imports this. Until now it was declared
# nowhere -- not a dependency, not an extra, not in the image -- so the source
# could not be constructed on any supported install: bootstrap took the
# ImportError path, logged `discovery_source_unavailable` and discovered
# nothing, while the guide, the cookbook and the config reference all described
# a working feature. `docker` is a base dependency, so its source always worked;
# this is the same standing for kubernetes.
# The fuzzing harnesses under `fuzz/`. Markered, not bare: atheris publishes
# manylinux x86_64 wheels for CPython 3.12-3.14 ONLY, so an unconditional entry
# would break `uv sync --all-extras` on this project's own 3.11 baseline and on
# every macOS machine. The invariants the harnesses assert live in
# `fuzz/invariants.py`, which imports nothing from atheris and is replayed by
# the normal test suite everywhere.
fuzz = ["atheris>=3.1.0; sys_platform == 'linux' and python_version >= '3.12' and platform_machine == 'x86_64'"]
kubernetes = ["kubernetes>=29.0.0"]
# 1.35 is the lowest release that installs beside the core dependencies:
# `opentelemetry-proto` requires `protobuf<6` through 1.34.x, and the core
# requires `protobuf>=6.33.5` (`mcp` alone already needs the API at >=1.28).
opentelemetry = [
    "opentelemetry-api>=1.35.0",
    "opentelemetry-sdk>=1.35.0",
    "opentelemetry-exporter-otlp>=1.35.0",
]
# The PostgreSQL stores import psycopg2 -- see `database_common.PostgresConnectionFactory`.
# This extra declared `asyncpg`, which appears nowhere in `src/` outside a docstring,
# so `pip install mcp-hangar[postgres]` installed a library nothing imports and left
# the driver unable to start (#779). Same failure shape as the kubernetes extra (#770),
# harder to notice because the extra existed and was merely wrong.
postgres = [
    "psycopg2-binary>=2.9.9",
]
# The truncation continuation cache's redis driver imports this (#1008). Same
# class as [postgres]: cluster-only, off the base install AND off `full` so a
# laptop stays small; the published image installs it (see Dockerfile).
redis = [
    "redis>=5.0.0",
]
full = [
    "fpdf2>=2.8.0",
]
[project.scripts]
mcp-hangar = "mcp_hangar.server.cli:cli_main"
[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://mcp-hangar.io"
Documentation = "https://mcp-hangar.io/docs/getting-started/quickstart"
Repository = "https://github.com/mcp-hangar/mcp-hangar"
[build-system]
# hatchling is PINNED. 1.32.1 (published 2026-09-16) loads a builder plugin
# chain whose binary builder imports the `hatch` CLI package
# (`hatchling/builders/binary.py`: `from hatch.plugin.manager import
# PluginManager`). That package is NOT present in the isolated build env that
# `hatch build` and `python -m build` each create from this `requires` list, so
# every build path died with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'hatch'` --
# the Docker image, the `build` CI job, `make build-core` and the release
# workflow. 1.32.0 is unaffected. See #1513.
#
# This one pin covers every path because all of them resolve the backend from
# this list. Before lifting it, check that a newer hatchling no longer imports
# `hatch` at plugin-load time, then prove it with `docker build .` and the
# `build` job -- not with a local `pip install`, which has `hatch` on hand and
# therefore cannot reproduce the failure.
requires = ["hatchling==1.32.4"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"
[tool.hatch.build]
exclude = ["/.github/brand"]
[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/mcp_hangar"]
[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.force-include]
"src/mcp_hangar/py.typed" = "mcp_hangar/py.typed"
[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
# The sdist ships what it takes to build and test the project from source, and
# nothing that is an artefact of having built it here. `scripts/` stays because
# the test suite imports it (`tests/unit/test_api_route_inventory.py` reads
# `scripts.dump_api_routes`), so dropping it would ship a tests/ directory that
# cannot run; `examples/` stays because the quickstart points at
# `examples/rugpull/` (#1193).
exclude = [
    ".github/brand",
    ".clusterfuzzlite",
    ".grimp_cache",
    ".import_linter_cache",
    "coverage.json",
]
[tool.ruff]
line-length = 120
target-version = "py311"
extend-exclude = ["packages/operator", "site", "dist"]
[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "N", "W", "UP", "B", "BLE001", "C4", "C90", "SIM"]
ignore = [
    "B007",
    "B011",
    "B017",
    "B024",
    "B027",
    "B904",
    "C401",
    "C416",
    "N806",
    "N818",
    "SIM102",
    "SIM103",
    "SIM105",
    "SIM108",
    "SIM110",
    "SIM117",
    "SIM118",
]
[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
# Cyclomatic complexity ceiling for NEW code. Everything above it today carries an
# explicit `# noqa: C901` naming its current score -- 16 functions, listed by
# `ruff check src --select C901`. That list is a debt ledger, not wallpaper: it is
# short enough to read, and each entry is visible to whoever next opens the
# function.
#
# 15 rather than mccabe's default 10 because 10 would have baselined 54 functions,
# and a 54-entry noqa list stops being read. Anything above 15 is indefensible in
# review, so the gate bites real monsters while leaving ordinary code alone.
#
# The rule: never add a noqa here. Lower the ceiling, or split the function.
max-complexity = 15

# Mypy strictness migration in progress (TASK-P1-5).
# Phase 1: baseline strictness with per-module debt overrides (DONE).
# Phase 2: clean union-attr + attr-defined site by site.
# Phase 3: enable disallow_untyped_defs, drop all per-module overrides.
# Goal: zero overrides + strict = true by 2026-Q4.
[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.11"
strict = false
warn_return_any = true
warn_unused_ignores = true
warn_redundant_casts = true
warn_unused_configs = true
disallow_untyped_defs = false      # TODO(mypy-phase-3): enable
disallow_incomplete_defs = false   # TODO(mypy-phase-3): enable
check_untyped_defs = true
no_implicit_optional = true
show_error_codes = true
ignore_missing_imports = true
# disable_error_code intentionally absent -- per-module overrides below
# carry the technical debt explicitly. Goal: zero per-module overrides
# by 2026-Q4 (tracked in the issue tracker; see TODO(mypy-phase-3) above).
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
    "docker.*",
    "yaml.*",
    "prometheus_client.*",
    "kubernetes.*",
    "psycopg2.*",
    "opentelemetry.*",
    "watchdog.*",
    "aiohttp.*",
    "httpx.*",
    "structlog.*",
]
ignore_missing_imports = true

[tool.coverage.run]
# branch = true lives HERE, not only on the command line, for two reasons.
# 1. The decision-path floors are BRANCH numbers. A floor compared against
#    statement-only data silently passes a lower bar than it claims.
# 2. Modes do not mix: combining a statement-mode .coverage with a branch-mode
#    run raises `coverage.exceptions.DataError: Can't combine branch coverage
#    data with statement data` as a pytest INTERNALERROR. Making every run
#    branch-mode removes the mixed state entirely.
branch = true
relative_files = true

[tool.coverage.report]
# Deliberately NO fail_under. coverage.py's threshold is GLOBAL -- there is no
# per-file setting -- so a single number would have to be low enough for the
# weakest module in the tree, which is exactly the modules that need the
# strongest guarantee. Per-module floors live below and are checked by
# scripts/check_decision_coverage.py.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Decision-path coverage floors
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A module is a DECISION PATH when a wrong branch produces a wrong allow/deny:
# authorization, human consent, egress and tool-access policy, supply-chain
# digest pinning. An untested branch there is a security defect, not a style
# complaint, so these modules get a floor and the rest of the tree does not.
#
# Values are combined line+branch coverage as MEASURED on this branch, rounded
# down -- not an aspirational 90. A gate that is red the day it lands teaches
# people to skip it; this one is green on arrival and catches regressions from
# the first commit. Raising a floor is the unit of progress
# (`check_decision_coverage.py coverage.json --bump` locks in what was gained).
#
# Floors are measured on the Python the GATE runs (3.11 in the decision-coverage
# job), not on a developer's interpreter. Branch-arc counts differ between CPython
# versions: server/tools/batch/executor.py measures 85.38 on 3.13 and 85.06 on
# 3.11, so a floor taken from 3.13 failed CI on arrival. When a floor moves, take
# the number from the CI job -- or the lower of the two if you have both.
#
#   server/tools/batch/executor.py at 84.5 -- deliberately below what anyone
#     measures locally. The module runs work on a thread pool with timeouts and
#     single-flight de-duplication, so a handful of branches fire or not
#     depending on scheduling. Measured: 85.38 three times on CPython 3.13,
#     85.06 twice on 3.11, and 85.06 then 84.75 on two CI runs of the same
#     tree. Local is reproducible; a loaded shared runner is not. The floor sits
#     under the lowest observed CI value rather than under the local one, so the
#     gate reports a real regression instead of the runner's mood.
#     Pinning those branches with deterministic tests would let this rise again.
#
# Two entries are visible debt rather than a target:
#   approvals/persistence/sqlite_approval_repository.py at 87.0 -- the store
#     holding approval state, tenant scoping and the arguments hash. Unit tests
#     use a fake repository; the real SQL of `transition` is exercised by the
#     multi-process race test (#1794) and the CLI resolve tests (#1778).
#   domain/value_objects/tool_access_policy.py at 84.2 -- _CompositePolicy's
#     merge and approval-list handling, i.e. the consent-preservation logic.
#   server/tools/batch/executor.py at 85.3 -- the invoke path, including the
#     455-line _execute_call_inner.
[tool.decision_coverage]
# How far a floor may sit below reality before it stops being a ratchet.
drift_allowance = 3.0

[tool.decision_coverage.floors]

  # 94.1 -> 96.0 when tests/unit/test_config_policies_are_adopted_in_one_step.py

testpaths = ["tests"]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
# No `addopts`. It used to carry `-v --cov=mcp_hangar --cov-report=term-missing`,
# which put an 18-second coverage pass and 6600 lines of per-test output on every
# local run, including runs of a single file. The jobs that read a coverage report
# ask for it explicitly, and the live tiers had to undo it with `-o addopts=""`

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=61.0", "wheel"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["."]
include = ["shopping*", "myproject*"]
exclude = ["tests*", "htmlcov*", "staticfiles*", "media*"]

# ==========================================
# Black Configuration (Code Formatting)
# ==========================================
[tool.black]
line-length = 127
target-version = ['py312']
exclude = '''
/(
    \.git
  | \.venv
  | venv
  | env
  | __pycache__
  | migrations
  | staticfiles
  | media
  | htmlcov
  | \.backup
)/
'''

# ==========================================
# isort Configuration (Import Sorting)
# ==========================================
[tool.isort]
profile = "black"
line_length = 127
skip_glob = ["*/migrations/*", "venv/*", "env/*", "htmlcov/*"]
known_django = ["django"]
known_third_party = [
    "rest_framework",
    "celery",
    "redis",
    "mptt",
    "allauth",
    "dj_rest_auth",
    "drf_spectacular"
]
known_first_party = ["shopping", "myproject"]
sections = ["FUTURE", "STDLIB", "DJANGO", "THIRDPARTY", "FIRSTPARTY", "LOCALFOLDER"]

# ==========================================
# pytest Configuration
# ==========================================
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE = "myproject.settings.test"
python_files = ["tests.py", "test_*.py", "*_tests.py"]
python_classes = ["Test*", "*Tests", "*TestCase"]
python_functions = ["test_*"]
addopts = """
    -n auto
    --dist=loadscope
    --cov=shopping
    --cov=myproject
    --cov-report=html
    --cov-report=term-missing:skip-covered
    --cov-fail-under=70
    --tb=short
    --strict-markers
    -m 'not load_test and not manual and not concurrency and not performance and not auth_race and not payment_race and not order_race and not point_race and not return_race and not heavy and not slow and not e2e and not requires_redis and not requires_db and not flaky'
"""
# selfhealing coverage는 별도 repo에서 측정 (https://github.com/gotoUSA/selfhealing-python)
testpaths = ["shopping/tests", "tests"]
markers = [
    "slow: marks tests as slow (deselect with '-m \"not slow\"')",
    "unit: marks tests as unit tests (fast, no external deps)",
    "integration: marks tests as integration tests",
    "e2e: marks tests as end-to-end tests (requires full infrastructure)",
    "performance: marks tests as performance tests",
    "load_test: load test related (excluded by default in CI)",
    "manual: manual/debugging tests (excluded by default in CI)",
    "concurrency: concurrency tests (race condition verification)",
    "auth_race: authentication related race condition tests",
    "payment_race: payment related race condition tests",
    "order_race: order related race condition tests",
    "point_race: point related race condition tests",
    "return_race: return related race condition tests",
    "heavy: high-load stress tests (optionally excluded in CI)",
    "schema: OpenAPI schema-based contract tests (Schemathesis)",
    "stateful: Stateful API workflow tests (state transition verification)",
    "fuzz: Fuzz tests - Hypothesis/Schemathesis based random input verification",
    "negative: Negative tests - proper error handling for invalid inputs",
    "security: Security tests - SQL Injection, XSS, SSTI attack defense verification",
    "chaos: Chaos engineering tests - fault injection and recovery verification",
    "compound: Compound failure tests - multiple failure modes simultaneously",
    # Self-Healing Test Tiers (Reference: docs/testing/SELF_HEALING_TEST_MATRICES.md)
    "tier1: Fast unit tests for PR validation (< 2 min, no external deps)",
    "tier2: Integration tests for merge to main (< 10 min, requires DB/Redis)",
    "tier3_chaos: Chaos engineering tests for nightly runs (< 30 min)",
    "tier4_load: Load and stress tests for releases (< 2 hours, dedicated runner)",
    # Self-Healing Domain Markers
    "tenant_aware: Multi-tenancy isolation tests (R-001)",
    "cost_sensitive: Cost-aware recovery tests (R-002)",
    "requires_redis: Tests requiring Redis connection",
    "requires_celery: Tests requiring Celery worker",
    "requires_db: Tests requiring database connection",
    "flaky: Tests with known flakiness (quarantined from CI)",
]
filterwarnings = [
    # Ignore dj-rest-auth deprecation warnings (library internal, cannot fix)
    "ignore:app_settings.USERNAME_REQUIRED is deprecated:UserWarning:dj_rest_auth.registration.serializers",
    "ignore:app_settings.EMAIL_REQUIRED is deprecated:UserWarning:dj_rest_auth.registration.serializers",
    # Ignore factory_boy deprecation warning (library internal)
    "ignore:.*_after_postgeneration will stop saving the instance.*:DeprecationWarning:factory.django",
    # Ignore coverage warnings from pytest-xdist parallel execution
    "ignore:No data was collected:coverage.exceptions.CoverageWarning",
    "ignore::coverage.exceptions.CoverageWarning",
    # Ignore CovReportWarning from pytest-cov
    "ignore::pytest_cov.plugin.CovReportWarning",
]

# ==========================================================================
# Test Logging: WARNING 이상만 출력하여 테스트 가독성 확보.
# 디버깅이 필요하면: SELFHEALING_TEST_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG pytest ...
# ==========================================================================
log_level = "WARNING"
log_cli_level = "WARNING"

# pytest-env: Set environment variables before test execution
# Resolves PostgreSQL cp949 encoding issue on Windows
[tool.pytest_env]
PGCLIENTENCODING = "UTF8"
PYTHONIOENCODING = "utf-8"
SELFHEALING_TEST_LOG_LEVEL = "WARNING"

# ==========================================
# coverage Configuration
# ==========================================
[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["shopping", "myproject"]
omit = [
    "*/migrations/*",
    "*/tests/*",
    "*/test_*.py",
    "*/__pycache__/*",
    "*/venv/*",
    "*/env/*",
    "manage.py",
    "myproject/wsgi.py",
    "myproject/asgi.py",
    "load_tests/*",
]
branch = true
# Parallel testing support (pytest-xdist)
parallel = true
concurrency = ["thread", "multiprocessing"]
# Explicitly set data file path
data_file = ".coverage"
# Do not retain existing data during parallel execution (measure fresh each time)
relative_files = true

[tool.coverage.report]
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "def __repr__",
    "def __str__",
    "raise AssertionError",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "class .*\\bProtocol\\):",
    "@(abc\\.)?abstractmethod",
]
precision = 2
show_missing = true
skip_covered = false

[tool.coverage.html]
directory = "htmlcov"

# ==========================================
# radon Configuration (Code Complexity)
# ==========================================
[tool.radon]
exclude = "*/migrations/*,*/tests/*,*/__pycache__/*,*/venv/*"
cc_min = "C"  # Show complexity C or above (A=1-5, B=6-10, C=11-20, D=21-30, E=31-40, F=41+)

# ==========================================
# bandit Configuration (Security Analysis)
# ==========================================
[tool.bandit]
exclude_dirs = ["tests", "migrations", "venv", "env", "htmlcov", "load_tests"]
skips = ["B101", "B311"]  # B101: assert usage, B311: random (non-security use)
targets = ["shopping"]

# ==========================================
# vulture Configuration (Dead Code Detection)
# ==========================================
[tool.vulture]
exclude = ["*/migrations/*", "*/tests/*", "venv/", "env/", "htmlcov/"]
min_confidence = 80
paths = ["shopping"]
sort_by_size = true

# ==========================================
# mutmut Configuration (Mutation Testing)
# ==========================================
# Not yet introduced in this project
# Will be introduced after core logic stabilization
#
# mutmut supports setup.cfg or [tool.mutmut] in pyproject.toml
# Limited to money-related services only
#

# ==========================================
# deptry Configuration (Unused Dependency Detection)
# ==========================================
# 사용: deptry .
# DEP001: 누락된 의존성, DEP002: 미사용 의존성, DEP003: 전이 의존성
[tool.deptry]
extend_exclude = [
    "load_tests",
    "tests",
    "htmlcov",
    "staticfiles",
    "media",
    "migrations",
]
# 내부/테스트 모듈 - DEP001 무시
ignore_missing = [
    "integrity",           # 내부 모듈 (상대 import)
    "wal",                 # 내부 모듈 (상대 import)
    "backports",           # Python 3.9+ 호환용 (3.12에서 불필요)
    "nonexistent_module",  # 테스트용 의도적 import
]

# CLI 도구 (import 안 함) - 오탐 무시
[tool.deptry.per_rule_ignores]

    # === CLI 도구 (터미널에서만 사용) ===

#

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py313"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "A",    # builtin shadowing
    "ARG",  # unused arguments
    "B",    # bugbear: likely bugs (B905 = zip without strict=)
    "BLE",  # blind except -- deliberate ones carry `# noqa: BLE001 -- <why>`
    "C4",   # comprehension / literal misuse
    "DTZ",  # naive datetimes -- the ledger already has a naive-local-time era
    "E",
    "F",
    "FLY",  # static join -> f-string
    "G",    # logging format
    "I",
    "ICN",  # import naming conventions
    "INT",  # gettext
    "ISC",  # implicit string concat
    "LOG",  # logging misuse
    "N",
    "PERF", # obvious perf smells
    "PGH",  # blanket noqa / type: ignore with no code
    "PIE",
    "PLC0415", # import inside a function -- deliberate ones carry `# noqa: PLC0415 -- <why>`
    "PLW1510", # subprocess.run without check= -- a swallowed exit code, again
    "PT",   # pytest style
    "PTH",  # os.path -> pathlib
    "Q",    # quote style
    "RET",
    "RSE",  # raise X() -> raise X
    "RUF",
    "SIM",
    "SLF",
    "SLOT", # __slots__ misuse
    "TC",   # annotation-only import -> `if TYPE_CHECKING:` (see flake8-type-checking)
    "TID",  # tidy imports
    "UP",
    "W",
]
ignore = [
    "RUF001",
    "RUF002",
    "RUF003",
    # G004 (f-string in a log call) does not pay for itself here: every such
    # line uses `{n:,}` formatting, which %-style cannot express, so the lazy
    # form would be `logger.info("%s rows", f"{n:,}")` -- worse to read, and
    # these are once-per-checkpoint lines, not a hot path. The rest of G still
    # catches real misuse (string concat / .format() in a log call).
    "G004",
    # ERA001 cannot tell a worked example from dead code, and this codebase
    # explains its arithmetic in comments: "# e_i = (u0 + u1) / 2" reads as
    # commented-out code to it. All four hits were false positives.
    "ERA001",
]

# TC assumes an annotation is never evaluated at runtime, and pydantic breaks
# that: it resolves field annotations to build the model, so a name hidden
# behind TYPE_CHECKING is a startup crash rather than a lint. Declared rather
# than left to inference -- the payload contract and the config schemas should
# not depend on a ruff version continuing to guess right. Two other runtime
# readers of annotations are NOT covered and must be added here if one ever
# appears in a moved import: a FastAPI route signature (request parsing is
# derived from it) and any dataclass reached by `get_type_hints`.
[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-type-checking]
# Both resolve their annotations at RUNTIME, so TC would move an import
# these classes need. SQLAlchemy is not theoretical: deferring `datetime`
# raises `MappedAnnotationError: Could not resolve all types within mapped
# annotation` at import, not at first use.
runtime-evaluated-base-classes = ["pydantic.BaseModel", "sqlalchemy.orm.DeclarativeBase"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"*.py" = ["E501"]
# Tests are full of deliberately-unused arguments: monkeypatch stand-ins that
# must match a real signature, and fixtures requested for their side effect.
# PLC0415 is off here because a test module ships nothing, and importing inside
# a test is how you import the module under test AFTER monkeypatching what it
# reads at import time, or keep a heavy optional dependency off the collection
# path (`conftest.py::requires_card_abstraction`).
"tests/**/*.py" = ["SLF001", "ARG001", "ARG002", "ARG005", "PLC0415"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
python_files = ["test_*.py"]
python_classes = ["Test*"]
python_functions = ["test_*"]
markers = [
    "slow: marks tests as slow (deselect with '-m \"not slow\"')",
    "timeout: test timeout in seconds",
]
# `-n auto` because the suite is dominated by a handful of genuinely expensive
# tests: 57 `slow`-marked ones carry 6m25s of the wall clock and the other ~2400
# are nearly free. Re-measured 08-24 at 2453 tests -- serial 12m22s full / 4m12s
# fast gate, across 12 workers 6m25s / 58s.
#
# Only the FAST GATE parallelises (4m12s -> 58s). The full suite does not, and
# the 6m25s is not a scheduling result: ONE test, `test_every_seven_card_hand`,
# runs 6m00s of it by itself. No worker count moves that floor -- splitting that
# test is the only thing that would.
#
# `--dist load` (the default) is what wins: `loadfile`/`loadscope` would pin a
# whole slow file to one worker and set the floor there, and `worksteal`
# measured no better. Do NOT add `--maxschedchunk=1` -- finer scheduling
# measured SLOWER, because these tests are CPU-bound and oversubscribing them
# costs more than the packing saves.
#
# To debug one test, `-n0` turns it off: worker startup and interleaved output
# are pure cost when there is nothing to parallelise.
addopts = "-v -n auto --durations=15"
# 60s, raised from 5 on 08-25. The old floor's rule was "if one flakes, mark
# THAT test, never raise this" -- and its evidence was 0 failures in 10 `-n auto`
# runs. That was measured on a quiet box. This one now carries several agent
# sessions at once, and the floor was found to be a load meter: three separate
# cohorts, ~20 distinct tests across nine files, each failing under `-n auto`
# and every one passing serially. Measured margins were 1.2-1.9x, not the 5x
# claimed (`test_unknown_scorer_rejected` 4.11s; three more at 2.6-2.9s).
#
# Twenty annotations would have been chasing it. A gate whose red carries no
# information is worse than no gate, so the budget is now sized for its real
# job -- catching a HANG -- and creeping slowness is surfaced by `--durations`
# above, which reports without failing. Explicit per-test marks of 30-180s
# still work and still win; nothing about them changes.
timeout = 60
timeout_func_only = true

[dependency-groups]
# Development, testing, and code quality tools
dev = [
    "pytest>=9.0.2",
    "ruff>=0.16.4",

# --- ruff: linter + formatter ----------------------------------------------
# Replaces black, isort, flake8, pyupgrade. Config aligned with the project's
# clean-code rules (type hints, docstrings on exports, no magic numbers, etc).
[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py313"
line-length = 100
extend-exclude = [
    ".venv",
    "alembic/versions",  # auto-generated migrations
    "workspaces",        # ephemeral runtime data
    # Vendored submodule — owned by openai/codex, lints under their rules
    # not ours. The submodule's own CI gates its style.
    "vendor",
    # Agentic tooling / editor metadata directories — never lint these.
    ".agents",
    ".claude",
    ".cursor",
    ".pi",
    ".opencode",
    ".crush",
    ".codex",
    ".beans",
    ".zed",
    ".vscode",
    ".sentrux",
]

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Strict ruleset. Each family adds a class of catch:
#   E, W    = pycodestyle errors/warnings
#   F       = pyflakes (unused imports, undefined names)
#   I       = isort (import sorting)
#   N       = pep8-naming (consistent naming conventions)
#   B       = flake8-bugbear (real bugs: mutable defaults, etc.)
#   A       = flake8-builtins (don't shadow builtins)
#   C4      = flake8-comprehensions (idiomatic comprehensions)
#   C90     = mccabe complexity (function complexity cap)
#   UP      = pyupgrade (modernize syntax for target Python)
#   SIM     = flake8-simplify (collapse redundant patterns)
#   ASYNC   = flake8-async (async/await footguns)
#   PERF    = perflint (avoid known-slow patterns)
#   PL      = pylint (subset)
#   PT      = flake8-pytest-style (idiomatic pytest)
#   PTH     = flake8-use-pathlib (prefer pathlib over os.path)
#   RET     = flake8-return (clean control flow on returns)
#   RUF     = ruff-specific (latest catches)
#   S       = flake8-bandit (security: hardcoded secrets, weak crypto, eval, etc.)
#   T20     = flake8-print (no stray print statements)
#   TID     = flake8-tidy-imports (banned-imports + relative-import policy)
#   TRY     = tryceratops (exception-handling antipatterns)
#   D       = pydocstyle (docstrings on public API — matches project rule)
select = [
    "E", "W", "F", "I", "N", "B", "A", "C4", "C90", "UP", "SIM", "ASYNC",
    "PERF", "PL", "PT", "PTH", "RET", "RUF", "S", "T20", "TID", "TRY", "D",
]
# Ruff's ``PLC2701`` (Pylint preview) would catch the cross-module
# private-import pattern described in
# ``.cursor/plugins/pawrrtal/rules/clean-code/python-module-privacy.mdc`` (issue #283).
# Today the codebase has ~124 existing violations (mostly tests
# importing module-level test helpers) so enabling the rule would
# fail CI on every PR.  The rule is documented for human + agent
# review; mechanical enforcement is a follow-up sweep, not this PR.
# When enabling: add ``"PLC2701"`` to ``select`` above and turn
# ``preview = true`` + ``explicit-preview-rules = true`` on.
ignore = [
    "E501",     # line length — handled by formatter, soft cap only
    "D100",     # missing module docstring (too noisy on small modules)
    "D104",     # missing docstring in __init__.py
    "D107",     # missing docstring in __init__ method (covered by class docstring)
    "D203",     # incompatible with D211 (no blank line before class)
    "D213",     # incompatible with D212 (multi-line summary on first line)
    "PLR0913",  # too many args — FastAPI handlers regularly need many deps
    "B008",     # function call in default arg — required for FastAPI Depends()
    "TRY003",   # long exception messages — over-prescriptive
    "TRY300",   # else-after-try — clearer to keep return inline for short paths
    "TRY301",   # raise within try — sometimes clearer for explicit re-raise
    "RET504",   # unnecessary assignment before return — assignment often aids readability
    "S101",     # assert in tests is fine (per-file ignore covers tests; this catches asserts in app code only)
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**" = [
    "D",       # tests don't need docstrings on every fn
    "PLR2004", # magic numbers in test data are fine
    "S101",    # assert is the whole point of pytest
    "S105",    # hardcoded password strings (test fixtures)
    "S106",    # hardcoded password (function arg)
    "S108",    # /tmp paths in test scenarios are fine
    "PT018",   # compound asserts in tests are fine if they're checking related state
    "PLC0415", # lazy/in-fn imports in tests are intentional: avoid module-load
               # side effects, isolate `importlib.reload` cases, and let fixtures
               # set env before the SUT is bound. Hoisting defeats those patterns.
]
"tests/conftest.py" = ["D", "E402"]   # sys.path manipulation must come before imports
"main.py" = ["E402"]                  # allow early logging configuration before other imports
"alembic/**" = ["D", "E", "I", "S"]   # migrations are auto-generated
"app/cli/**" = [
    "T20",   # CLI scripts legitimately use print
    "S603",  # subprocess calls in CLI are operator-driven, not user-input
    "S607",  # `git` and similar trusted binaries on PATH are intentional
]
"tests/test_alembic_postgres_upgrade.py" = [
    "S603",  # spawns the real `alembic` CLI (via sys.executable -m) on purpose:
             # the advisory-lock DDL-rollback bug only reproduces through a real
             # env.py connection lifecycle, not an in-process call. URL is built
             # from a test-controlled scratch DB name, not external input.
]

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports]

[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]

[tool.ruff.format]

# --- pytest -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Pinned to ``tests/`` so pytest never wanders into the vendored codex SDK's
# own test suite (``backend/vendor/codex/sdk/python/tests/``), which depends
# on the codex binary being available and fails in our CI environment.
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
norecursedirs = ["vendor", ".venv", "node_modules", "__pycache__", "*.egg-info"]
filterwarnings = [
    # google-genai defines an aiohttp.ClientSession subclass at import time.
    # aiohttp emits this deprecation from aiohttp.client before Pawrrtal code
    # can influence the SDK internals; keep the filter exact so first-party
    # warnings still surface.
    "ignore:Inheritance class AiohttpClientSession from ClientSession is discouraged:DeprecationWarning",
]

# --- mypy: static type checker ---------------------------------------------
# Strict-ish defaults. Project rule forbids cast(Any, ...), so we want mypy
# to surface real type holes rather than letting them slip through.
[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.13"
strict = true
# Targeted relaxations — strict mode is too loud against FastAPI/SQLAlchemy
# ecosystems where many third-party annotations are still incomplete.
warn_return_any = true
warn_unused_ignores = true
warn_redundant_casts = true
disallow_untyped_decorators = false  # FastAPI/pytest decorators trip this
# Required because ``app.models`` and ``app.api.models`` both end with ``models.py``
# — without explicit package bases, mypy can't disambiguate them.
explicit_package_bases = true
# Optional provider SDKs live behind plugin/provider boundaries; local stubs
# let strict checks run when a worktree has not initialized every SDK.
mypy_path = ".:typestubs:vendor/codex/sdk/python/src"
plugins = ["pydantic.mypy"]
exclude = [
    "alembic/versions/",
    "workspaces/",
    ".venv/",
    # Vendored submodules (e.g. backend/vendor/codex) follow their own
    # type conventions; mypy treats them as authoritative for the SDK
    # surface but the SDK's example scripts + ad-hoc tests are noisy.
    "vendor/",
    # Agentic tooling / editor metadata directories.
    "\\.agents/",
    "\\.claude/",
    "\\.cursor/",
    "\\.pi/",
    "\\.opencode/",
    "\\.crush/",
    "\\.codex/",
    "\\.beans/",
    "\\.zed/",
    "\\.vscode/",
    "\\.sentrux/",
    # Provider image translation is not implemented for every host yet.
    "tests/test_provider_images.py",
]
files = ["app", "tests", "main.py"]

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "tests.*"
disallow_untyped_defs = false  # test fixtures are fine without explicit types

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
# Vendored Codex Python SDK (``vendor/codex/sdk/python``) is on ``mypy_path``
# so ``import openai_codex`` resolves, but the generated sources are not held
# to Pawrrtal's strict gate.
module = "openai_codex.*"
follow_imports = "skip"

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
# Third-party packages without complete type stubs.
# xai_sdk ships generated protobuf classes without a ``py.typed`` marker;
# mypy can't follow the .pyi files the SDK omits.  The provider does its
# own narrow type-checking at the seam.
module = ["sqlalchemy_utils.*", "mcp.*", "markitdown.*", "xai_sdk.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
# google-auth ships ``py.typed`` but its service_account credential
# constructors are still untyped (``from_service_account_file`` returns
# ``Any``), so strict-mode ``disallow_untyped_calls`` / ``warn_return_any``
# fire at the call site. This module is the single, narrow boundary that
# touches google-auth; relax those two checks here only, rather than
# scatter inline ignores. Everything else in the module stays strict.
module = "app.channels.google_chat.auth"
disallow_untyped_calls = false
warn_return_any = false

[tool.setuptools]
include-package-data = true

[tool.setuptools.dynamic]
version = {attr = "deeptutor.__version__.__version__"}

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["."]
include = ["deeptutor*", "deeptutor_cli*"]

[tool.setuptools.package-data]
# Runtime data shipped inside the deeptutor package: prompt YAMLs (loaded by
# PromptManager from PACKAGE_ROOT/deeptutor/.../prompts/*.yaml), markdown
# templates (builtin SKILL.md files, vision_solver prompts), and helper shell
# scripts. Without these, ``pip install deeptutor`` ships a wheel missing
# every agent prompt and capability fails at first use.
deeptutor = [
    "**/*.yaml",
    "**/*.yml",
    "**/*.md",
    "**/*.json",
    "**/*.sh",
    "**/*.j2",
    "**/*.jinja",
]
deeptutor_cli = ["**/*.md"]
deeptutor_web = ["**/*", ".next/**/*"]

# ============================================
# Black code formatter configuration
# ============================================
[tool.black]
line-length = 100
target-version = ['py311', 'py312', 'py313', 'py314']
include = '\.pyi?$'
extend-exclude = '''
/(
  # Exclude directories
  \.eggs
  | \.git
  | \.hg
  | \.mypy_cache
  | \.tox
  | \.venv
  | venv
  | _build
  | buck-out
  | build
  | dist
  | __pycache__
  | node_modules
  | \.next
)/
'''

# ============================================
# Ruff linter and formatter configuration
# ============================================
[tool.ruff]
# Target Python version
target-version = "py311"
line-length = 100

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Enable only foundational lint rules (intentionally relaxed)
select = [
    "E",   # pycodestyle errors (语法错误)
    "F",   # pyflakes (未使用的导入、变量等)
    "I",   # isort (import 排序)
    # Keep only essential checks; other rules stay relaxed
]

extend-select = [
    "B006",  # Do not use mutable data structures for argument defaults
]

# Ignore specific rules (keep the lint profile relaxed)
ignore = [
    "E501",  # Line too long (handled by formatter)
    "B008",  # Do not perform function calls in argument defaults
    "PLR0911", # Too many return statements
    "PLR0912", # Too many branches
    "PLR0913", # Too many arguments
    "PLR0915", # Too many statements
    "PLR2004", # Magic value used in comparison
    "TRY003", # Avoid specifying long messages outside exception class
    "T201",  # print found (allowed for debugging scripts)
    "E722",  # Do not use bare except (kept relaxed for legacy paths)
    "E402",  # Module level import not at top of file (kept relaxed)
    "PLC0415", # import should be at top-level (kept relaxed)
    "PTH123", # open() should be replaced by Path.open() (standard open allowed)
    "PTH103", # os.makedirs() should be replaced by Path.mkdir() (os.makedirs allowed)
    "PTH118", # os.path.join() should be replaced by Path (os.path.join allowed)
    "EM101",  # Exception must not use a string literal
    "EM102",  # Exception must not use an f-string literal
    "TRY002", # Create your own exception
    "TRY300", # Consider moving this statement to an else block
    "DTZ005", # datetime.now() called without tz argument
    "RET504", # Unnecessary assignment before return
    "PLW2901", # for loop variable overwritten by assignment target
    "F841",  # Local variable assigned but never used
    "ERA001", # Found commented-out code (kept relaxed)
]

# Exclude patterns
exclude = [
    ".bzr",
    ".direnv",
    ".eggs",
    ".git",
    ".git-rewrite",
    ".hg",
    ".mypy_cache",
    ".nox",
    ".pants.d",
    ".pyenv",
    ".pytest_cache",
    ".pytype",
    ".ruff_cache",
    ".svn",
    ".tox",
    ".venv",
    ".vscode",
    "__pypackages__",
    "_build",
    "buck-out",
    "build",
    "dist",
    "node_modules",
    ".next",
    "out",
    "venv",
    "__pycache__",
]

# Allow autofix for all enabled rules
fixable = ["ALL"]
unfixable = []

# Allow unused variables when underscore-prefixed
dummy-variable-rgx = "^(_+|(_+[a-zA-Z0-9_]*[a-zA-Z0-9]+?))$"

[tool.ruff.format]
# Use double quotes for strings
quote-style = "double"
# Indent with spaces
indent-style = "space"
# Respect magic trailing comma
skip-magic-trailing-comma = false
# Automatically detect the appropriate line ending
line-ending = "auto"

# ============================================
# Ruff import sorting (isort replacement)
# ============================================
[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["deeptutor", "deeptutor_cli", "scripts"]
force-sort-within-sections = true
split-on-trailing-comma = true

# ============================================
# Ruff per-file-ignores
# ============================================
[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Allow longer lines in test files
# F401: Allow unused imports for availability checks in tests
"**/test_*.py" = ["E501", "PLR2004", "F401"]
"**/__init__.py" = ["F401"]  # Allow unused imports in __init__.py

# ============================================
# Ruff mccabe complexity
# ============================================
[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 10

# ============================================
# Pytest configuration
# ============================================
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests", "deeptutor/learning/tests"]
pythonpath = ["."]
markers = [
    "asyncio: mark async tests that require pytest-asyncio",
    "integration: requires explicitly configured external services",
    "redis_integration: requires DEEPTUTOR_TEST_REDIS_URL",
    "real_llm_resolver: exercises LLM config resolution itself, so it keeps the real resolver",
]
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "function"
addopts = [
    "--strict-markers",
    "--strict-config",
    "--disable-warnings",
    "--tb=short",
    "--import-mode=importlib",
]

# ============================================
# MyPy type checking configuration
# ============================================
[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.11"
# Relaxed type checking for gradual adoption
pretty = false
show_error_context = false
warn_return_any = false
warn_no_return = false
show_error_codes = true
ignore_missing_imports = true
follow_imports = "silent"
# Disable strict checks that generate too many errors
check_untyped_defs = false
disallow_untyped_defs = false
disallow_incomplete_defs = false
no_implicit_optional = false

# Module-specific overrides
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "tests.*"
ignore_errors = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "deeptutor.tools.*"
ignore_errors = true  # Some tools may have dynamic imports

# ============================================
# Bandit security linting configuration
# ============================================
[tool.bandit]
exclude_dirs = ["tests", "scripts"]
# B101=assert, B311=random, B403/B404=pickle/subprocess imports
# B110=try_except_pass (intentional for non-critical error handling)
# B104=hardcoded_bind_all_interfaces (required for server binding)
# B112=try_except_continue (intentional for iteration)
# B105=hardcoded_password_string (false positive on empty string initialization)
# B301=pickle (used for internal embedding cache, not untrusted data)
# B501=request_with_no_cert_validation (opt-in via env var for dev/testing)
# B603=subprocess_without_shell_equals_true (controlled execution)
# B202=tarfile_unsafe_members (already using safe_members filter)
skips = ["B101", "B311", "B403", "B404", "B110", "B104", "B112", "B105", "B301", "B501", "B603", "B202"]

description = "AI-powered troubleshooting copilot for incident investigation"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
license = {text = "FSL-1.1-ALv2"}
authors = [
    {name = "FaultMaven Team", email = "team@faultmaven.com"}
]
keywords = ["troubleshooting", "incident-response", "ai", "investigation", "observability"]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 4 - Beta",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "Intended Audience :: System Administrators",
    "License :: Other/Proprietary License",
    "Operating System :: OS Independent",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Topic :: System :: Monitoring",
    "Topic :: System :: Systems Administration",
]

# ============================================================================
# CORE DEPENDENCIES (Standalone)
# Lightweight installation for local development and self-hosting
# Uses SQLite, local file storage, in-memory sessions
# ============================================================================
dependencies = [
    # Core FastAPI and server
    "fastapi>=0.115.8",
    # Direct import (main.py overrides Request.form's multipart limit);
    # >=1.3.1: form-limit enforcement + StaticFiles UNC SSRF GHSA fixes
    "starlette>=1.3.1",
    "uvicorn>=0.28.0",
    "python-multipart>=0.0.30",  # >=0.0.30: multipart DoS (unbounded header / quadratic parse) fixes
    "sse-starlette>=2.0.0",

    # LLM Framework (REQUIRED - core functionality)
    # NOTE: no fireworks-ai SDK — the Fireworks provider speaks REST via
    # aiohttp (infrastructure/llm/providers/fireworks_provider.py).
    "openai>=1.0.0",
    "anthropic>=0.25.0",
    "tiktoken>=0.5.0",

    # Database (SQLite in base, PostgreSQL drivers in cloud)
    "sqlalchemy>=2.0.0",
    "alembic>=1.13.0",
    "aiosqlite>=0.19.0",

    # Core utilities and validation
    # >=2.10: the floor every patched litellm release declares. The old
    # <2.10 ceiling pinned litellm to 1.83.0 and held ten proxy-server
    # advisories open (fm#904); <3 stays a deliberate major boundary.
    "pydantic>=2.10,<3",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.3.0",
    "httpx>=0.28.1",
    # [speedups]: aiodns/c-ares keeps DNS resolution off the shared thread
    # executor (aiohttp falls back to ThreadedResolver without it, contending
    # with BGE-M3 encode work); >=3.14: request-smuggling/parse GHSA fixes
    "aiohttp[speedups]>=3.14.0",
    "aiofiles>=23.2.1",
    # Floor raised past CVE-2026-63374 / CVE-2026-64847 (both fixed in 4.14.2).
    # The lockfiles are what pip-audit reads, but a consumer resolving from this
    # file directly — or any future re-resolution — would otherwise be free to
    # select 4.13.0 again and reintroduce both advisories with CI still green.
    "anyio>=4.15.1",
    "requests>=2.31.0",
    "PyJWT>=2.15.1",  # >=2.13.0: GHSA key-confusion (HS256 forgery) fix; >=2.14.0: CVE-2026-102274 / GHSA-w6j9-cwv2-h6wq (JWK-set parsing; not reachable here, pinned to keep the audit clean); >=2.15.1: floor = lock pin (#1518)
    # RS256 JWT keys; >=50.0.0: PKCS#7 EnvelopedData Bleichenbacher oracle
    # (GHSA-g6cj-pr64-35w5). Reachable only once workos 10.1.1 relaxed its
    # own cryptography~=49.0 pin — the two floors move together.
    "cryptography>=50.0.0",
    "bcrypt>=4.0.0",
    "email-validator>=2.0.0",
    "python-dotenv>=1.0.1",
    "typing-extensions>=4.12.2",
    "tenacity>=8.3.0",

    # Logging (structured logging for all editions)
    "structlog>=24.1.0",
    "python-json-logger>=2.0.7",

    # Knowledge base and embeddings (ChromaDB + sentence transformers)
    "chromadb>=1.0.0",
    # Floored at the release the lockfiles pin and the image is built with.
    # The security floor is 5.6.0: below it, loading a model from a path that
    # exists on local disk runs that directory's Python even with
    # trust_remote_code=False (CVE-2026-68770 / GHSA-jhr6-gm9c-rqjv). 6.x is a
    # major release (transformers>=5, huggingface-hub>=1.3); `model_cache`
    # uses only the constructor and `encode`, and BGE-M3 vectors are
    # byte-identical on 5.4.1 and 6.1.0.
    "sentence-transformers>=6.1.0",
    # Transitive via sentence-transformers, floored here for two GHSAs it
    # is the only lever on: torch <=2.12.1 is itself vulnerable
    # (GHSA-rrmf-rvhw-rf47), and torch 2.11's `setuptools<82` pin held the
    # graph below the patched setuptools 83.0.0 (GHSA-h35f-9h28-mq5c).
    # 2.13.0 drops the cap to `setuptools>=77.0.3`. The Dockerfile installs
    # the CPU wheel at whatever version the lockfile pins — it reads the pin
    # rather than repeating it, so there is nothing here to keep in step.
    "torch>=2.13.0",
    # Transitive via sentence-transformers, floored here for the same reason:
    # below 5.10.0, `save_pretrained` writes files at paths taken from a Hub
    # repo's `chat_template` keys, so a malicious repo escapes the save
    # directory (CVE-2026-9856 / GHSA-xrqw-3rrv-vx5w).
    "transformers>=5.10.0",
    # >=6.14.2: inline-image infinite-loop GHSA fixes; >=6.15.0:
    # CVE-2026-71852; >=6.16.1: three denial-of-service advisories — outline
    # retrieval and XForm extraction blow up on crafted files
    # (GHSA-23w6-3w8w-8484, GHSA-763m-79hh-57f2) and TreeObject.insert_child
    # can loop forever (GHSA-jp53-mhqp-8xcg). Reached from evidence upload.
    "pypdf>=6.19.0",
    "python-docx>=1.1.2",

    # Data processing and analysis
    "numpy>=1.26.4,<2",
    "pandas>=1.5.0",
    "pandas-stubs>=2.0.0",
    "pylogrus>=0.1.2",
    "scikit-learn>=1.5.0",
    "pyod>=2.0.1",
    # >=5.29.6: GHSA-7gcm-g887-7qv7 + GHSA-8qvm-5x2c-j2w7 fixes. <6 is a
    # deliberate major-version boundary (the locked consumers allow 6.x per
    # their metadata) — lift it deliberately when a 6.x need arises.
    "protobuf>=5.29.6,<6",
    # Transitive (spacy / thinc / torch import it at runtime), floored here
    # because nothing else in the graph moves it: >=83.0.0 patches
    # GHSA-h35f-9h28-mq5c. torch 2.11's `setuptools<82` used to cap it.
    "setuptools>=83.0.0",
    # Transitive (requests and kubernetes; botocore and sentry-sdk in the
    # cloud lockfile), floored here because none of them requires the
    # patched release: >=2.8.0 fixes target-server TLS settings applied to an
    # HTTPS proxy connection (CVE-2026-97687), an infinite loop on chunked
    # Deflate responses (CVE-2026-97688) and an unbounded chunk-size line
    # buffered into memory (CVE-2026-97689).
    "urllib3>=2.8.0",

    # Web utilities
    "beautifulsoup4>=4.12.3",
    "tavily-python>=0.7.0",

    # Document processing
    "python-frontmatter>=1.0.0",

    # Background task scheduling
    "apscheduler>=3.10.4",

    # In-process Redis (standalone deployment: API-compatible Redis without external server)
    "fakeredis[lua]>=2.21.0",
]

# ============================================================================
# OPTIONAL DEPENDENCIES FOR CLOUD
# Full-featured installation with observability, security, and cloud storage
# ============================================================================
[project.optional-dependencies]
cloud = [
    # Observability (Opik tracing, Prometheus metrics)
    "opik>=1.11.13",
    # Transitive via opik and never imported by FaultMaven; declared solely
    # to floor it at the release that patches the ten LiteLLM Proxy
    # advisories (critical GHSA-4xpc-pv4p-pm3w / GHSA-r75f-5x8p-qvmc among
    # them). Held back for months by the pydantic ceiling lifted above.
    "litellm>=1.84.0",
    "prometheus-client>=0.20.0",

    # Security (Presidio PII redaction)
    # Note: Production uses K8s Presidio microservice
    # These libraries are for local cloud testing
    "presidio-analyzer>=2.2.0",
    "presidio-anonymizer>=2.2.0",

    # Cloud infrastructure
    "redis[hiredis]>=5.0.0",      # Distributed session management (microservice in production)
    "psycopg2-binary>=2.9.0",     # PostgreSQL driver
    "asyncpg>=0.29.0",            # Async PostgreSQL driver
    "boto3>=1.34.0",              # AWS S3 storage
    "azure-storage-blob>=12.0.0", # Azure Blob storage

    # Identity (WorkOS AuthKit cloud SSO — ADR-015; imported only in oauth mode)
    # >=10.1.1: the first release to declare cryptography~=50.0 rather than
    # ~=49.0, which is what lets the cloud extra reach the patched
    # cryptography. AuthKit call sites used here are unchanged across the
    # 9→10 major (see modules/auth/infrastructure/sso/workos_provider.py).
    "workos>=10.1.1,<11",
]

# ============================================================================
# TESTING DEPENDENCIES
# For development and CI/CD testing
# ============================================================================
test = [
    # Core testing framework
    "pytest>=8.0.0",
    "pytest-asyncio>=0.21.0",
    "pytest-cov>=4.1.0",
    "pytest-mock>=3.12.0",
    "pytest-xdist>=3.5.0",
    "pytest-html>=3.2.0",
    "pytest-json-report>=1.5.0",

    # HTTP testing
    "httpx>=0.24.0",

    # Mocking and test utilities
    "responses>=0.23.0",
    "freezegun>=1.2.0",
    "factory-boy>=3.3.0",
    "Faker>=40.0.0",

    # Coverage and reporting
    "coverage>=7.2.0",
    "codecov>=2.1.0",

    # Performance testing
    "pytest-benchmark>=4.0.0",
    "locust>=2.20.0",
    "psutil>=5.9.0",

    # Security testing
    "bandit>=1.7.0",

    # Code quality (for CI checks)
    "black==26.3.1",  # Pinned for consistent formatting across environments
    "ruff==0.9.10",    # Pinned — CI env-check gates on this exact version in the lockfile
    # Installed, but NOT configured and NOT invoked: ruff replaced flake8 here in
    # #179, and no CI job, pre-commit hook or script runs it. There is deliberately
    # no [tool.flake8] section to go with it — flake8 cannot read pyproject.toml
    # without the Flake8-pyproject plugin, which is in no requirements file, so the
    # section this file used to carry was read by nothing and drifted accordingly
    # (it still named two files deleted with faultmaven/agent/). Do not re-add it;
    # if flake8 is ever wanted again it needs a .flake8 file and a job that runs it.
    # Dropping the dependency itself means recompiling dev/test/cloud lockfiles
    # and amending tests/installation/test_pyproject.py, which asserts this extra
    # holds it — two more decisions, each its own change.
    "flake8>=7.0.0",
]

# ============================================================================
# DEVELOPMENT DEPENDENCIES
# For local development, linting, and type checking
# ============================================================================
dev = [
    # Code quality and formatting
    "ruff==0.9.10",             # Fast Python linter and formatter (pinned to match CI)
    "black==26.3.1",           # Code formatter (pinned to match CI)
    "mypy>=1.8.0",              # Type checking

    # Pre-commit hooks
    "pre-commit>=3.6.0",
    # Transitive via pre-commit, floored here because pre-commit does not
    # require the patched release: >=21.7.13 fixes unverified seed-wheel
    # downloads (PYSEC-2026-4011), pyvenv.cfg injection through the prompt
    # (PYSEC-2026-4012), and shell commands run by activation scripts from a
    # crafted path or prompt (PYSEC-2026-4013, PYSEC-2026-4014).
    "virtualenv>=21.7.13",

    # Architecture enforcement
    "import-linter>=2.0.0",
]

# ============================================================================
# BUILD SYSTEM
# Modern setuptools-based build
# ============================================================================
[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=68.0", "wheel"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["."]
include = ["faultmaven*"]
exclude = ["tests*", "docs*", "scripts*", ".github*"]

# ============================================================================
# OPERATOR CONSOLE ENTRYPOINTS
# ============================================================================
# Operator procedures ship WITH the installed package, not as loose files under
# scripts/ — the wheel excludes scripts/ and the image never COPYs it, so a
# path-based in-pod invocation could never work (#887). These commands land on
# PATH wherever faultmaven is installed:
#
#     kubectl exec deploy/faultmaven-api -- fm-provision-sso-org --name ...
#
# Targets live in faultmaven/cli/; each `main()` is synchronous and exits with a
# meaningful status code.
[project.scripts]
fm-provision-sso-org = "faultmaven.cli.provision_sso_org:main"
fm-provision-service-account = "faultmaven.cli.provision_service_account:main"
fm-promote-platform-admin = "faultmaven.cli.promote_platform_admin:main"
fm-demote-platform-admin = "faultmaven.cli.demote_platform_admin:main"
fm-remove-org-member = "faultmaven.cli.remove_org_member:main"
fm-personal-tenant = "faultmaven.cli.personal_tenant:main"
fm-reassign-cases = "faultmaven.cli.reassign_cases:main"
fm-set-turn-cap = "faultmaven.cli.set_turn_cap:main"
fm-reset-kb = "faultmaven.cli.reset_kb:main"
fm-wipe-deployment = "faultmaven.cli.wipe_deployment:main"

# ============================================================================
# PROJECT METADATA AND URLS
# ============================================================================
[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/FaultMaven/faultmaven"
Documentation = "https://github.com/FaultMaven/faultmaven/blob/main/README.md"
Repository = "https://github.com/FaultMaven/faultmaven"
Issues = "https://github.com/FaultMaven/faultmaven/issues"
Changelog = "https://github.com/FaultMaven/faultmaven/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md"

# ============================================================================
# TOOL CONFIGURATION
# ============================================================================

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
minversion = "7.0"
testpaths = ["tests"]
python_files = ["test_*.py", "*_test.py"]
python_classes = ["Test*"]
python_functions = ["test_*"]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "function"
addopts = [
    "-ra",
    "--strict-markers",
    "--strict-config",
    "-v",
    "--tb=short",
    "-m", "not real_llm",
]
markers = [
    "unit: Unit tests (fast, isolated)",
    "integration: Integration tests (cross-layer)",
    "slow: Slow running tests (excluded from fast CI)",
    "cloud: Tests requiring Redis, PostgreSQL, etc.",
    "postgres: Tests that require a real PostgreSQL (skipped unless DATABASE_URL is postgresql)",
    "security: Security-related tests",
    "benchmark: Performance benchmarks (baseline tracking)",
    "performance: Performance overhead tests",
    "asyncio: Async tests",
    "api: API endpoint tests",
    "llm: LLM-related tests",
    "agent: Agent-related tests",
    "session: Session management tests",
    "knowledge_base: Knowledge base tests",
    "architecture: Architecture validation tests",
    "real_llm: Real-LLM integration tests (hits live provider API; opt-in via `pytest -m real_llm` and provider API key env var; excluded from default test runs)",
]
filterwarnings = [
    "ignore::DeprecationWarning:websockets.*",
    "ignore::DeprecationWarning:uvicorn.*",
    "ignore::UserWarning:pytest_asyncio.*",
    "ignore::PendingDeprecationWarning",
]

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["faultmaven"]
omit = [
    "*/tests/*",
    "*/test_*.py",
    "*/__pycache__/*",
    "*/site-packages/*",
    "*/conftest.py",
]

[tool.coverage.report]
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "def __repr__",
    "raise AssertionError",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "@abstractmethod",
    "@abc.abstractmethod",
]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 88
target-version = "py311"

[tool.ruff.lint]
# THIS LIST IS THE GATE. CI (`code-quality` in .github/workflows/ci-cd.yml) and
# the ruff pre-commit hook both run bare `ruff check faultmaven/ tests/`, with no
# `--select`, so what is written here is exactly what is enforced. Never pass
# `--select` on a command line: it REPLACES this list rather than narrowing it,
# which is how the previously declared set (E, W, F, I, B, C4, UP, G) came to be
# published for months without ever running — `faultmaven/` and `tests/` carry
# 10,275 violations of it (ruff 0.9.10, measured at cfbc9e23e).
#
# The set below is what `faultmaven/` and `tests/` actually pass today:
#   E9    syntax / IO errors — the file does not parse
#   F63   comparison mistakes (`is` on literals, invalid `==` types)
#   F7    misplaced statements (`break` outside a loop, etc.)
#   F82   undefined names — a NameError waiting for the right branch
#   F811  a name redefined before its first use: the earlier definition is dead
#         and never runs. Added here with the sweep that made it pass, which
#         turned up four real defects: ten DI getters in `_container_impl.py`
#         shadowed by later definitions of the same names, and a duplicate
#         `TitleResponse` whose required `view_state` the live route never
#         passes — the published one is the second.
#   I     import sorting (ruff replaced isort here in #179)
#
# E9,F63,F7,F82 is not a chosen set: it is GitHub's starter-workflow flake8 line
# (`flake8 . --count --select=E9,F63,F7,F82`), added in 2025 and translated
# verbatim into ruff by #179, whose recorded rationale concerns which PATHS are
# linted, not which rules. Widening it is a correction, not a re-litigation —
# but widen it one rule at a time, with the sweep that makes the tree pass in
# the same PR, so this list never again names something that is not enforced.
select = [
    "E9",    # pycodestyle: syntax/IO errors
    "F63",   # pyflakes: invalid comparisons
    "F7",    # pyflakes: misplaced statements
    "F82",   # pyflakes: undefined names
    "F811",  # pyflakes: redefinition of an unused name (dead definition)
    "I",     # isort: import sorting
]
# Inert while the set above stays narrow (none of these is selected). Kept so
# that widening `select` does not also have to rediscover these decisions.
ignore = [
    "E501",  # line too long (handled by formatter)
    "B008",  # do not perform function calls in argument defaults
    "C901",  # too complex
]

# NOTE: Error logging standard (not currently enforceable by linter):
# All logger.error() and logger.critical() calls within exception handlers
# MUST include exc_info=True or use logger.exception()
# See docs/operations/monitoring/logging-policy.md for details

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Every path named here must exist — tests/unit/test_lint_config_is_live.py
# asserts it. Two entries (faultmaven/agent/doctrine.py,
# faultmaven/data_processing/log_processor.py) named files deleted long ago and
# went unnoticed because nothing ever resolved them.
"__init__.py" = ["F401"]  # Allow unused imports in __init__.py
"test_*.py" = ["F401", "F811"]  # Redefinition is the pytest-fixture idiom
"conftest.py" = ["F401"]  # Allow unused imports in conftest files
"faultmaven/main.py" = ["F841"]  # Allow unused variables (dependency injection)


[tool.black]
line-length = 88
target-version = ["py311"]
include = '\.pyi?$'

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.11"
warn_return_any = false
warn_unused_configs = true
disallow_untyped_defs = false
ignore_missing_imports = true
show_error_codes = true
check_untyped_defs = false
warn_no_return = false
warn_unreachable = false
no_implicit_optional = false
ignore_errors = true
warn_unused_ignores = false
# No `files` key. It named faultmaven/session_management.py and
# faultmaven/agent/tools/web_search.py — neither has existed for a long time, so
# a bare `mypy` could not even start ("cannot read file ... No such file or
# directory") while the config looked configured. Nothing in CI runs mypy, and
# `ignore_errors = true` above means it reports nothing anyway (measured: `mypy
# faultmaven` spends 2m05s to print "no issues found in 472 source files"). So
# rather than point the key at a real path and publish a second no-op that reads
# as a gate, the key is removed: run `mypy <paths>` explicitly. Giving mypy
# teeth — dropping `ignore_errors`, picking a scope, wiring a CI job — is its
# own change, not this one.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
    "pandas.*",
    "sklearn.*",
    "numpy.*",
    "yaml.*",
    "mcp.*"
]
ignore_missing_imports = true

# psycopg(v3): pgvector_store.py가 지연 import하는 실제 드라이버 — extra 없이는 provider 설치 불가

    "chromadb>=0.4.0",
    "pinecone>=7.0.1",
    "qdrant-client>=1.7.0",
    "pgvector>=0.2.0",
    "psycopg[binary]>=3.1",
]

# BM25 엔진 (Phase 1: Dense 전용 DB의 하이브리드 검색 지원)

# PDF 추출 품질 게이트(#12) 전용. PyMuPDF(fitz)는 mojibake 재추출 폴백에만 쓰이며
# 미설치 시 graceful degradation 하므로 코어 의존성에 추가하지 않는다(opt-in).
extraction-quality = ["pymupdf>=1.24.0,<2"]

# Vertex AI(GCP) 선택적 provider 전용. ADC 토큰 발급용 google-auth만 명시한다.
# 임베딩/LLM/리랭커 vertex provider는 httpx + ADC로 동작하며(무거운 vertexai SDK 비의존),
# google-auth는 이미 google-generativeai 경유 전이 의존성이지만 명시성을 위해 extra로 둔다.
# 미설치 시 vertex provider 인증 시점에 설치 안내 에러가 발생한다(코어 동작 영향 0).
vertex = ["google-auth>=2.0.0,<3"]

# 원본 파일 보관(#10) GCS 백엔드 전용. original_file_storage.py가 지연 import하며
# 미설치 시 OriginalFileStorageConfigurationError로 graceful 실패(local 기본은 0-dep).
gcs = ["google-cloud-storage>=2.0"]

[tool.black]
line-length = 100
target-version = ['py311']
include = '\.pyi?$'
extend-exclude = '''
/(
  # directories
  \.eggs
  | \.git
  | \.hg
  | \.mypy_cache
  | \.tox
  | \.venv
  | build
  | dist
)/
'''

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py311"
extend-exclude = [
    "frontend/node_modules",
    "frontend/dist",
    "frontend/coverage",
    "notebooks",
]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",  # pycodestyle errors
    "W",  # pycodestyle warnings
    "F",  # pyflakes
    "I",  # isort
    "C",  # flake8-comprehensions
    "B",  # flake8-bugbear
    "UP", # pyupgrade
]
ignore = [
    "E501",  # line too long
    "B008",  # do not perform function calls in argument defaults
    "C901",  # too complex
    "B904",  # exception chaining (보안: HTTPException에 원본 에러 노출 방지)
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"__init__.py" = ["F401"]
"main.py" = ["E402"]  # .env 로드를 위해 import가 파일 상단이 아님
"scripts/**/*.py" = ["E402"]  # 스크립트는 sys.path 조작 필요
# 선택적 의존성 테스트: pytest.importorskip() 뒤에 import 필요
"tests/unit/infrastructure/storage/vector/test_mongodb_atlas_store.py" = ["E402"]
"tests/unit/infrastructure/storage/vector/test_pgvector_store.py" = ["E402"]
"tests/unit/infrastructure/storage/vector/test_qdrant_store.py" = ["E402"]
"tests/unit/retrieval/retrievers/test_pinecone_retriever.py" = ["E402"]

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.11"
warn_return_any = true
warn_unused_configs = true
ignore_missing_imports = true
follow_imports = "skip"  # 프로젝트 파일은 mypy . 대상으로 직접 검사하고, heavy third-party stub graph는 건너뜀
incremental = false  # 오래된 third-party stub 캐시가 release gate를 장기 실행시키지 않도록 함
exclude = [
    "\\.venv/",
    "scripts/",
    "frontend/node_modules",
    "frontend/dist",
    "frontend/coverage",
    "notebooks/",
]
# 엄격 모드 설정 (2025-11-29 활성화)
check_untyped_defs = true
disallow_untyped_defs = true  # 모든 함수에 타입 힌트 필수
disallow_incomplete_defs = true  # 부분적 타입 힌트 금지
no_implicit_optional = true
warn_redundant_casts = true
warn_unused_ignores = true
warn_no_return = true
show_error_codes = true
strict_optional = true

# 모듈별 점진적 적용 (각 모듈별로 개별 설정)
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
    "app.lib.types",
    "app.lib.llm_client",
    "app.api.services.chat_service",
    "app.api.services.rag_pipeline",
    "app.modules.core.retrieval.orchestrator",
]
check_untyped_defs = true

# 엄격 모드 제외 모듈: 외부 인터페이스 및 설정 관련 (2025-12-01)
# 이 모듈들은 외부 라이브러리 의존성이 높아 타입 추론이 어려움
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
    # 테스트 파일 - pytest fixture 및 mock 의존 (타입 추론 복잡)
    "tests.*",
    # 배치 처리 모듈 - 크롤러 관련 (외부 라이브러리 의존)
    "app.batch.*",
    # API 라우터 - FastAPI 엔드포인트 (FastAPI 타입 추론 복잡)
    "app.api.*",
    # 미들웨어 (FastAPI/Starlette 의존)
    "app.middleware.*",
    # 데이터베이스 레이어 (SQLAlchemy/Motor 의존)
    "app.database.*",
    # 설정 스키마 - Pydantic 기반 (이미 타입 안전)
    "app.config.*",
    # 모델 정의 - Pydantic 기반 (이미 타입 안전)
    "app.models.*",
    # DI 컨테이너 (dependency-injector 라이브러리 의존)
    "app.core.*",
    # 세션 관리 (MongoDB/Redis 의존)
    "app.modules.core.session.*",
    # enrichment (외부 LLM 의존)
    "app.modules.core.enrichment.*",
    # tools (외부 API 호출)
    "app.modules.core.tools.*",
]
disallow_untyped_defs = false
disallow_incomplete_defs = false
check_untyped_defs = false
warn_return_any = false
ignore_errors = true

# 엄격 모드 적용 모듈: 핵심 데이터 처리 로직 (2025-12-01 확장)
# 타입 에러 발생 가능성이 높고, 데이터 무결성이 중요한 모듈
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
    # 기존 Phase 1 모듈
    "app.modules.core.privacy.*",
    "app.modules.core.self_rag.*",
    # 유틸리티 라이브러리 - 공통 타입 정의
    "app.lib.*",
    # 검색 파이프라인 - RAG 핵심 데이터 흐름
    "app.modules.core.retrieval.orchestrator",
    "app.modules.core.retrieval.interfaces",
    "app.modules.core.retrieval.query_expansion.*",
    "app.modules.core.retrieval.retrievers.*",
    "app.modules.core.retrieval.rerankers.*",
    "app.modules.core.retrieval.bm25.*",
    "app.modules.core.retrieval.cache.*",
    # 답변 생성 - LLM 응답 처리
    "app.modules.core.generation.*",
    # 문서 처리 - 파싱/청킹 데이터 변환
    "app.modules.core.documents.*",
    # 임베딩 - 벡터 데이터 처리
    "app.modules.core.embedding.*",
    # 라우팅 - 쿼리 분류 로직
    "app.modules.core.routing.*",
]
disallow_untyped_defs = true
disallow_incomplete_defs = true
warn_return_any = true
# 로컬 mypy와 pre-commit mypy 버전 차이로 인한 unused-ignore 에러 방지
warn_unused_ignores = false

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
python_files = ["test_*.py", "*_test.py"]
python_classes = ["Test*"]
python_functions = ["test_*"]
addopts = "-ra -q --strict-markers --tb=short -p no:cacheprovider -p no:respx -p no:anyio -p no:pytest_cov"
markers = [
    "slow: marks tests as slow (deselect with '-m \"not slow\"')",
    "integration: marks tests as integration tests",
    "basic: marks tests as basic functionality tests",
    "unit: marks tests as unit tests",
    "system: marks tests that require system Python environment",
    "e2e: marks tests as end-to-end tests with real APIs (costs money, slower)",
    "eval: marks tests as evaluation tests for CI/CD quality gates",
    "performance: marks in-process concurrency/performance acceptance tests (mock-based, no external cost)",
]

# Test discovery patterns
filterwarnings = [
    "ignore::DeprecationWarning",
    "ignore::PendingDeprecationWarning",
    "ignore::UserWarning:pytest_asyncio.*",
    # Python 3.11 AsyncMock 내부 버그: side_effect=Exception(...)으로도
    # _execute_mock_call 코루틴이 GC 시 미소비 경고 발생 (CPython #100090)
    "ignore:coroutine 'AsyncMockMixin._execute_mock_call' was never awaited:RuntimeWarning",
]

# Asyncio configuration
asyncio_mode = "auto"

# Coverage settings for pytest-cov
[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["app"]
omit = [
    "*/tests/*", 
    "*/test_*.py",
    "*/.venv/*",
    "*/.venv_system/*",
    "*/venv/*"
]

[tool.coverage.report]
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "def __repr__",
    "raise AssertionError",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
    "pass",
    "\\.\\.\\.",
]
show_missing = true
precision = 2
