[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=61.0", "wheel"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "schematika"
version = "0.1.7"
description = "A Python library for creating electrical schematic diagrams programmatically"
requires-python = ">=3.14"
license = "MIT"
license-files = ["LICENSE"]
authors = [
    { name = "Ole Johan Bondahl" }
]
keywords = ["electrical", "schematic", "diagram", "svg", "iec"]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 3 - Alpha",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering :: Electronic Design Automation (EDA)",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14",
]

# core/ uses deal contracts (@deal.pure etc.) at import time, so it is a runtime dependency.
dependencies = [
    "deal>=4.24.6",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
pdf = ["typst"]
cable = ["wireviz"]
pcb = ["skidl>=2.2.3,<3", "pillow==12.3.0"]
excel = ["openpyxl"]
mcp = ["mcp>=1.0"]
dev = ["cairosvg", "playwright"]

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/OleJBondahl/Schematika"
Repository = "https://github.com/OleJBondahl/Schematika"
Issues = "https://github.com/OleJBondahl/Schematika/issues"

[project.scripts]
schematika-pcb-review = "schematika.pcb.visual_review:main"

[tool.setuptools]
package-dir = {"" = "src"}

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["src"]
include = ["schematika*"]

[tool.setuptools.package-data]
schematika = ["rendering/typst/templates/*.typ", "overview/assets/*"]


[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
python_files = ["test_*.py"]
python_classes = ["Test*"]
python_functions = ["test_*"]
# --inline-snapshot=disable: CI fails on stale snapshots; dev runs `pytest --inline-snapshot=update` to rewrite.
addopts = "--verbose --cov=src --cov-report=term-missing --inline-snapshot=disable"
# Refactor safety net: kill any test that hangs >30s. Override per-test with @pytest.mark.timeout(N).
timeout = 30

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "dirty-equals>=0.9",
    "hypothesis>=6.104",
    "import-linter>=2.11",
    "inline-snapshot>=0.20",
    # mutmut 3.x blocks on native Windows (see issue #397). Pin to 2.x for
    # cross-platform mutation testing (baseline kill-rate runs on Windows).
    "mutmut>=3.5.0",
    "pdoc>=16.0.0",
    "pre-commit>=4.6.0",
    "pymupdf>=1.27.2.2",
    "pytest>=9.0.3",
    "pytest-cov>=5.0.0",
    "pytest-examples>=0.0.18",
    "pytest-subtests>=0.13",
    "pytest-timeout>=2.3",
    "ruff>=0.15.12",
    "ty>=0.0.32",
    "vulture>=2.16",
]

[tool.ruff]
# Same as Black.
line-length = 88
# Assume Python 3.13.
# target-version is intentionally pinned to py313 (not py314) due to a ruff
# 0.15.12 format bug under target-version="py314" that strips the parens
# from `except (X, Y):` tuples, producing Python-2 invalid syntax.  See
# docs/ratchet/SUPPRESSIONS.md (Wave P1) for context.  requires-python =
# ">=3.14" remains correct; only the target-version is held back.
target-version = "py313"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",    # pycodestyle errors
    "W",    # pycodestyle warnings
    "F",    # pyflakes
    "I",    # isort
    "C",    # flake8-comprehensions
    "B",    # flake8-bugbear
    "UP",   # pyupgrade
    "SIM",  # flake8-simplify
    "FA",   # flake8-future-annotations
    "N",    # pep8-naming
    "D",    # pydocstyle
    "ARG",  # flake8-unused-arguments
    "PLR",  # pylint refactor
    "PT",   # flake8-pytest-style
    "RET",  # flake8-return
    "C90",  # mccabe complexity (replaces complexipy)
    "RUF",  # Ruff-specific rules
    "PERF", # perflint
    "PIE",  # flake8-pie
    "ICN",  # flake8-import-conventions
    "ISC",  # flake8-implicit-str-concat
    "T20",  # flake8-print
    "LOG",  # flake8-logging
    "G",    # flake8-logging-format
    "Q",    # flake8-quotes
    "BLE",  # flake8-blind-except
    "RSE",  # flake8-raise
    "TRY",  # tryceratops
    "S",    # flake8-bandit (security)
    "DTZ",  # flake8-datetimez
    "PTH",  # flake8-use-pathlib (os.path → pathlib)
    "ERA",  # flake8-eradicate (commented-out code)
    "FBT",  # flake8-boolean-trap
    "EM",   # flake8-errmsg (exception message style)
    "TC",   # flake8-type-checking
    "TID",  # flake8-tidy-imports
    "ANN",  # flake8-annotations
]
ignore = ["TRY003"]

[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "google"

# L3 freeze (2026-04-25): these thresholds are frozen at the post-R7 high-water mark.
# Raising them in the future requires explicit justification recorded in
# docs/ratchet/SUPPRESSIONS.md, the same way per-line noqa entries are tracked.
# Current near-the-line offenders are listed in SUPPRESSIONS.md.
[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
# Wave R7c raised default 10 → 22 to accommodate dispatch tables and the
# build-pipeline phase functions. C0a-e + C1a-d drove every offender in
# core/ and electrical/builder_phases.py back below the default threshold;
# C1e drops the threshold to 18 — the new peak in src/, held by
# CircuitBuilder.build (electrical/builder.py:921). The remaining 7 C901
# violators between 12 and 18 (svg_path match dispatch + the four add_*
# /build methods on CircuitBuilder) are tier-C2 territory.
max-complexity = 18

# L3 freeze (2026-04-25): these thresholds are frozen at the post-R7 high-water mark.
# Raising them in the future requires explicit justification recorded in
# docs/ratchet/SUPPRESSIONS.md, the same way per-line noqa entries are tracked.
# Current near-the-line offenders are listed in SUPPRESSIONS.md.
[tool.ruff.lint.pylint]
# Schematika builders/factories legitimately take many kwargs (positional-only
# identity + many keyword-only flags).  Raised from ruff default 5 → 8 in Wave
# R3. C2d-1/2/3 bundled all ≥8-arg functions into option dataclasses; C2d-4
# returns the threshold to ruff's default of 8.
max-args = 8
# Wave R7c: PLR0911/PLR0912/PLR0915 threshold relaxations.
# max-returns raised from 6 → 10: translate() and _render_page() are
# singledispatch/match-style dispatch functions where each branch must return
# independently; merging returns would worsen readability.
# Wave C0a: lowered from 10 to 6 (translate + _render_page now use match/case
# with single final return; behavior-compatible refactoring achieved the goal).
max-returns = 6
# Wave R7c raised default 12 → 22; C0b extracted the SVG path parsers and
# C1a-d extracted the four build-pipeline phase functions. C1e drops the
# threshold to 13 — the new peak in src/, held by parse() in core/svg_path.py
# (inherent 10-arm match dispatch on PathCommand) and add_symbol/add_spdt in
# electrical/builder.py (tier C2).
max-branches = 13
# Wave R7c raised default 50 → 70; C0c rewrote _rotate_path_d (was 70+ stmts)
# to a one-liner and C1a-d collapsed the four build-pipeline phases into
# 3-5 line orchestrators. C1e drops the threshold to 51 — the new peak in
# src/, held by CircuitBuilder.build (electrical/builder.py:921; tier C2).
max-statements = 51

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"__init__.py" = ["F401", "F403", "I001"]  # isort disabled for all __init__.py: deliberate import orders avoid circular imports (electrical: system.system first; catalog: errors -> device -> registry -> cables); F403 OK because shims declare __all__ (Wave L3a / L1)
# Inline Typst code in string literals has long lines
"src/schematika/rendering/typst/compiler.py" = ["E501"]
"tests/**/*.py" = ["E501"]
# tests/** ignores:
#   D    — no pydocstyle on test fixtures/asserts
#   ARG  — fixture/subclass params aren't always used
#   PLR2004 — "magic value" comparisons are the whole point of assertions
#   PLR0913 — parametrised fixtures legitimately take many args
#   S101 — asserts are pytest's assertion mechanism, not a security risk
#   S108 — /tmp paths in tests are deliberate test fixtures, not real temp-file creation
#   S314 — ET.fromstring() parses our own renderer output, not untrusted data
#   ANN  — annotation completeness is a library-API concern; pytest fixtures and
#          assertions don't benefit from `-> None` / `*args: object` noise (Wave T4a)
"tests/**" = ["D", "ARG", "PLR2004", "PLR0913", "S101", "S108", "S314", "ANN"]
# examples/** are demonstration scripts; same rationale as tests/** for ANN (Wave T4a).
"examples/**" = ["ANN"]
# test_transform.py exercises SVG path commands (M, L, H, V, C, S, Q, T, Z)
# whose uppercase letters are part of the grammar — test names mirror them.
"tests/unit/test_transform.py" = ["N802"]
# Wave R5 — IEC/PLC naming in tests
"tests/unit/test_pcb_adapter.py" = ["N806"]      # F1/T1/_F1 are IEC fuse/terminal designators
"tests/unit/test_plc_resolver.py" = ["N806", "N817"]  # PLC identifiers and import aliases
"tests/unit/test_terminal_type.py" = ["N817"]    # T alias for Terminal in IEC context
"src/schematika/**/__init__.py" = ["D104"]
# mcp/server.py is a sandboxed code executor; it intentionally catches all
# user-raised exceptions (Exception) to return structured error strings.
# S102: exec() is the explicit mechanism for executing user-submitted Python code
# in the MCP sandbox — there is no alternative, and this is intentional.
"src/schematika/mcp/server.py" = ["BLE001", "S102"]
# test_builder.py mock_symbol helper uses an intermediate variable for clarity;
# fixing RET504 would require test body changes (blocked per wave R6 spec).
"tests/unit/test_builder.py" = ["RET504"]

[tool.ty.src]
exclude = [
    "tools/",
    "scripts/vulture_whitelist.py",
    "scripts/pid_review.py",
]

[tool.mutmut]
# Mutation testing config — target the two files slated for refactor.
# Kill-rate floor: see docs/baselines/<date>/mutmut_results.txt.
# Runner uses .venv python directly (skip `uv run` cold-start overhead per mutant)
# and narrows to tests exercising the two target files.
paths_to_mutate = ["src/schematika/"]
runner = "python -m pytest -x -q --no-cov"
tests_dir = ["tests/"]

[tool.coverage.run]
# schematika.mcp.__main__ has no `if __name__ == "__main__":` guard — importing
# it calls mcp.run() and blocks on stdio. Omit from coverage; the server module
# itself is smoke-tested in tests/unit/test_mcp_smoke.py.
omit = ["src/schematika/mcp/__main__.py"]

name = "datarax"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.12,<3.14"
version = "0.1.17"

[project.optional-dependencies]
# Platform-specific installation:
# - Linux with GPU: pip install datarax[all]
# - macOS (Apple Silicon): pip install datarax[all-macos]
# - macOS/Linux CPU-only: pip install datarax[all-cpu]
all = ["datarax[cuda12,data,dev,docs,test,wandb]"]
all-cpu = ["datarax[data,dev,docs,test,wandb]"]
all-macos = ["datarax[data,dev,docs,metal,test,wandb]"]
automation = [
  # Local cloud orchestration dependencies (benchmarks/automation/vast_orchestrator.py)
  "skypilot[vast]>=0.11,<0.12",
  "click<8.3", # SkyPilot 0.11.x launch incompatibility with click>=8.3
  # vastai-sdk 1.0+ removed VastAI.api_key_access which sky/adaptors/vast.py
  # uses for credential validation; pin to the 0.2.x line until SkyPilot
  # 0.12 upgrades its adapter. Bounce the SkyPilot API daemon
  # (`sky api stop`) after upgrading these so the new adapter is loaded.
  # The 0.2.x line pins aiohttp==3.10.1 (35 open advisories); every 1.x release
  # of the underlying `vastai` package pins cryptography==49.0.0 instead, which the
  # cryptography>=50 constraint below refuses, so neither line is clean.
  "vastai-sdk>=0.2.6,<0.3",
  # Required by benchmarks.export when the orchestrator's --analyze step
  # imports benchmarks.cli locally (the remote VM gets matplotlib via the
  # benchmark extra; the local box only installs `automation`).
  "matplotlib>=3.8"
]
# benchmark extra is separate — it pulls in 12 Linux-only frameworks (DALI, PyTorch, Ray, etc.)
# Install explicitly: pip install datarax[benchmark]
benchmark = [
  # Peer frameworks for comparative benchmarking (Section 14.2 of benchmark report)
  # Tier 1: JAX ecosystem (Grain already in base deps)
  "jax-dataloader>=0.1", # jax-dataloader — minimal JAX-native loader
  "tensorflow-datasets>=4.9.10", # tf.data adapter; CIFAR-10 is read through TFDSEagerSource
  "protobuf>=6.31.1", # tensorflow-metadata 1.21 is generated for 6.31.1; protobuf 5 fails its import
  # Tier 2: High-performance leaders
  "nvidia-dali-cuda120>=1.0; sys_platform == 'linux'", # NVIDIA DALI — GPU-native data loading + augmentation (Linux/CUDA only)
  "spdl>=0.1", # Meta SPDL — thread-based data loading
  "torch>=2.0,<2.11", # PyTorch DataLoader baseline (<2.11 for CUDA 12 wheels; 2.11+ pulls libcudart.so.13)
  "torchvision>=0.15,<0.26", # torchvision transforms + batch JPEG decode (paired with torch <2.11)
  "torchaudio>=2.0,<2.11", # paired with torch (avoid the 2.11 CUDA-13 transitive dep)
  # Tier 2: Cloud/streaming
  "mosaicml-streaming>=0.7", # MosaicML StreamingDataset — MDS format
  "webdataset>=0.2", # WebDataset — TAR-based streaming
  # Tier 3: Specialized
  "litdata>=0.2", # Lightning LitData — cloud streaming
  "ray[data]>=2.9", # Ray Data — distributed actor-based
  "datasets>=2.21", # Hugging Face Datasets (>=2.21 for pyarrow 15+ compat)
  "pyarrow>=21", # >=21 for pa.json_ (datasets 4+) and macOS-14 arm64 wheel stability
  "deeplake>=4.0", # Deep Lake — AI database
  # Benchmark infrastructure
  "matplotlib>=3.8", # Plotting for benchmark reports
  "tabulate>=0.9", # Table formatting for reports
  "rich>=13.0", # Rich terminal output for benchmark runners
  # benchmarks/cli.py imports click at module level, and the nightly workflow runs it as
  # `from benchmarks.cli import main`. click was declared only under `automation`, which
  # was harmless while the nightly installed every extra and load-bearing the moment
  # automation became a conflicting extra. It stays in `automation` as well, pinned <8.3
  # there for SkyPilot, because the orchestrator invokes benchmarks.cli locally; the two
  # declarations never resolve together because the extras conflict by construction.
  "click>=8.1" # benchmarks/cli.py
]
# Note: FFCV requires system OpenCV (libopencv-dev) — install separately via:
# sudo apt-get install libopencv-dev && pip install ffcv>=1.0
# Note: Energon (megatron-energon) requires Megatron-LM — install separately
cuda-dev = [
  # Complete CUDA development environment
  # Includes all dev tools, testing, and GPU support
  # Automatically configured via setup.sh and scripts/setup_env.py
  "datarax[cuda12,dev]"
]
cuda12 = [
  # Named for the CUDA major version, as JAX names its own extras (cuda12, cuda12-local,
  # cuda13); JAX publishes no `gpu` extra, and this package also ships `metal`, which is a
  # GPU too. No jaxlib line: every jax cuda extra already requires jaxlib<=X,>=X at its own
  # version, so restating it here only creates a second place for the two to disagree.
  "jax[cuda12]>=0.11.1; sys_platform == 'linux'"
]
data = [

[tool.bandit]
# Note: bandit excludes tests/scripts/examples because security scanning focuses on
# production code. .pre-commit-config.yaml does NOT exclude these — pre-commit hooks
# (ruff, pyright, formatting) intentionally run on all code including tests.

# B101: assert_used - Assert statements are the idiomatic way to write pytest tests
# They are safe in test files as pytest rewrites them for better error messages
# B110: try_except_pass - Used intentionally for optional statistics collection
skips = ["B101", "B110"]

[tool.coverage.html]
directory = "htmlcov"
skip_covered = false
skip_empty = false

[tool.coverage.paths]
source = [
  "src",
  "*/datarax/src"
]

[tool.coverage.report]
exclude_lines = [
  "pragma: no cover",
  "def __repr__",
  "if self.debug:",
  "if settings.DEBUG",
  "raise AssertionError",
  "raise NotImplementedError",
  "if 0:",
  "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
  "class .*\\bProtocol\\):",
  "@(abc\\.)?abstractmethod",
  "raise ImportError"
]
# Adjusted for large codebase with focused testing approach
fail_under = 80
precision = 2
show_missing = true
skip_covered = false

[tool.coverage.run]
branch = true
omit = ["*/tests/*", "*/conftest.py", "*/__pycache__/*", "*/scripts/*", "*/examples/*", "*/benchmark/*", "*/example_data/*"]
parallel = true
relative_files = true
source = ["src"]

environment_file = ".datarax.env"

[tool.mypy]
# This project uses pyright as its type checker (see [tool.pyright] below).
# mypy is NOT configured and will produce false positives due to JAX/Flax/NNX
# type stubs. Do not use mypy --strict for audit purposes.
follow_imports = "skip"

[tool.pydoclint]
allow-init-docstring = true
arg-type-hints-in-docstring = false
# Instance attributes are documented under Attributes per the Google style; pydoclint would
# compare them with class-level attributes only.
check-class-attributes = false
# Annotations are the source of truth for types; docstrings carry the prose.
check-return-types = false
check-yield-types = false
# `# noqa: DOC...` is read from the def line, where propagated exceptions are annotated.
native-mode-noqa-location = "definition"
skip-checking-short-docstrings = true
style = "google"

[tool.pylint."messages_control"]
# NNX modules require nnx.Variable as direct attrs; config dataclasses map 1:1
# to parameters. Default max-attrs=7 is too restrictive for this domain.
max-args = 10
max-attributes = 12

[tool.pyright]
exclude = ["example_data", ".deprecated", "**/__pycache__", "**/.venv"]
include = ["src", "tests", "examples", "scripts", "benchmarks"]
pythonVersion = "3.12"
# JAX/Flax/NNX ecosystem requires these specific suppressions due to
# dynamic attribute access patterns and type stub limitations.
reportFunctionMemberAccess = false
reportIncompatibleVariableOverride = false
# Benchmarks depend on many optional adapters/frameworks that are intentionally
# not required in every dev environment or pre-commit hook env.
reportMissingImports = false
# tensorflow lives in the tfds extra, which setup.sh does not install; pyright checks its uses
# against the stubs it bundles either way, so a stub without a source is information.
reportMissingModuleSource = "information"
reportMissingTypeStubs = false
# The checkpoint package was rewritten in 0.1.6 and holds the full standard.
strict = ["src/datarax/checkpoint"]
typeCheckingMode = "standard"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
addopts = "--strict-markers --strict-config --verbose --tb=short --color=yes --durations=10 --cov=src/ --cov-report=term-missing --cov-report=html --cov-fail-under=80 --timeout=300 --json-report --json-report-file=temp/test-results.json --json-report-indent=2"
cache_dir = ".pytest_cache"
# Additional settings
console_output_style = "progress"
filterwarnings = [
  "ignore::DeprecationWarning:pkg_resources.*",
  "ignore::DeprecationWarning:jax.*",
  "ignore:jax.interpreters.xla.pytype_aval_mappings is deprecated:DeprecationWarning",
  "ignore::pytest.PytestCollectionWarning:cannot collect test class 'TestFileAnalysis'",
  "ignore::pytest.PytestCollectionWarning:cannot collect test class 'TestStructureAnalyzer'",
  # CUDA-related warnings (automatically handled by conftest.py)
  "ignore::UserWarning:jax._src.xla_bridge",
  "ignore:.*cuSPARSE.*",
  "ignore:.*CUDA-enabled jaxlib.*",
  # TODO: Fix Orbax checkpoint warnings - need to provide proper sharding info when restoring
  "ignore:Sharding info not provided when restoring.*:UserWarning:orbax.*",
  "ignore:Sharding info not provided when restoring.*:UserWarning",
  # Resource warnings from checkpoint operations (cleanup issues, not functional failures)
  "ignore:unclosed <socket.socket.*:ResourceWarning",
  "ignore:unclosed event loop.*:ResourceWarning",
  # Ignore all ResourceWarnings during testing (they don't affect functionality)
  "ignore::ResourceWarning"
]
log_cli = true
log_cli_level = "INFO"
markers = [
  "tfds: marks tests that read the TFDS fixture or prepared datasets (CI long-running job)",
  "hf: marks tests that require huggingface datasets to be installed",
  "slow: marks tests as slow (deselect with '-m \"not slow\"')",
  "integration: marks tests as integration tests",
  "unit: marks tests as unit tests",
  "benchmark: marks tests as performance benchmarks (requires pytest-benchmark)",
  "e2e: marks tests as end-to-end tests",
  "performance: marks tests as performance tests",
  "contract: marks tests as contract tests"
]
# Minimum version
minversion = "6.0"
python_classes = "Test*"
python_files = "test_*.py"
python_functions = "test_*"
# Main pytest configuration
testpaths = ["tests"]

[tool.pytest-benchmark]
compare = ["last", "base"]
disable_gc = true
histogram = "histogram.svg"
min_rounds = 5
min_time = 0.1
save = "benchmark-results"
save_data = true
warmup = true
warmup_iterations = 3

[tool.pytest_env]
# D: prefix = set as default only (don't override existing env vars)
JAX_ENABLE_X64 = {skip_if_set = true, value = "0"}
JAX_SKIP_CUDA_CONSTRAINTS_CHECK = {skip_if_set = true, value = "1"}
# Ray 2.53's uv runtime_env hook detects uv-managed venvs and tries to
# recreate them for workers — but the new venv lacks ray itself, causing
# workers to crash silently and from_numpy()/iter_batches() to hang.
RAY_DATA_DISABLE_PROGRESS_BARS = "1"
RAY_ENABLE_UV_RUN_RUNTIME_ENV = "0"
TF_CPP_MIN_LOG_LEVEL = {skip_if_set = true, value = "1"}
XLA_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION = {skip_if_set = true, value = "0.75"}
XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_PREALLOCATE = {skip_if_set = true, value = "false"}

[tool.ruff]
extend-include = ["*.ipynb"]
line-length = 100
# Only src/ is searched for first-party packages. The default also searches the repository
# root, where a generated directory (wandb/, site/, temp/) would be read as a package and its
# import sorted into the first-party block on the machine that has it and the third-party block
# everywhere else. The root-level packages are named in known-first-party instead.
src = ["src"]
target-version = "py312"

[tool.ruff.format]
indent-style = "space"
line-ending = "auto"
quote-style = "double"
skip-magic-trailing-comma = false

[tool.ruff.lint]
# pydoclint's DOC codes appear in `# noqa` comments on def lines.
external = ["DOC"]
# Add W291, W292, W293 to fixable to handle whitespace issues
fixable = ["I001", "F401", "E", "W", "W291", "W292", "W293", "F841"]
ignore = [
  "E402", # Module level import not at top of file
  "E721", # Do not compare types directly
  "E741", # Ambiguous variable name
  "F722", # Forward annotation syntax error
  "W391", # Blank line at end of file
  "E203", # Whitespace before ':'
  # UP035 — fixed: imports now use collections.abc
  "RUF005", # Consider using unpacked tuple instead of concatenation
  # --- Documented exemptions from the adopted rule set ---
  "ANN401", # `Any` is legitimate for JAX pytree leaves and dynamic data payloads
  "TRY003", # inline exception messages are the established, readable style here
  "TRY300", # return-in-`else` restructuring adds no safety to guard-heavy flow
  "TRY004", # state/checkpoint validation intentionally raises ValueError for structural incompatibility
  "PLR2004", # magic-value comparisons pervade numeric/array/scientific code
  "SIM102", # collapsing nested `if`s reduces readability in guard-heavy validation
  "SIM108" # ternary-over-if is not always clearer in these branches
]
# Adopt the shared SWE guide's rule set. C90 (mccabe, max-complexity=10) is active:
# every library function is at or below rank B. ANN401/TRY003/etc. exemptions above.
select = ["E", "F", "I", "UP", "W", "ANN", "ARG", "B", "C90", "D", "PLR", "PTH", "RET", "SIM", "T20", "TRY"]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
combine-as-imports = true
extra-standard-library = []
known-first-party = ["benchmarks", "datarax", "tests"]
lines-after-imports = 2
order-by-type = false

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
# Rule 2 (SRP/KISS): cyclomatic complexity ceiling. Functions above this must be
# decomposed; matches the radon rank-B boundary and the xenon --max-absolute B gate.
max-complexity = 10

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"benchmarks/**" = ["ANN", "C90", "D", "T20", "PLR", "B", "SIM", "TRY", "ARG", "RET", "PTH", "E501"]
"examples/**" = ["ANN", "C90", "D", "T20", "PLR", "B", "SIM", "TRY", "ARG", "RET", "PTH", "E501"]
"scripts/**" = ["ANN", "C90", "D", "T20", "PLR", "B", "SIM", "TRY", "ARG", "RET", "PTH", "E501"]
# buffer_sampler's nested jax.lax.cond branch closures have structurally-enforced,
# pyright-inferred return types; per-closure annotations add noise, not safety.
"src/datarax/samplers/buffer_sampler.py" = ["ANN202", "ANN001"]
# Tests, examples, benchmarks, and scripts keep baseline correctness rules
# (E/F/I/W/UP) but are exempt from production-only strictness — examples and
# benchmarks legitimately use print(), and none ship as library API.
"tests/**" = ["ANN", "C90", "D", "PLR", "B", "SIM", "TRY", "ARG", "RET", "PTH"]

[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "google"

[tool.ruff.lint.pylint]
# Datarax exposes configuration-heavy scientific entrypoints. Keep the threshold
# explicit and bounded so PLR0913 remains active for accidental API sprawl.
max-args = 13

[tool.substrax.compute]
backend = "modal"

[tool.substrax.compute.backends.modal]
outputs_volume = "datarax-compute-outputs"

# R53: an NCCL all-reduce on two GPUs after a TFDS read, eager or streamed, with no TensorFlow
# in the process (tests/sources/test_tfds_collective.py). The control runs the same program with TensorFlow
# imported first, which breaks JAX's NCCL collectives.
[tool.substrax.compute.jobs.tfds-nccl]
env = {DATARAX_TEST_JAX_PLATFORMS = "cuda,cpu", DATARAX_TFDS_FIXTURE_DIR = "/tmp/tfds_fixture", NCCL_DEBUG = "WARN"}
extras = ["cuda12", "data", "dev", "test", "tfds"]
resources = {accelerator = {count = 2, kind = "L40S"}, cpu = 8, memory_mib = 32768}
runtime = {platforms = ["cuda"], preallocate = false, xla_flags = ["--xla_gpu_deterministic_ops=true"]}
task_timeout_seconds = 900
timeout_seconds = 2700

# Tasks run in table order and the table is kept sorted, so their names carry the order.
[tool.substrax.compute.jobs.tfds-nccl.commands]
1-fixture = ["python", "-m", "tests.test_common.tfds_fixture", "/tmp/tfds_fixture"]
2-program = ["python", "-m", "tests.test_common.tfds_collective", "/tmp/tfds_fixture"]
3-stream-program = ["python", "-m", "tests.test_common.tfds_collective", "/tmp/tfds_fixture", "--stream"]
4-collective = ["python", "-m", "pytest", "tests/sources/test_tfds_collective.py", "-p", "no:cacheprovider", "--no-cov", "-rs", "-v"]
5-control = ["python", "-m", "tests.test_common.tfds_collective", "/tmp/tfds_fixture", "--import-tensorflow"]
6-stream-control = ["python", "-m", "tests.test_common.tfds_collective", "/tmp/tfds_fixture", "--stream", "--import-tensorflow"]

[tool.uv]
# The automation extra is benchmark tooling: skypilot[vast] and vastai-sdk, used only
# by benchmarks/automation/ and imported nowhere under src/. vastai-sdk pins
# aiohttp==3.10.1 exactly and the extra pins click<8.3. uv resolves ONE universal
# lockfile across every extra, so those two pins governed the aiohttp and click that
# ordinary installs and CI received, putting 37 advisories into an audit of
# .[dev,test,data], which does not include automation at all.
# Declaring the conflict lets uv fork the resolution: automation keeps aiohttp 3.10.1
# and click 8.1.8, everything else gets 3.14.3 and 8.5.0.
conflicts = [
  [{extra = "automation"}, {extra = "benchmark"}],
  [{extra = "automation"}, {extra = "cuda-dev"}],
  [{extra = "automation"}, {extra = "tfds"}],
  [{extra = "automation"}, {extra = "data"}],
  [{extra = "automation"}, {extra = "dev"}],
  [{extra = "automation"}, {extra = "docs"}],
  [{extra = "automation"}, {extra = "examples"}],
  [{extra = "automation"}, {extra = "cuda12"}],
  [{extra = "automation"}, {extra = "metal"}],
  [{extra = "automation"}, {extra = "test"}]
]
# Floors for transitively-reached packages carrying advisories, raised here because no
# direct dependency declares them. Same mechanism the sibling repositories use.
constraint-dependencies = [
  "cryptography>=50" # PYSEC-2026-3552, PKCS#7 EnvelopedData decryption oracle
]
python-preference = "only-managed"

# Configure for GPU package installation
[tool.uv.pip]
find-links = ["https://storage.googleapis.com/jax-releases/jax_cuda_releases.html"]

version = "0.1"
description = "Open-source SRE agent for automated incident investigation and root cause analysis. Automatically analyzes alerts from Slack, Grafana, Datadog, and other tooling."
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
license = { text = "Apache-2.0" }
authors = [
  { name = "OpenSRE", email = "support@opensre.com" },
]
keywords = ["sre", "devops", "incident", "rca", "llm", "ai", "agent", "observability"]
dependencies = [
    # Core AI/Agent
    "anthropic>=0.77.1",
    "mcp>=1.28.1",
    "openai>=2.0.0",
    "litellm>=1.90.0,<1.104.0",
    # Data validation
    "pydantic>=2.12.5,<3",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.12.0,<3",
    "kubernetes>=28.1.0,<37.0.0",
    # HTTP and async
    "httpx[socks]>=0.27.0",
    "aiohttp>=3.9.0",
    "fastapi>=0.135.3",
    "uvicorn[standard]>=0.30.0",

    # PKCS#7 Bleichenbacher oracle). cryptography >=49 ships no x86-64 macOS wheel,
    # so the frozen darwin-x64 release binary builds it from source against
    # OpenSSL >= 3.2 (SSL_get0_group_name). release.yml pins Homebrew openssl@3
    # and re-copies those dylibs into the PyInstaller onedir bundle.
    "cryptography>=50.0.0,<51",
    # AWS
    "boto3>=1.42.88",
    # Slack (Socket Mode gateway + Web API)
    "slack-sdk>=3.31.0",
    # Discord (Gateway WebSocket chat transport)
    "discord.py>=2.4.0,<3",
    # Utilities
    "python-dotenv>=1.2.2",
    "click>=8.1.0",
    "rich>=15.0.0",
    "questionary>=2.1.1",
    "prompt_toolkit>=3.0.0",
    "PyYAML>=6.0",
    "tzdata>=2026.1",
    # OpenTelemetry
    "opentelemetry-api>=1.41.0",
    "opentelemetry-sdk>=1.20.0",
    "opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http>=1.41.0",
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation>=0.40b0",
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-botocore>=0.40b0",
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-requests>=0.40b0",
    # Tracer
    "tracer_decorator",
    # Google APIs
    "google-api-python-client>=2.194.0,<3.0.0",
    "google-auth>=2.0.0,<3.0.0",
    # MongoDB
    "pymongo>=4.6.0,<6.0.0",
    # Redis
    "redis>=5.0.0,<9.0.0",
    # Signature verfication for discord
    "PyNaCl>=1.5.0",
    # MariaDB
    "pymysql>=1.1.0,<2.0.0",
    # ClickHouse (used by first-class SigNoz + ClickHouse integrations)
    "clickhouse-connect>=0.15.1,<1.0.0",
    "sentry-sdk>=2.59.0",
    # File locking for atomic store operations
    "filelock>=3.29.0",
    "psutil>=5.9",
    # Scheduler for cron-driven deliveries
    "APScheduler>=3.10.0,<4.0.0",
]

# With pytest-xdist (-n auto), each worker writes a fragment; put them under
# .pytest_cache/ (already gitignored) instead of .coverage.<hostname>.* at repo root.
[tool.coverage.run]
data_file = ".pytest_cache/.coverage"

[tool.vulture]
paths = [
  "bootstrap",
  "config",
  "core",
  "gateway",
  "infrastructure",
  "integrations",
  "surfaces",
  "tools",
]
exclude = [
  "gateway/tests/",
]
ignore_decorators = [
  "@*.command",          # Click / Typer subcommands
  "@*.group",
  "@*.callback",
  "@*.add",              # prompt_toolkit KeyBindings handlers
  "@app.*",              # FastAPI routes
  "@*router.*",          # FastAPI sub-routers (discord_router etc.)
  "@field_validator",    # Pydantic validators
  "@model_validator",
  "@validator",
  "@cache",
  "@lru_cache",
  "@tool",               # @tools.tool_decorator.tool registrations
  "@mcp.tool",
  "@register*",
]
ignore_names = [
  "shell_complete", "format_help", "show",        # Click overrides
  "__getattr__", "__dir__",                        # PEP 562 lazy exports
  "_normalize_*",                                  # Pydantic field validators
  "_require_*",                                    # Pydantic model validators
  "model_config",                                  # Pydantic v2 ConfigDict alias
  "verify_*",                                      # integrations/_verifiers_loader.py
  "validate_*_config",                             # integration config validators
  "*_config_from_env",                             # env-backed integration helpers
  "describe_llm_*", "llm_provider_*", "has_credentials_*",
  "get_account_*",
  "configure_grafana_cloud", "apply_otel_env_defaults", "validate_grafana_cloud_config",
  "on_thread_*", "on_assistant_*", "on_cron_*",
  "discord_interactions", "health_check",
  "version_check", "deep_health_check",
  "investigate_stream",
  "clean_env", "empty_store",                      # pytest fixtures
  "_isolated_*", "_reset_*", "_harness_*", "_no_*", # pytest fixtures / autouse hooks
  "_metering_*", "metering_on",
  "lex_document",                                  # prompt_toolkit Lexer API
  "do_*", "log_message",                           # http.server handler overrides
  "_accept_*", "_tab_*", "_shift_*", "_next_*", "_previous_*", "_on_*",
  "_quit", "_ctrl_c", "_bulk_*", "_handle_*", "_toggle", "_escape", "_submit",
  "_escape_checkbox", "_get_choice_tokens",
  "parse_chunk", "from_tokens",                    # fleet_monitoring meter protocol
  "steer", "emit_update", "on_update",             # agent runtime protocol surface
  "tool_description",                              # slash adapter protocol
  "reset_guardrail_evaluator", "reset_runtime_flags", "reset_cli_session_id",
  "register_external_tool_package", "get_tool_descriptors", "load_tool",
  "signoz_is_available",
  "load_remote_url", "save_named_remote", "delete_named_remote", "save_remote_ops_config",
  "is_cancelling", "idle_hint_ansi",
  "is_held", "holder", "holder_pid", "rate_per_minute",
  "should_block", "to_state",
  "RichGroup",
]

# uv installs this PEP 735 group by default (`uv sync`; omit with `--no-dev`).
# `pre-commit` is also under `[project.optional-dependencies] dev` for `pip install .[dev]`.
[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "pre-commit>=4.0.0",
    "pytest>=9.0.3",
    "pytest-cov>=7.1.0",
    # pytest.ini sets ``timeout``; without the plugin that key is silently
    # inert and pytest warns "Unknown config option". Keep it in every install
    # path, not just the ``dev`` extra that ``make install`` uses.
    "pytest-timeout>=2.3.0",
    "types-psutil>=7.2.2.20260408",
    "types-PyYAML>=6.0.12",
    "import-linter>=2.0",
    "vulture>=2.14",
]

name = "soctalk"
version = "0.2.1"
description = "SecOps LLM Agent using LangGraph with Wazuh, Cortex, and TheHive integration via MCP"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.14"
license = {text = "Apache-2.0"}
authors = [
    {name = "Gianluca Brigandi"}
]
keywords = ["secops", "siem", "langgraph", "mcp", "security", "incident-response"]

dependencies = [
    "langgraph>=0.2.0",
    "langchain>=0.3.0",
    "langchain-anthropic>=0.3.0",
    "langchain-openai>=0.3.0",
    "mcp>=1.0.0,<2",  # cap: the image installs unpinned (pip install .); 2.x renamed Tool.inputSchema and broke worker enrichment (#111). Lift once 2.x is validated.
    "pydantic>=2.0.0",
    "python-dotenv>=1.0.0",
    "aiohttp>=3.9.0",
    "rich>=13.0.0",
    "structlog>=24.0.0",
    "sqlmodel>=0.0.22",
    "asyncpg>=0.29.0",
    "greenlet>=3.0.0",
    "alembic>=1.13.0",
    "fastapi>=0.115.0",
    "uvicorn[standard]>=0.32.0",
    "sse-starlette>=2.1.0",
    "psycopg2-binary>=2.9.0",
    # V1 additions (codex P1-7):
    "prometheus-client>=0.20.0",
    "kubernetes>=29.0.0",
    # Async client for cross-namespace Secret reads from the chat agent
    # (per-tenant Wazuh routing). The sync ``kubernetes`` package would
    # block the event loop.
    "kubernetes-asyncio>=32.0.0",
    "pyyaml>=6.0",
    # Internal auth (internal-auth):

[project]
name = "imbue-common"
version = "0.1.20"
description = "Core libraries for Imbue projects"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
license = "MIT"
authors = [
    {name = "Imbue"},
    {name = "Josh Albrecht"},
]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 3 - Alpha",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
]
dependencies = [
    "argon2-cffi>=23.1",
    "boto3>=1.34",
    "click>=8.0",
    "cryptography>=42.0",
    "cowsay-python>=1.0.2",
    "httpx>=0.27",
    "loguru>=0.7",
    "pydantic>=2.0",
    "sentry-sdk>=2.63.0",
    "tenacity>=8.0",
    "traceback-with-variables>=2.0",
    "urllib3>=2.0",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = ["inline-snapshot>=0.13"]
# What a downstream test suite needs to use the test library this wheel ships
# (imbue.imbue_common.ratchet_testing, imbue.imbue_common.pytest_utils).
testing = [
    "import-linter>=2.0",
    "inline-snapshot>=0.13",
    "pytest>=9.0",
]

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/imbue-ai/mngr"
Repository = "https://github.com/imbue-ai/mngr"

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["imbue"]
exclude = ["*_test.py", "test_*.py", "**/conftest.py", "**/testing.py", "**/conftest_hooks.py"]

# Shared pytest settings (markers, filterwarnings, coverage report config)
# are centralized in:
#   libs/imbue_common/imbue/imbue_common/conftest_hooks.py
# The settings below remain here because they are read from pyproject.toml
# before any hooks run: addopts, coverage.run, inline-snapshot, timeout_func_only.
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
timeout_func_only = true
junit_family = "xunit1"
testpaths = ["."]
addopts = [
  "--cov=imbue.imbue_common",
  "--cov-report=term-missing",
  "--cov-report=xml",
  "--durations=20",
  "--timeout=10",
  "--timeout-method=signal",
  "--slow-tests-to-file",
  "--coverage-to-file",
]

[tool.coverage.run]
parallel = true
concurrency = ["multiprocessing", "thread"]
omit = [
  "*_test.py",
  "test_*.py",
  "*/tests/*",
  "*/conftest.py",
  "*/utils/testing.py",
  # Test infrastructure modules are exercised by tests that use them
  "*/conftest_hooks.py",
  "*/ratchet_testing/*",
  # The Sentry error-reporting machinery is mostly runtime integration glue
  # (the live ``sentry_sdk.init`` wiring, the custom HTTP transport's network
  # paths, and the threaded background S3 uploader) that needs a real Sentry

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[project]
name = "grillmaster"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Japanese variety show transcription"
requires-python = ">=3.13"
dependencies = [
    "claude-agent-sdk>=0.2.135",
    "click>=8.1.8",
    "elevenlabs>=2.24.0",
    "loguru>=0.7.3",
    "mcp>=1.28.0",
    "pycryptodomex>=3.23.0",
    "pydantic>=2.12.5",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.12.0",
    "rich>=14.3.1",
    "textual>=6.0.0",
    "tomlkit>=0.15.1",
    "typer>=0.21.1",
    "yt-dlp[default]>=2026.8.19",
]

[project.scripts]
grill = "grillmaster.cli:main"

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "pytest>=8.4",
    "ruff>=0.17",
    "basedpyright>=1.31",
    "import-linter>=2.3",
    "poethepoet>=0.37",
]

[tool.uv]
package = true

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/grillmaster"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
pythonpath = ["."]
markers = ["live: calls real agent CLIs and spends subscription quota"]
addopts = "-ra --strict-markers --import-mode=importlib -m 'not live'"

[tool.poe.tasks]
fmt = "ruff format"
fmt-check = "ruff format --check"
lint = "ruff check"
types = "basedpyright"
layers = "lint-imports"
test = "pytest"
schema = "python -m grillmaster.config.schema ${POE_ROOT}/grill.schema.json"
check = ["fmt-check", "lint", "types", "layers", "test"]

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py313"
line-length = 88
src = ["src", "tests"]
# Skill scripts follow their own conventions; code blocks in docs/ are sketches.
extend-exclude = [".agents", "docs"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E", "W", "F", "I", "N", "UP", "B", "A", "C4", "DTZ", "T10", "T20", "ISC",
    "ICN", "PIE", "PT", "RET", "SIM", "TID", "TC", "ARG", "PTH", "ERA", "PL",
    "TRY", "FLY", "PERF", "FURB", "LOG", "RUF", "S", "BLE", "FBT001", "FBT002",
    "SLF", "INP", "Q",
]
ignore = [
    "E501",    # the formatter owns line length; long prompt strings are fine
    "ISC001",  # conflicts with the formatter
    "TRY003",  # exception messages carry context on purpose
    "PLR0913", # argument bundles are collapsed into Inputs dataclasses instead
    "S603", "S607",  # external CLIs run on purpose, only via the two process modules
]
# Full-width punctuation in Chinese strings is content, not a confusable.
allowed-confusables = ["，", "。", "（", "）", "：", "；", "、", "「", "」", "！", "？", "～", "－", "〔", "〕"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**" = ["S101", "PLR2004", "ARG", "FBT", "SLF001", "INP001"]
"scripts/**" = ["T20", "INP001"]
"src/grillmaster/cli/**" = ["TC", "PLC0415"]  # Typer annotations; lazy imports keep --help fast
"src/grillmaster/agents/adapters/__init__.py" = ["PLC0415"]
"src/grillmaster/core/process.py" = ["TID251"]
"src/grillmaster/media/ffmpeg.py" = ["TID251"]
"src/grillmaster/agents/process.py" = ["TID251"]
"src/grillmaster/agents/adapters/claude.py" = ["TID251"]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["grillmaster"]
required-imports = ["from __future__ import annotations"]

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports]
ban-relative-imports = "parents"

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports.banned-api]
"subprocess.run".msg = "Use grillmaster.media.ffmpeg or grillmaster.agents.process"
"subprocess.Popen".msg = "Use grillmaster.media.ffmpeg or grillmaster.agents.process"
"subprocess.call".msg = "Use grillmaster.media.ffmpeg or grillmaster.agents.process"
"subprocess.check_output".msg = "Use grillmaster.media.ffmpeg or grillmaster.agents.process"
"asyncio.run".msg = "Pipeline code is thread-based; only agents.adapters.claude runs an event loop"

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-type-checking]
runtime-evaluated-base-classes = [
    "pydantic.BaseModel",
    "pydantic_settings.BaseSettings",
    "grillmaster.core.models.StrictModel",
    "grillmaster.core.models.FrozenModel",
]

[tool.ruff.lint.pylint]
max-branches = 15
max-returns = 8

[tool.basedpyright]
typeCheckingMode = "standard"
pythonVersion = "3.13"
include = ["src", "tests"]
reportMissingTypeStubs = false
reportUnknownMemberType = false

    "integration: marks tests as integration tests",
    "system_local: marks tests that use locally runnable external services (e.g. testcontainers)",
    "system_external: marks tests that depend on real external systems/secrets",
]

[tool.coverage.run]
# Coverage measurement settings
source = ["middleware"]
omit = [
    "*/tests/*",
    "*/__pycache__/*",
    "*/.venv/*",
    "*/venv/*",
    "*/.pytest_cache/*",
    "*/build/*",
    "*/dist/*",
    "*/*.egg-info/*",
]
branch = true  # Measure branch coverage

[tool.coverage.report]
# Coverage reporting settings
precision = 2
show_missing = true
skip_covered = false
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "def __repr__",
    "raise AssertionError",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "@abstractmethod",
    "@abc.abstractmethod",
]

[tool.coverage.html]
directory = "htmlcov"

[tool.hatch.version]
source = "vcs"
# CI docker tags look like `{id}-docker-v1.1.1` or
# `{id}-docker-v1.1.1-introduce-report-lib.4`. The branch suffix after
# X.Y.Z is GitVersion SemVer, not PEP 440 — hatch-vcs rejects it. Capture
# only the numeric triple (same rationale as docker/Dockerfile.sql_to_arc).
tag-pattern = '^(?:\d+-docker-)?(?P<version>[vV]?\d+\.\d+\.\d+)(?:-.*)?$'

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
include = ["README.md"]

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling", "hatch-vcs"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[project]
name = "upstream-api"
version = "1.1.1"
description = "A shared learning library with personal course tracking and resource recommendations"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.14,<3.15"
dependencies = [
    "bcrypt>=4.1.2",
    "fastapi>=0.110.0",
    "pydantic>=2.0.0",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.0.0",
    "sqlalchemy[asyncio]>=2.0.0",
    "asyncpg>=0.29.0",
    "alembic>=1.13.0",
    "uvicorn[standard]>=0.27.0",
    "httpx>=0.28.1",
    "opentelemetry-api>=1.28.2",
    "opentelemetry-sdk>=1.28.2",
    "opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http>=1.28.2",
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-fastapi>=0.49b2",
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-httpx>=0.49b2",
    "opentelemetry-instrumentation-sqlalchemy>=0.49b2",
]

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "ruff>=0.14.14",
    "mypy>=1.11.2",
    "pre-commit>=4.0.1",
    "pytest>=8.0.0",
    "pytest-cov>=5.0.0",
    "anyio>=4.0.0",
    "pillow>=10.4.0",
    "pip-audit>=2.9.0",
    "import-linter>=2.7",
]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 128

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Keep this ruleset architecture-focused and low-noise:
# - import hygiene/boundaries (`I`, `TID`)
# - undefined names (`F821`)
# - risky exception handling (`BLE`)
# - avoid ad-hoc print debugging in app code (`T20`)
# - function complexity guardrails (`C901`, `PLR091x`)
select = ["I", "F821", "BLE", "TID", "T20", "C901", "PLR0911", "PLR0912", "PLR0913", "PLR0915", "D102", "D103", "D107"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Non-product code keeps a lighter baseline:
# - tests may use print/debug output and verbose setup patterns
# - scripts may stay operational and direct
# - Alembic migrations are one-off delivery artifacts
"tests/**/*.py" = ["T20", "C901", "PLR0911", "PLR0912", "PLR0913", "PLR0915", "D102", "D103", "D107"]
"scripts/**/*.py" = ["T20", "D102", "D103", "D107"]
"alembic/**/*.py" = ["D102", "D103", "D107"]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["backend"]
combine-as-imports = true
force-sort-within-sections = true
lines-after-imports = 2
order-by-type = false
section-order = ["future", "standard-library", "third-party", "first-party", "local-folder"]

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports]
ban-relative-imports = "all"

[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "google"

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
# Function complexity limits.
max-complexity = 19

[tool.ruff.lint.pylint]
# Function complexity limits.
max-args = 10
max-branches = 12
max-returns = 7
max-statements = 67

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.14"
pretty = true
show_error_codes = true
warn_return_any = true
warn_unused_ignores = true
warn_redundant_casts = true
warn_unreachable = true
strict_equality = true
no_implicit_optional = true
check_untyped_defs = true
disallow_untyped_defs = true
ignore_missing_imports = true
exclude = ["^tests/"]

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
# API endpoints permit untyped definitions; other backend modules require annotations.
module = [
    "backend.api.*",
    "backend.main",
]
disallow_untyped_defs = false

layeredArchitecture()
            .consideringOnlyDependenciesInLayers()
            .layer(CORE_API)
            .definedBy("$ROOT_PACKAGE.coreapi..")
            .layer(DOMAIN)
            .definedBy("$ROOT_PACKAGE.domain..")
            .layer(STORAGE)
            .definedBy("$ROOT_PACKAGE.storage..")
            .layer(CLIENTS)
            .definedBy("$ROOT_PACKAGE.clients..")
            .layer(MODULES)
            .definedBy("$ROOT_PACKAGE.modules..")
            .layer(COMMON)
            .definedBy("$ROOT_PACKAGE.common..")
            // 진입 모듈은 최상위 — 아무도 의존하지 못한다
            .whereLayer(CORE_API)
            .mayNotBeAccessedByAnyLayer()
            // domain 은 진입 모듈에서만 접근(storage·c

classes()
            .that()
            .areAnnotatedWith("jakarta.persistence.Entity")
            .or()
            .areAnnotatedWith("jakarta.persistence.MappedSuperclass")
            .should()
            .resideInAPackage("..storage..")
            .allowEmptyShould(true)
            .check(importedClasses)
    }

    @Test
    fun `Spring Data Repository 는 storage 레이어에만 존재한다`() {

noClasses()
            .that()
            .resideInAPackage("$ROOT_PACKAGE.common..")
            .should()
            .dependOnClassesThat()
            .resideInAnyPackage("..coreapi..", "..domain..", "..storage..", "..clients..", "..modules..")
            .allowEmptyShould(true)
            .check(importedClasses)
    }

    @Test
    fun `레이어 간 순환 의존이 없다`() {

slices()
            .matching("$ROOT_PACKAGE.(*)..")
            .should()
            .beFreeOfCycles()
            .check(importedClasses)
    }

    companion object {
        private const val ROOT_PACKAGE = "com.tj.boilerplate"
        private const val CORE_API = "CoreApi"
        private const val DOMAIN = "Domain"
        private const val STORAGE = "Storage"
        private const val CLIENTS = "Clients"
        private const val MODULES = "Modules"
        private const val COMMON = "Common"
    }
}

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 120
indent-width = 4

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["ALL"]
ignore = [
    "COM812", # trailing commas
    "FBT",    # boolean trap
    "INP001", # part of an implicit namespace package
    "RSE102", # Unnecessary parentheses on raised exception
    "TRY003", # strings in exceptions
    "FIX002", # resolve TODOs
    "TD003",  # leave link to issue near TODO
    "RUF001", # ambiguous characters (like cyrillic)
    "RUF002", # ambiguous characters (like cyrillic)
    "RUF003", # ambiguous characters (like cyrillic)
    "TC001",  # runtime frameworks inspect annotations; keep imports explicit
    "TC002",  # runtime frameworks inspect annotations; keep imports explicit
    "TC003",  # runtime frameworks inspect annotations; keep imports explicit
    "S105",   # many public error-code/template constants look like token names
    "PLR0913", # FastAPI/Dishka route signatures intentionally inject many services
    "PLR0917", # same rationale as PLR0913: DI/route/data signatures take many positional parameters
    "D417",   # argument docs are noisy for DI-heavy route handlers
    "N815",   # external Minecraft/Yggdrasil DTO fields are camelCase by contract
    "D203",   # incompatible with D211
    "D213",   # incompatible with D212
    "S104",   # local dev entrypoint intentionally binds to all interfaces in containers
    "UP037",  # SQLModel relationships need quoted forward refs for SQLAlchemy mapper resolution
    "CPY001", # private project; source files carry no copyright header
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"migrations/*.py" = [

]
"tests/**/*.py" = [
    "PLR2004", # explicit boundary values make test scenarios readable
    "S101", # assertions are the pytest contract
]
"tests/test_index_contract_mechanism.py" = [

build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[tool.hatch.version]
source = "uv-dynamic-versioning"

[tool.uv-dynamic-versioning]
vcs = "git"
style = "pep440"

[tool.fastapi]
entrypoint = "acodex.http.app:app"

[tool.uv]
cache-keys = [{ file = "pyproject.toml" }, { git = { commit = true, tags = true } }]

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.11"
strict = true
exclude = ["^references/", "^tmp/"]
ignore_missing_imports = true
local_partial_types = true
warn_unreachable = true
enable_error_code = [
    "truthy-bool",
    "truthy-iterable",
    "redundant-expr",
    "unused-awaitable",
    "ignore-without-code",
    "possibly-undefined",
    "redundant-self",
    "unimported-reveal",
    "deprecated",
    "exhaustive-match",
]
disable_error_code = [
    "unused-ignore",
    "no-any-return",
]

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["tests.*"]
strict = false
disable_error_code = ["valid-type", "misc", "untyped-decorator", "attr-defined"]

[tool.pyright]
include = ["src/acodex", "tests"]
exclude = ["references", "tmp", ".venv"]
pythonVersion = "3.11"
venvPath = "."
venv = ".venv"
typeCheckingMode = "basic"
strict = ["src/acodex"]
reportUnknownMemberType = false
reportUnknownArgumentType = false
reportUnknownVariableType = false
reportMissingTypeStubs = false
reportPrivateUsage = false

[tool.pyrefly]
project-includes = ["src/acodex", "tests"]
project-excludes = ["references", "tmp", ".venv"]
preset = "strict"
min-severity = "warn"

[tool.pyrefly.errors]
implicit-any-attribute = false
implicit-any-empty-container = false
missing-attribute = false
missing-override-decorator = false
unused-ignore = true

[tool.slotscheck]
strict-imports = false
exclude-classes = '''
(
  :.*Error
  |:.*Exception
  |acodex\.config\..*:.*Config
  |acodex\.config\.models:.*Config
  |acodex\.core\.codex_app\.bridge:CodexAppBridgeSettings
  |acodex\.core\.codex_app\.cdp\.settings:CodexCDPSettings
)
'''

[tool.codespell]
skip = [
    "__pycache__",
    "_build",
    ".mypy_cache",
    "*.lock",
    "references/**",
    "tmp/**",
]

[tool.typos.files]
extend-exclude = [
    "__pycache__",
    "_build",
    ".mypy_cache",
    "*.lock",
    "references/**",
    "tmp/**",
]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
pythonpath = ["."]
addopts = [
    "-ra",
    "--strict-markers",
    "--strict-config",
]
markers = [
    "real_integration: opt-in tests that exercise a live local Codex CLI setup",
]
filterwarnings = [
    "error",
    # Ignore ResourceWarnings from unclosed sockets/event loops during GC
    # These come from pytest-asyncio internals and are not related to test code
    "ignore:unclosed <socket.socket:ResourceWarning",
    "ignore:unclosed event loop:ResourceWarning",
]

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["src/acodex"]
branch = true
parallel = true

[tool.coverage.report]
fail_under = 100
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "if typing.TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "@overload",
    "@typing.overload",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "\\.\\.\\.",
]
show_missing = true
skip_covered = true

  "FBT002",  # boolean default in test helpers are fine

  "PLC2701", # private imports for test access

  "PT017",   # exception variable assertions in tests
  "PT018",   # compound assertions in tests
  "RUF029",  # async test helpers without await

  # Docs: https://pypi.org/project/covdefaults
  "covdefaults",
]

  # Is not reported, because is imported during setup:
  "server/settings/components/logging.py",
  # ASGI entrypoint — imported only by the application server, not tests:
  "server/asgi.py",
  # Production settings — only active in production deployments:
  "server/settings/environments/production.py",
  # Django management entry point — runs only as a CLI command, not via tests:
  "manage.py",
  # Third-party package metadata (dist-info text files picked up by template plugin):

  ".local/**",
  # Sphinx docs templates — not testable Django templates:

[tool.django-stubs]

# Deptry: https://deptry.com/usage/
[tool.deptry]
# Local application package; imports like `from server...` are first-party.
known_first_party = ["server"]

[tool.deptry.per_rule_ignores]
# Used via Django settings / deploy
DEP002 = [
  "django-axes",               # INSTALLED_APPS, middleware, auth backend
  "django-cors-headers",       # INSTALLED_APPS + middleware via dotted path
  "django-permissions-policy", # Permissions-Policy middleware (dotted path)
  "psycopg2-binary",           # PostgreSQL driver for `ENGINE = ***REMOVED***ql`
  "gunicorn",                  # production WSGI process (docker/, CI)
]
# Imported directly but pulled in only as transitive deps

  "attrs",      # imported directly, provided transitively via django-modern-rest extra
  "msgspec",    # DTOs (also via django-modern-rest extra)
  "pydantic",   # payloads/schemas (also via django-modern-rest extra)
]
# Dev dependencies referenced from application code
DEP004 = [
  "debug_toolbar",     # DEBUG urls/settings
]

noClasses()
                .that().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..domain..")
                .should().dependOnClassesThat().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..application..")
                .because("the domain layer is the innermost ring and must not depend on the application layer")
                .check(allClasses);

noClasses()
                .that().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..domain..")
                .should().dependOnClassesThat().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..adapter..")
                .because("the domain layer must stay free of adapter concerns")
                .check(allClasses);

noClasses()
                .that().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..application..")
                .should().dependOnClassesThat().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..adapter..")
                .because("application services should orchestrate ports instead of depending on adapters directly")
                .check(allClasses);

noClasses()
                .that().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..adapter..inbound..")
                .should().dependOnClassesThat().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..adapter..outbound..")
                .because("inbound adapters must communicate through ports instead of reaching into outbound adapters")
                .check(allClasses);

noClasses()
                .that().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..adapter..outbound..")
                .should().dependOnClassesThat().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..adapter..inbound..")
                .because("outbound adapters must not depend on inbound adapter implementation details")
                .check(allClasses);

classes()
                .that().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..domain..model..")
                .and().areNotEnums()
                .and().areNotInterfaces()
                .and().areNotAnonymousClasses()
                .should().beAssignableTo(Record.class)
                .because("hexagon domain models should be immutable records unless they are enums or closed interfaces")
                .check(allClasses);

classes()
                .that().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..domain..model..")
                .should().notBeAnnotatedWith(JAKARTA_PERSISTENCE_ANNOTATION)
                .because("jakarta.persistence annotations are adapter concerns and must not leak into hexagon domain models")
                .check(allClasses);

classes()
                .that().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..application..port..inbound..")
                .and().areInterfaces()
                .should().haveSimpleNameEndingWith("UseCase")
                .because("inbound port interfaces represent use case contracts and should end with UseCase")
                .check(allClasses);

classes()
                .that().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..application..port..inbound..")
                .and().areNotInterfaces()
                .should().beAssignableTo(Record.class)
                .because("supporting types in inbound port packages should be immutable records")
                .check(allClasses);

classes()
                .that().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..domain..port..outbound..")
                .should().beInterfaces()
                .because("outbound ports define contracts that adapters implement")
                .check(allClasses);

classes()
                .that().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..application..")
                .and(IMPLEMENTS_USE_CASE_INTERFACE)
                .should().haveSimpleNameEndingWith("Service")
                .because("hexagon use case implementations should follow the Service naming convention")
                .check(allClasses);

classes()
                .that().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..application..")
                .and(IMPLEMENTS_USE_CASE_INTERFACE)
                .should().beAnnotatedWith(ApplicationScoped.class)
                .because("hexagon use case implementations should be exposed as application-scoped beans")
                .check(allClasses);

classes()
                .that().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..")
                .and().areAnnotatedWith(Entity.class)
                .should().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..adapter..outbound..")
                .because("hexagon JPA entities must be confined to outbound adapters")
                .check(allClasses);

classes()
                .that().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..adapter..outbound..")
                .and().areAnnotatedWith(Entity.class)
                .should().haveSimpleNameEndingWith("Entity")
                .because("hexagon JPA entities should follow the Entity suffix naming convention")
                .check(allClasses);

classes()
                .that().areAssignableTo(PanacheRepository.class)
                .should().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..adapter..outbound..")
                .because("Panache repositories are outbound persistence adapters and should stay in that layer")
                .check(allClasses);

classes()
                .that().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..")
                .and().areAnnotatedWith(Mapper.class)
                .should().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..adapter..")
                .because("MapStruct mappers are infrastructure adapters and should only live in adapter packages")
                .check(allClasses);

noClasses()
                .that().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..")
                .and().resideOutsideOfPackage("..application..")
                .should().beAnnotatedWith(Transactional.class)
                .because("hexagon transaction boundaries belong to application services, not adapters or domain code")
                .check(allClasses);

noMethods()
                .that().areDeclaredInClassesThat().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..")
                .and().areDeclaredInClassesThat().resideOutsideOfPackage("..application..")
                .should().beAnnotatedWith(Transactional.class)
                .because("hexagon transaction boundaries should not be declared on non-application methods")
                .check(allClasses);

classes()
                .that().resideInAPackage("..hexagon..application..")
                .and(IMPLEMENTS_USE_CASE_INTERFACE)

classes()

[tool.bandit]
exclude_dirs = [
  "benchmarks",
  "examples",
  "scripts",

]
skips = [
  "B101"
]

[tool.coverage.html]
directory = "htmlcov"
skip_covered = false
skip_empty = false

[tool.coverage.report]
exclude_lines = [
  "@(abc\\.)?abstractmethod",
  "class .*\\bProtocol\\):",
  "def __repr__",
  "if 0:",
  "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
  "if self.debug:",
  "if settings.DEBUG",
  "pass",
  "pragma: no cover",
  "raise AssertionError",
  "raise ImportError",
  "raise NotImplementedError"
]
fail_under = 80
precision = 2
show_missing = true
skip_covered = false

[tool.coverage.run]
branch = true
omit = [
  "*/__pycache__/*",
  "*/conftest.py",
  "*/examples/*",
  "*/scripts/*",
  "*/tests/*"
]
parallel = true
source = ["src"]

[tool.coverage.xml]
output = "coverage.xml"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]
include = [
  "LICENSE",
  "README.md",
  "pyproject.toml",
  "src/calibrax"
]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/calibrax"]

[tool.hatch.version]
path = "src/calibrax/__init__.py"

[tool.interrogate]
exclude = ["examples", "scripts", "tests"]
fail-under = 80
ignore-init-method = true
ignore-init-module = false
ignore-magic = true

[tool.pydoclint]
allow-init-docstring = true
arg-type-hints-in-docstring = false
# Instance attributes are documented under Attributes per the Google style; pydoclint would
# compare them with class-level attributes only.
check-class-attributes = false
# Annotations are the source of truth for types; docstrings carry the prose.
check-return-types = false
check-yield-types = false
# `# noqa: DOC...` is read from the def line, where propagated exceptions are annotated.
native-mode-noqa-location = "definition"
style = "google"

[tool.pylint."messages_control"]
max-args = 10
max-attributes = 12

[tool.pyright]
exclude = [
  "examples",
  "scripts"
]
include = [
  "src",
  "tests"
]
pythonVersion = "3.12"
reportMissingTypeStubs = false
typeCheckingMode = "standard"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
addopts = "--strict-markers --strict-config --verbose --tb=short --color=yes --durations=10 --disable-warnings --cov=src/calibrax --cov-report=term-missing --cov-report=html --cov-fail-under=80 --timeout=300 --json-report --json-report-file=temp/test-results.json --json-report-indent=2"
cache_dir = ".pytest_cache"
console_output_style = "progress"
filterwarnings = [
  "ignore:.*CUDA-enabled jaxlib.*",
  "ignore:.*cuSPARSE.*",
  "ignore::DeprecationWarning:jax.*",
  "ignore::DeprecationWarning:pkg_resources.*",
  "ignore::UserWarning:jax._src.xla_bridge",

markers = [
  "benchmark: marks tests as performance benchmarks (requires pytest-benchmark)",
  "contract: marks tests as contract tests",
  "cpu: marks tests that should run on CPU only",
  "cuda: marks tests that specifically test CUDA functionality",
  "doctest: marks tests as documentation example tests",
  "e2e: marks tests as end-to-end tests",
  "gpu: marks tests that require GPU (deselect with '-m \"not gpu\"')",
  "gpu_required: marks tests as requiring GPU (will fail if GPU unavailable)",
  "integration: marks tests as integration tests",
  "performance: marks tests as performance tests (alias for benchmark)",
  "slow: marks tests as slow (deselect with '-m \"not slow\"')",
  "unit: marks tests as unit tests"
]
minversion = "6.0"
python_classes = "Test*"
python_files = "test_*.py"
python_functions = "test_*"
testpaths = ["tests"]

MPLBACKEND = {skip_if_set = true, value = "Agg"}

[tool.ruff]
extend-include = ["*.ipynb"]
line-length = 100
# First-party modules come from src/ and the isort settings only, so an untracked directory at the
# repository root (wandb's run logs are ./wandb) cannot make a third-party package first-party.
src = ["src"]
target-version = "py312"

[tool.ruff.format]
indent-style = "space"
line-ending = "auto"
quote-style = "double"
skip-magic-trailing-comma = false

[tool.ruff.lint]
# pydoclint's codes, so a `# noqa: DOC...` is not reported as unknown.
external = ["DOC"]
fixable = [
  "E",
  "F",
  "F401",
  "F841",
  "I001",
  "W",
  "W291",
  "W292",
  "W293"
]
ignore = [
  # Google-style docstrings: D203 and D213 conflict with D211 and D212.
  "D203",
  "D213",
  # The formatter owns line length.
  "E501",
  # The __all__ lists are grouped by domain with comments; a sort would destroy the grouping.
  "RUF022",
  # Exception messages are written inline; a message class per raise is noise.
  "TRY003"
]
select = [
  "ANN",
  "ARG",
  "B",
  "C4",
  "C90",
  "D",
  "E",
  "F",
  "I",
  "N",
  "PIE",
  "PL",
  "PT",
  "PTH",
  "RET",
  "RUF",
  "S",
  "SIM",
  "T20",
  "TRY",
  "UP",
  "W"
]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
combine-as-imports = true
known-first-party = ["calibrax", "tests"]
lines-after-imports = 2
order-by-type = false

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 10

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Examples are narrative walkthroughs: they print, and their main functions are long.
"examples/*" = ["C901", "PLR0915", "T20"]
# Development scripts report on stdout.
"scripts/*" = ["T20"]
# The CLI's output is print by design.
"src/calibrax/cli/*" = ["T201"]
# Test factories are keyword-only builders with one parameter per field.
"tests/*" = ["D", "PLR0913", "PLR2004", "S101"]
# Local stubs for untyped libraries spell names as the library does (NVML's camelCase).
"typings/*" = ["N"]

[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "google"

[tool.ruff.lint.pylint]
max-args = 8

[tool.substrax.compute]
backend = "modal"

[tool.substrax.compute.backends.modal]
outputs_volume = "calibrax-example-outputs"

[tool.substrax.compute.jobs.examples]
accelerator = {kind = "L4"}
examples = ["examples/metrics"]
extras = ["cuda12"]
runtime = {platforms = ["cuda"], preallocate = false, xla_flags = ["--xla_gpu_deterministic_ops=true"]}
task_timeout_seconds = 1800
timeout_seconds = 10800

[tool.uv]
# calibrax does not import optax; flax does. Below 0.2.8 optax calls
# jax.config.update("jax_pmap_shmap_merge"), which jax removed in 0.10, so importing
# flax raises AttributeError and takes out collection for the whole suite. Constrained
# rather than declared, because this is a transitive requirement, not a direct one.
constraint-dependencies = ["optax>=0.2.8"]
python-preference = "only-managed"

[tool.uv.pip]
find-links = [

]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/cognithor"]
# Templates (.jinja / .yaml / non-.py files) are shipped automatically by the
# `packages` discovery — Hatch walks the package tree and includes all files,
# not just .py. The earlier explicit `force-include` of the templates
# directory caused PyPI to reject the wheel with "Duplicate filename in local
# headers" because the same files landed twice (once via packages, once via
# force-include). Keep it out — packages alone is correct.

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "function"
markers = [
    "slow: marks tests as slow",
    "integration: marks tests requiring external services",
    "security_contract: marks security contract invariant tests",
    "benchmark: performance budget tests (spec §8.5)",
]
filterwarnings = [
    # starlette uses deprecated multipart import — third-party, can't fix
    "ignore::PendingDeprecationWarning:starlette",
    # asyncio transport cleanup after event loop is closed (Windows + Linux)
    "ignore:Exception ignored in.*Transport:pytest.PytestUnraisableExceptionWarning",
    # Mock artifacts: coroutines created by AsyncMock but never awaited
    "ignore:coroutine .* was never awaited:RuntimeWarning",
]

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py312"
line-length = 100
src = ["src", "tests"]
# Crew scaffolder templates are Jinja2 source trees, not Python packages —
# they use ``{{ project_name }}`` in directory/file names and ship ``.jinja``
# templates that aren't valid Python until rendered.
extend-exclude = ["src/cognithor/crew/templates"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E", "W", "F", "I", "N", "UP", "B", "SIM", "TCH", "RUF",
]
ignore = [
    "RUF001",  # Ambiguous EN DASH in strings (korrekt im Deutschen)
    "RUF002",  # Ambiguous EN DASH in docstrings
    "RUF003",  # Ambiguous EN DASH in comments
    "RUF012",  # Mutable class defaults — dataclass pattern, harmless
    "N806",    # Non-lowercase variable in function — Windows API constants
    "N801",    # Invalid class name — test naming conventions
    "N802",    # Invalid function name — intentional conventions
    "N805",    # Invalid first argument name — intentional
    "N811",    # Constant imported as non-constant — intentional
    "N814",    # Camelcase imported as constant — intentional
    "N818",    # Error suffix on exception name — intentional
    "E402",    # Module import not at top — conditional imports by design
    "E741",    # Ambiguous variable name — l, O, I in math code
    "SIM117",  # Multiple with statements — style preference only
    "SIM103",  # Needless bool — style preference
    "SIM108",  # If-else-block instead of if-exp — readability preference
    "SIM112",  # Uncapitalized env vars — intentional
    "SIM115",  # Open file with context handler — controlled usage
    "B027",    # Empty method without abstract decorator — intentional pattern
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"__init__.py" = ["F401"]  # Re-exports in __init__.py are intentional
"tests/test_install_fixes.py" = ["E501"]  # Embedded shell/JS scripts in strings
"tests/test_packs/test_installer.py" = ["TC003"]  # Path used in runtime test bodies via pytest fixtures
"tests/test_gateway/test_video_cleanup.py" = ["TC003"]  # Path used in runtime test bodies via pytest fixtures

"src/cognithor/crew/compiler_hierarchical.py" = ["TC001"]  # CrewAgent/CrewTask used at runtime in pure-function signatures
"src/cognithor/crew/crew.py" = ["TC001"]  # CrewAgent/CrewTask/CrewProcess must be imported at runtime for Pydantic validation
# Hardware-Aware Runtime: dataclasses + manifest models are accessed at runtime
# (e.g. `manifest.tiers` iteration, `Solution.blockers` access). Ruff's TC001
# over-flags these because of `from __future__ import annotations`.

    "src/cognithor/_bundled_packs/.*",
