[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[project]
name = "rigplane"
version = "3.0.0b18"
description = "Multi-vendor radio control library and Web UI with native providers and planned Hamlib-backed CAT coverage"
readme = "README.md"
license = "MIT"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
dependencies = [
    "aiohttp>=3.13.3",
    "pyserial>=3.5",
    "pyserial-asyncio>=0.6",
    "opuslib",
    "sounddevice>=0.4,<0.5; sys_platform == 'win32' and platform_machine != 'ARM64'",
    "sounddevice>=0.5; sys_platform != 'win32' or platform_machine == 'ARM64'",
    "numpy",
    "platformdirs>=4.2",
]
authors = [
    { name = "Sergey Morozik", email = "morozsm@gmail.com" },
]
keywords = ["rigplane", "ham-radio", "amateur-radio", "transceiver", "icom", "yaesu", "xiegu", "lab599", "ci-v", "cat", "rigctld", "ic-7610", "ic-7300", "ic-705", "ftx-1"]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 4 - Beta",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License",
    "Topic :: Communications :: Ham Radio",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
]

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://rigplane.dev/"
Documentation = "https://rigplane.dev/"
Repository = "https://github.com/rigplane/rigplane-core"
Issues = "https://github.com/rigplane/rigplane-core/issues"

[project.scripts]
rigplane = "rigplane.cli:main"
# Deprecated alias of `rigplane` — prints DeprecationWarning then forwards.
icom-lan = "icom_lan._cli_shim:main"

[project.optional-dependencies]
# `audio` and `bridge` extras are kept as no-op aliases for backwards
# compatibility — `opuslib`, `sounddevice`, and `numpy` are now part of
# the core dependencies (#1090). New users should run `pip install rigplane`.
audio = []
bridge = []
scope = [
    "pillow>=10.0",
]
dsp = ["scipy>=1.11"]
webrtc = ["aiortc>=1.9"]
tls = ["cryptography>=41.0"]
# SoapySDR Python bindings have no official PyPI wheel — they come from the
# system (`python3-soapysdr` on Debian/Raspberry Pi OS) or a SoapySDR build.
# The extra is a feature marker for the SDR IQ source; it adds no packages
# and runtime dependencies are unchanged.
sdr = []
# Dev/build-only: pydantic drives the public-state JSON-Schema → TypeScript
# codegen (MOR-881). It must NEVER enter the runtime `dependencies` above —
# core stays zero-runtime-dep. Only the conformance test and the
# `scripts/gen_state_types.py` generator import it; `state_schema.py` is never
# imported on the live request path.
# `jsonschema` drives the consumer-driven contract (CDC) runner (MOR-883):
# `scripts/run_consumer_contracts.py` validates the real producer artifacts
# against consumer-authored expectations. Like `pydantic`, it is DEV/CI-only and
# must NEVER enter the runtime `dependencies` above — core stays zero-runtime-dep.
# Only the runner and its conformance test import it.
codegen = ["pydantic>=2.13,<3", "jsonschema>=4.0"]
dev = ["pytest", "pytest-asyncio", "pytest-cov", "pytest-timeout", "pytest-xdist", "ruff", "mypy", "pydantic>=2.13,<3", "jsonschema>=4.0"]

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "import-linter>=2.0,<3",
    "mkdocs-material>=9.7.3",
    "mkdocstrings[python]>=1.0.3",
    "mypy>=1.18.1",
    # Dev/build-only — drives MOR-881 state-payload codegen + conformance test.
    # NOT a runtime dependency (core stays zero-runtime-dep).
    "pydantic>=2.13,<3",
    # Dev/build-only — drives the MOR-883 consumer-driven contract runner.
    # NOT a runtime dependency (core stays zero-runtime-dep).
    "jsonschema>=4.0",
    # Dev/test-only — imported only by the property tests under tests/property.
    "hypothesis>=6.0",
    "pytest>=8.0",
    "pytest-asyncio>=1.3.0",
    "pytest-cov>=7.0.0",
    "pytest-timeout>=2.0",
    "pytest-xdist>=3.6",
    "ruff>=0.15.2",
    "types-pyserial>=3.5",
    # Dev/CI-only — drives the weekly mutation-testing trend job.
    "mutmut>=3.8,<4",
]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/rigplane", "src/icom_lan"]
# The web UI is placed at src/rigplane/web/static exclusively via the custom
# build hook's force-include (see hatch_build.py). When building a wheel from an
# sdist (uv build's default sdist->wheel chain), the sdist has already
# materialized src/rigplane/web/static on disk; exclude it from normal project
# file selection so the force-include is the single source and the tree is not
# bundled twice.
exclude = ["src/rigplane/web/static"]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.force-include]
"rigs" = "rigplane/rigs"

# Builds the Svelte web UI during packaging (if not prebuilt) and force-includes
# the result at src/rigplane/web/static for BOTH wheel and sdist targets, so
# source/git installs are self-contained. See hatch_build.py.
[tool.hatch.build.hooks.custom]
path = "hatch_build.py"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "function"
markers = [
    "integration: tests requiring real radio hardware (skip if not configured)",
    "hardware: opt-in tests that may key a real transmitter or require attached devices",
    "e2e: end-to-end tests for PCM API and CLI audio workflows",
    "slow: marks tests as slow (deselect with '-m \"not slow\"')",
    "validation_hardware: real-radio validation runs; requires explicit env opt-in",
    "benchmark: wall-clock measurements, reported rather than gated on; deselected by default (run with -m benchmark)",
    "property: Hypothesis property-based tests under tests/property",
]
testpaths = ["tests"]
# Repo root on sys.path so tests can import the top-level rigplane_testkit package.
pythonpath = ["."]
python_files = ["test_*.py"]
python_classes = ["Test*"]
python_functions = ["test_*"]
addopts = "-v --tb=short -m 'not slow and not benchmark'"

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py311"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E4", "E7", "E9", "F", "TID251"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/*" = ["TID251"]
# Build/codegen scripts may import tier-3 internals (e.g. the state-payload
# schema for TypeScript codegen, MOR-881). They are dev/build-only, never
# shipped in the wheel.
"scripts/**" = ["TID251"]
# CLI is the orchestrator that composes tier-3 web and rigctld servers (issue-blessed).
"src/rigplane/cli/**" = ["TID251"]
# Package entry point dispatches to cli.main.
"src/rigplane/__main__.py" = ["TID251"]
# Backwards-compat shim — re-exports rigplane internals; banned-imports
# checks for tier-3 boundaries don't apply to a deprecated alias package.
"src/icom_lan/**" = ["TID251", "F401", "F403"]

[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports.banned-api]
"rigplane.radio.IcomRadio".msg = "Use radio_protocol.Radio in web/ modules (and capability protocols) instead of IcomRadio."
"rigplane.web".msg = "tier 3 — internal; do not import outside web/ subtree (tests are exempt)."
"rigplane.rigctld".msg = "tier 3 — internal; do not import outside rigctld/ subtree (tests are exempt)."
"rigplane.cli".msg = "tier 3 — internal; do not import outside cli + tests."

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.11"
follow_imports = "skip"

# Backwards-compat shim — pure re-export façade, no semantic content to type-check.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["icom_lan", "icom_lan.*"]
follow_imports = "skip"
warn_unused_ignores = false

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["rigplane.web.*"]
strict = true
follow_imports = "skip"
warn_unused_ignores = false

# Codegen-only contract schema (MOR-881). Under the global ``follow_imports =
# skip`` policy pydantic's ``BaseModel`` resolves to ``Any``, so strict mypy
# reports "cannot subclass BaseModel (has type Any)". The module is dev/build-
# only (never on the runtime import path) and is covered by the conformance
# test + the codegen drift gate, so suppress that single ``misc`` diagnostic
# rather than wiring the pydantic mypy plugin into the strict web boundary.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["rigplane.web.state_schema"]
disable_error_code = ["misc"]

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["cryptography", "cryptography.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["scipy", "scipy.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = true

# ``Pillow`` is an optional dep behind ``[scope]``; suppress the missing-stubs
# error so ``mypy src/`` is clean regardless of whether Pillow is installed.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = ["PIL", "PIL.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = true

# Audio / DSP deps without published type stubs.  ``numpy``, ``sounddevice``
# and ``opuslib`` ship with the core install since #1090; ``scipy`` is still
# behind the ``[dsp]`` extra.  Ignore missing stubs so mypy runs cleanly.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
    "numpy",
    "numpy.*",
    "sounddevice",
    "sounddevice.*",
    "opuslib",
    "opuslib.*",
]
ignore_missing_imports = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
    "rigplane.cli",
    "rigplane.web.radio_poller",
    "rigplane.web.handlers.control",
    "rigplane.rigctld.routing",
    "rigplane.rigctld.handler",
]
disable_error_code = ["attr-defined"]

[tool.mutmut]
# Weekly mutation-testing trend job. The whole src/ tree is
# copied into mutants/ so imports stay intact; only_mutate restricts
# mutation to the small high-risk modules of the stabilization program.
source_paths = ["src/"]
# Top-level test-support and rig-profile data; without these the copied
# tree cannot import rigplane_testkit (pythonpath=["."]) or discover any
# rig TOML profiles (profiles: _RIG_DIRS).
also_copy = ["rigplane_testkit/", "rigs/"]
only_mutate = [
    "src/rigplane/web/_delta_encoder.py",
    "src/rigplane/rigctld/protocol.py",
    "src/rigplane/core/civ.py",
    "src/rigplane/audio/_codecs.py",
    "src/rigplane/commands/_frame.py",
    "src/rigplane/core/types.py",
    "src/rigplane/core/state_store.py",
    "src/rigplane/core/acquisition_drain.py",
    "src/rigplane/runtime/controller_authority.py",
    "src/rigplane/core/tx_safety.py",
    "src/rigplane/core/tx_target.py",
    "src/rigplane/core/tx_observation.py",
    "src/rigplane/runtime/managed_tx_fence.py",
    "src/rigplane/runtime/managed_tx_state.py",
    "src/rigplane/web/handlers/rigctl.py",
    "src/rigplane/backends/yaesu_cat/parser.py",
    "src/rigplane/rigctld/routing.py",
]
# Per-mutant pytest invocation: -x -q -p no:cacheprovider. The selection
# is the focused per-module unit-test files, not every file that imports
# the mutated modules: the import closure (~84 files) makes popular
# functions inherit hundreds of slow integration tests and pushed
# per-mutant runs past a minute, while this list keeps the full
# baseline fifteen-module sweep near an estimated fifteen minutes (from a 590 s
# bounded window on the builder's Linux test host, not the CI runner;
# see docs/development/mutation-testing.md). Source-introspection tests
# (census/inventory scans such as tests/test_command_map_parity.py)
# cannot run inside the mutants copy at all and must stay out.
# mutmut runs only the tests its stats phase saw covering each mutated
# function, so per-mutant cost stays bounded by those tests.
pytest_add_cli_args = ["-x", "-q", "-p", "no:cacheprovider"]
pytest_add_cli_args_test_selection = [
    "tests/contracts/test_tx_observation_conformance.py",
    "tests/test_acquisition_drain.py",
    "tests/test_audio_codecs.py",
    "tests/test_civ_rx_coverage.py",
    "tests/test_combined_acquisition_drain.py",
    "tests/test_controller_authority.py",
    "tests/test_controller_sessions.py",
    "tests/test_delta_encoder.py",
    "tests/test_managed_tx_fence.py",
    "tests/test_managed_tx_state.py",
    "tests/test_pcm_ingress_decode.py",
    "tests/test_raw_civ_transaction.py",
    "tests/test_response_shape_from_profile.py",
    "tests/test_rigctl_ws_channel.py",
    "tests/test_rigctld_protocol.py",
    "tests/test_rigctld_routable_extension.py",
    "tests/test_single_rx_plain_routing.py",
    "tests/test_state_queries.py",
    "tests/test_state_store.py",
    "tests/test_tx_band_edge.py",
    "tests/test_tx_safety.py",
    "tests/test_tx_safety_diagnostics.py",
    "tests/test_wire_tuple_splitting.py",
    "tests/test_yaesu_cat_parser.py",
]

[project]
name = "luxury-lakehouse"
version = "0.5.124"
description = "Serverless soccer analytics platform built on Databricks Lakebase"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.10,<3.11"
license = { text = "Apache-2.0" }
dependencies = [
    # Core ingestion dependencies (must work on Databricks serverless Python 3.10)
    # NOTE: pandas and numpy are pre-installed on Databricks serverless runtime.
    # Do NOT pin them here — version conflicts break the Python kernel.
    "requests>=2.33.0",
    "requests-cache>=1.2.0",
    # Transitive dep (requests, httpx, anyio). Pinned to >=3.15 to resolve
    # CVE-2026-45409 (idna 3.11 vulnerability).
    "idna>=3.15",
    # Transitive dep (mlflow + fsspec[http] via huggingface-hub/datasets/torch). Pinned to
    # >=3.14.3 to resolve CVE-2026-34993 + CVE-2026-47265 (aiohttp < 3.14.0), the
    # CVE-2026-54273..54280 batch (aiohttp 3.14.0, fixed in 3.14.1), and
    # PYSEC-2026-3545 (fixed 3.14.3) + PYSEC-2026-3546 / PYSEC-2026-3547 (fixed 3.14.2)
    # in one bump — 3.14.3 is the lowest version clearing all three.
    "aiohttp>=3.14.3",
    # Transitive dep (httpx/starlette → anyio; pulled forward to 4.12.1 by the silly-kicks 4.120.0
    # re-lock via ruthless-efficiency 0.6.0). Floored to >=4.14.2 to resolve CVE-2026-63374 +
    # CVE-2026-64847 (anyio < 4.14.2). The lakehouse uses anyio only transitively (httpx async
    # transport); 4.14.2 is the lowest version clearing both.
    "anyio>=4.14.2",
    # Transitive dep (mlflow-skinny → fastapi). Floored to >=1.3.1 to resolve
    # CVE-2026-48818 + CVE-2026-48817 + CVE-2026-54283 + CVE-2026-54282 (starlette < 1.x
    # web-server vulnerabilities). fastapi (>=0.46.0, no ceiling) accepts the starlette 1.x
    # major; the lakehouse uses mlflow as a tracking client only (no server/gateway), so the
    # starlette web-server paths are never exercised. uv kept 0.52.1 only because the 1.x line
    # released after the last lock; the floor forces the upgrade.
    "starlette>=1.3.1",
    # Transitive dep (google-auth -> databricks-sdk -> mlflow-skinny; also directly).
    # Floored to >=50.0.0 to resolve GHSA-537c-gmf6-5ccf (cryptography < 48.0.1),
    # PYSEC-2026-3553 + PYSEC-2026-3554 (fixed 49.0.0), and PYSEC-2026-3552 (needs >=50.0.0).
    #
    # The >=50 floor became reachable only once full `mlflow` was dropped for
    # `mlflow-skinny` (see the [mlflow] extra + ADR-027, 2026-08-31 amendment): full
    # mlflow capped `cryptography<50` (3.15.x -> `cryptography>=43,<50`), which made
    # 49.0.0 the prior ceiling and left PYSEC-2026-3552 unresolvable (it was ignored
    # in .pip-audit-ignores.yml). mlflow-skinny carries no cryptography pin, so the
    # floor now resolves and that ignore is REMOVED — a genuine fix, not a suppression.
    "cryptography>=50.0.0",
    # Transitive dep (mlflow / databricks-sdk / distributed). Floored to >=1.2.1 to resolve
    # GHSA-6v7p-g79w-8964 (msgpack < 1.2.1).
    "msgpack>=1.2.1",
    # Transitive dep (dbt-core, flask/taipy, typer). Floored to >=8.3.3 to resolve
    # PYSEC-2026-2132 (click < 8.3.3). No parent caps click, so the floor is satisfiable.
    "click>=8.3.3",
    # Transitive dep (matplotlib / taipy). Floored to >=12.3.0 to resolve the PYSEC-2026-2253,
    # -2254, -2255, -2256, -2257 batch (pillow < 12.3.0) in one bump. No parent caps pillow.
    "pillow>=12.3.0",
    # Transitive dep (dbt-core). Floored to >=0.6.0 to resolve PYSEC-2026-3696 / -3697 / -3698 /
    # -3699 (sqlparse < 0.6.0 parsing vulnerabilities), all fixed in 0.6.0.
    "sqlparse>=0.6.0",
    # Workflow framework (card parsing + validation)
    "pydantic>=2.0",
    "PyYAML>=6.0",
    # HF Hub (cost tracking, dataset publishing, model weight sync)
    "huggingface_hub>=1.5.0",
    # Floored to >=3.1.51 to resolve GHSA-2f96-g7mh-g2hx / -v396-v7q4-x2qj /
    # -956x-8gvw-wg5v (gitpython < 3.1.51).
    "gitpython>=3.1.58",
    "pygments>=2.20.0",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
spadl = [
    "silly-kicks[ghost-gk,parse-dfl]>=4.133.0,<5",
]
analytics = [
    "luxury-lakehouse[spadl]",
    "pandas>=2.1.0",
    "numpy>=1.26.0",
    "mplsoccer>=1.1.3",
    "matplotlib>=3.8.0",
    "scipy>=1.11.0",
    "scikit-learn>=1.3.0",
    # xgboost-cpu: drop-in for xgboost (same `import xgboost`, same API) without
    # the 300 MB nvidia-nccl-cu12 GPU dep. Matches the Databricks analytics env
    # spec so CI exercises the same package prod installs. Serverless is CPU-only.
    "xgboost-cpu==3.2.0",
    "rapidfuzz>=3.14.5",
    "unidecode>=1.3.0",
    "sparse-dot-topn>=1.1.0",
    # PR-1.5 (SK3-MIG-B): Live Kimball contract tests require direct SQL
    # queries to dev_gold marts. The databricks-sql-connector provides the
    # `databricks.sql` module used by tests/data_quality/ live tests and the
    # tests/smoke_gates/sk3_mig_b/ smoke gates.
    "databricks-sql-connector>=4.0.0",
    # Transitive dep (databricks-sql-connector). Pinned to >=2.15.0 to resolve
    # PYSEC-2026-175/177/178/179 (pyjwt < 2.13.0) AND PYSEC-2026-4141 + CVE-2026-102275
    # (pyjwt < 2.15.0 JWT-verification vulnerabilities). No parent caps pyjwt.
    "pyjwt>=2.15.0",
]
dbt = [
    "dbt-core>=1.11.12",
    "dbt-databricks>=1.12.2",
]
sdk = [
    "databricks-sdk==0.121.0",
    # psycopg2 lives here so the grants automation (GitHub Actions
    # lakebase-grants.yml + scripts/run_lakebase_grants.py) can install a
    # minimal dependency set without pulling the full taipy-app extra.
    # Lakebase is a Databricks service — a PG client belongs with SDK

    "psycopg2-binary==2.9.12",
]
embeddings = [
    "gensim>=4.3.0",
]

]

    # verified with a live log/load round-trip.
    "mlflow-skinny>=2.19.0",
]
training = ["torch>=2.0", "pyarrow>=14.0", "datasets>=3.0", "safetensors>=0.4.0"]
evolve = ["openevolve>=0.3.2"]
taipy-app = [
    "taipy==4.1.1",
    "psycopg2-binary==2.9.12",
    "mplsoccer==1.8.0",
    "pandas==2.3.3",
    "numpy==1.26.4",
    "pydantic>=2.0",
    # Floored to >=2.14.2 to resolve GHSA-4xgf-cpjx-pc3j (pydantic-settings < 2.14.2).
    "pydantic-settings>=2.14.2",
    "requests>=2.33.0",
    "databricks-sdk==0.121.0",
    "huggingface-hub>=1.5.0",

# --- uv configuration ---
[tool.uv]
# Security floors on TRANSITIVE dependencies live here — NOT in
# [project.dependencies] — so the project's declared deps stay limited to what we
# actually import. constraint-dependencies apply a floor across the whole
# resolution without creating a phantom direct dependency. This is the canonical
# home for "vulnerable transitive package, fix version exists" (per the CVE-floor
# convention). Direct-dep CVEs are floored inline in [project.dependencies].
constraint-dependencies = [
    # CVE-2026-59885 + CVE-2026-59886 (pyasn1 < 0.6.4). Transitive via the
    # cryptography / pyOpenSSL / databricks-sdk auth chain — no direct import.
    "pyasn1>=0.6.4",
    # PYSEC-2026-2151 (flask < 3.1.3). The Space resolves flask 3.1.1 because taipy-rest 4.1.1
    # caps it at <=3.1.1; taipy-rest 4.1.0 does not, so this floor takes 4.1.0 instead. Measured
    # 2026-08-11 and re-verified 2026-08-12: 136 packages before and after, nothing added or
    # removed, and only taipy-rest + apispec + apispec-webframeworks move — none of which appear
    # anywhere in hf_taipy_app/ (they arrive solely as transitives of the taipy metapackage, and
    # the Space is a GUI app that never touches the REST layer).
    # This is the D5 carve-out: a backwards move accepted as the measured, named, bounded price
    # of a security fix.
    #
    # This constraint binds the DEPLOY-TIME compile, not uv.lock — the lock already resolves
    # flask 3.1.3 / taipy-rest 4.1.0. It therefore does NOT fix production on its own; only the
    # next deploy does (Task 5b).
    "flask>=3.1.3",
    # PYSEC-2026-3032 + PYSEC-2026-3033 (python-engineio < 4.13.2) and PYSEC-2026-3042
    # (python-socketio < 5.16.2). These two floors exist BECAUSE of the flask floor above.
    #
    # Measured 2026-08-12 against the deployed Space: flask>=3.1.3 forces taipy-rest 4.1.0, and
    # that older taipy-rest caps python-engineio at 4.13.1 and python-socketio at 5.16.1 — both
    # vulnerable. An UNCONSTRAINED compile takes 4.13.4 / 5.16.4, which are fixed. So taking the
    # flask fix alone would have *caused* three advisories to persist that a plain redeploy would
    # have cleared: 9 of 12 fixed instead of 12.
    #
    # All three floors resolve together: 136 packages, taipy-rest still 4.1.0, nothing added, and
    # only the typer chain (typer, shellingham, annotated-doc) drops — verified unimported by
    # hf_taipy_app (the only matches were incidental byte sequences inside .pyc files).
    #
    # The D5 change manifest did NOT catch this: it measures movement RELATIVE TO PRODUCTION, so a
    # package sitting still at a vulnerable version is invisible to it.
    "python-engineio>=4.13.2",
    "python-socketio>=5.16.2",
    # CVE-2026-104851 (fsspec < 2026.6.0): NOT floored here — `datasets` caps fsspec<=2025.3.0, and
    # the newer `datasets` that would lift the cap requires pyarrow>=21, which taipy-core caps at
    # <19 (ResolutionImpossible). Carried as a justified ignore in .pip-audit-ignores.yml (BLOCKED).
    # CVE-2026-104874 (multidict < 6.9.1). Transitive via aiohttp / yarl (the HF/http async stack).
    "multidict>=6.9.1",
    # PYSEC-2026-4114 (oauthlib < 4.0.0): NOT floored here — databricks-sql-connector hard-caps
    # oauthlib>=3.1.0,<4.0.0 across every available version, so the 4.0.0 floor is unsatisfiable
    # (ResolutionImpossible). Carried as a justified ignore in .pip-audit-ignores.yml (BLOCKED).
    # PYSEC-2026-4175 + PYSEC-2026-4176 + PYSEC-2026-4177 (urllib3 < 2.8.0). Transitive via
    # requests / the HTTP stack — no direct import.
    "urllib3>=2.8.0",
    # CVE-2026-102598 (werkzeug < 3.1.9). Transitive via flask (already floored >=3.1.3); flask 3.1.x
    # requires werkzeug>=3.1, so 3.1.9 is in-range.
    "werkzeug>=3.1.9",
    # PYSEC-2026-4011/-4012/-4013/-4014 (virtualenv < 21.7.13). DEV-only transitive via pre-commit;
    # 21.7.13 is the lowest version clearing all four.
    "virtualenv>=21.7.13",
]

# Taipy-GUI 4.1.2 caps flask-socketio <5.5, but Flask 3.1.3 (pinned by the
# PYSEC-2026-2151 floor above) made RequestContext.session a read-only property.
# flask-socketio <5.5.1 still assigns `ctx.session = ...` directly, raising
# `AttributeError: can't set attribute 'session'` on EVERY Socket.IO connect —
# Taipy delivers page content over that websocket, so the app rendered blank in
# production from the 2026-08-12 D5 CVE deploy (which introduced the flask>=3.1.3
# floor) until this override. Fixed upstream in flask-socketio 5.5.1 (the
# `_session` compatibility branch). Taipy-GUI 4.1.2 uses only stable SocketIO APIs
# (SocketIO(), .on, .run, .async_mode, .wsgi_server), so its <5.5 cap is
# conservative and safe to lift here. Keeping flask>=3.1.3 preserves the CVE fix.
# Verified: 5.4.1 reproduces the exact prod traceback, 5.6.1 connects cleanly.
# See ADR-083. Requires hf_taipy_app/Dockerfile to install with --no-deps
# (plain `pip install -r` fails ResolutionImpossible against taipy-gui's cap).
override-dependencies = [
    "flask-socketio>=5.5.1",
]

# taipy requires sqlalchemy>=2.0; dbt-databricks requires sqlalchemy<2.0.
# These extras are separate deployment targets that never coexist in a single env.
conflicts = [
    [
        { extra = "taipy-app" },
        { extra = "dbt" },
    ],

    # Temporary suppression — remove when #1035 lands (module deletion)
    # Message pattern is matched via re.match (prefix, not full-string): match on the

[tool.coverage.report]

[tool.pyright]
pythonVersion = "3.12"
typeCheckingMode = "strict"
include = ["src", "tests", "tools", "packages/roxabi-nats/src", "packages/roxabi-contracts/src", "packages/roxabi-blobs/src", "packages/roxabi-obs/src", "packages/roxabi-satellite/src"]
venvPath = "."
venv = ".venv"
# ── Permanent policy ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# reportPrivateUsage: Python's _name is a convention (advisory), not access
# control. Pyright enforcing it generates false positives on tightly-coupled
# partner modules, stdlib internals, and white-box test access — none of which
# represent real violations. Enforced by code review, not by the type checker.
reportPrivateUsage = "none"
#
# reportUnusedFunction: Decorator-registered callables (Discord app_commands,
# Telegram update handlers, asyncio task targets) are not statically reachable.
# Confirmed by manual audit 2026-03-23: all 48 src hits are dynamic registrations
# or private module helpers called through the module's public entry point.
reportUnusedFunction = "none"
# ── Wave 4 (#411) — config loading migrated to Pydantic ──────────────────────
# Rules still suppressed: cascading errors from non-config dict[str, Any] in
# business logic, LLM drivers, and tests (~3,165 hits total). Config sites
# are now fully typed. Re-enable incrementally in follow-up issues.
reportUnknownVariableType = "none"
reportUnknownMemberType = "none"
reportUnknownArgumentType = "none"
reportUnknownParameterType = "none"
reportMissingParameterType = "none"
reportUnknownLambdaType = "none"
reportMissingTypeArgument = "none"

[tool.ruff]
src = ["src", "tests", "packages/roxabi-nats/src", "packages/roxabi-nats/tests", "packages/roxabi-contracts/src", "packages/roxabi-contracts/tests", "packages/roxabi-blobs/src", "packages/roxabi-blobs/tests", "packages/roxabi-satellite/src", "packages/roxabi-satellite/tests"]
exclude = [".claude/worktrees", "deploy"]
# Vendored gate scripts, copied from roxabi-plugins/plugins/dev-core/tools.
# tools/ also holds host-owned gates, so the directory stays in scope — only
# these four filenames are excluded. Formatting them rewrites upstream bytes
# (or, for license_check.py, the declared local variant) and recreates the
# drift ssot-verify V18 reports.
extend-exclude = [
    "tools/check_file_length.sh",
    "tools/check_folder_size.sh",
    "tools/check_lib.sh",
    "tools/license_check.py",
]
# Explicit paths bypass exclude unless force-exclude is set; ruff check/format
# on a staged or named file is inert without this.
force-exclude = true

[build-system]

[project]
name = "pipeplan"
version = "1.0.0"
description = "A declarative, configuration-driven batch ETL framework on pandas."
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
license = { text = "MIT" }
authors = [{ name = "PipePlan" }]
keywords = ["etl", "pandas", "pipeline", "declarative", "data-engineering"]
classifiers = [
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "Topic :: Database",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries",
    # The package ships `py.typed`; without this a consumer has no way to know
    # the annotations are there before installing it.
    "Typing :: Typed",
]
# The three below carry an upper bound; the rest do not. The rule is not
# "cap everything" -- a cap the maintainer forgets to lift is how a package
# becomes unresolvable in someone else's environment. It is "cap what this
# framework is built *on top of*", where a major release is a redesign rather
# than a deprecation cycle: pandas owns the data model, pydantic owns every
# schema, SQLAlchemy owns the whole relational family. A major of any of the
# three is a version of PipePlan, not a free upgrade.
#
# The floor is proved by CI (the `floor` job resolves every minimum). Nothing
# proved the *ceiling* until the matrix grew a column that tracks the newest
# interpreter and therefore the newest pandas -- which is what a cap is for:
# to say where the tested range stops, rather than to guess where it breaks.
dependencies = [
    "pandas>=2.0,<4",
    "pydantic>=2.5,<3",
    "sqlalchemy>=2.0,<3",
    # 2.8.2, not 2.8: pandas 2.0 -- our own floor -- already requires it, so the
    # lower bound was never actually installable and nobody could have noticed
    # until the floor was pinned in CI. Nothing new is asked of any user.
    "python-dateutil>=2.8.2",
    "requests>=2.28",
    "pyyaml>=6.0",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
# Excel/parquet file support.
files = ["openpyxl>=3.1", "pyarrow>=14.0"]
# Database drivers. Access additionally needs the OS-level ODBC driver.
postgres = ["psycopg2-binary>=2.9"]
access = ["pyodbc>=5.0", "sqlalchemy-access>=2.0"]
mysql = ["pymysql>=1.1"]
# MongoDB / DocumentDB resources.
mongo = ["pymongo>=4.6"]
# REST/HTTP API resources.
rest = ["requests>=2.28"]
# High-performance fuzzy matching (falls back to stdlib difflib without it).
fuzzy = ["rapidfuzz>=3.0"]
# Ship run events as OpenTelemetry spans and metrics. The API only: an
# exporter and its configuration belong to the deployment, not to us.
otel = ["opentelemetry-api>=1.20"]

# schedule one, so these are the glue every deployment would otherwise write by

dagster = ["dagster>=1.6"]
prefect = ["prefect>=2.16"]

    "pymongo>=4.6",

    # docstring of `pipeplan.adapters.mongo`.
    "mongomock>=4.1",
    "pytest>=7.0",
    "pytest-cov>=5.0",
    "import-linter>=2.0",
    "mypy>=1.10",
    "ruff>=0.5",

]

    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",

]
dependencies = [
    "telethon>=1.43.2",
    "telethon-floodgate>=0.1.2,<0.2",
    "telethon-cli>=0.1.1",
    # Telethon's SOCKS/HTTP proxy path (TG_PROXY) needs python-socks with the
    # asyncio extra; without it Telethon silently ignores `proxy=` (warns only).
    "python-socks[asyncio]>=2.0",
    # Live dialog history reads (`dialogs read` / GET /dialogs/history, #1234
    # follow-up) reuse tg_messenger's StandaloneTelegramClient.history() for its
    # model mapping and flood-wait retry — see tg_agent/telegram/dm_history.py for why
    # it never opens a second connection. Note its per-instance history TTL cache
    # does NOT apply here: we build a throwaway client per call, so every read
    # hits Telegram. Caching happens one level up, in runtime_snapshots.
    "tg-messenger>=0.1.0",
    "fastapi>=0.136.3,<0.144",
    "uvicorn[standard]>=0.48.0",
    "jinja2>=3.1.6",
    "aiosqlite>=0.22.1",
    "apscheduler>=3.11.3",
    "pydantic>=2.13.4",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.14.1",
    "pyyaml>=6.0.3",
    "python-dotenv>=1.2.2",
    "python-multipart>=0.0.29",
    # CLI framework (epic #959, argparse→Typer migration). Typer was already in
    # the tree transitively; pinning it directly makes the dependency explicit
    # for the Wave-0 scaffold (tg_agent/cli/typer_app.py). 0.12 is the first release
    # with the modern click 8.x API the scaffold relies on.
    "typer>=0.12.0",
    "cryptography>=48.0.0",
    "openpyxl>=3.1.5",
    "aiohttp>=3.13.5",
    "numpy>=2.4.6",
    "scikit-learn>=1.8.0",
    "jieba>=0.42.1",
    "langdetect>=1.0.9",
    "textual[syntax]>=8.2.8",
    "claude-agent-sdk>=0.2.87",
    "deepagents>=0.6.4",
    "huggingface_hub>=1.16.4",
    # Image-generation SDKs (issue #958): the OpenAI/Together/Replicate image
    # adapters use these instead of raw aiohttp. ``openai`` was already in the
    # tree transitively via ``langchain-openai``; pinning it directly makes the
    # dependency explicit. Together's images endpoint is OpenAI-compatible, so it
    # reuses the ``openai`` SDK with a custom ``base_url`` (no heavy ``together``
    # SDK). ``replicate`` is lightweight (httpx + pydantic, both already present)
    # and removes the hand-rolled prediction-polling loop. HuggingFace stays on
    # raw aiohttp on purpose — its SDK returns a PIL.Image (a Pillow dependency)
    # whereas the raw path saves the image/* bytes directly.
    # openai 3.x adopted (the deliberate revisit the #1300 cap promised): 3.x
    # replaced the default httpx transport with the httpx2 package, so every
    # httpx.Client/AsyncClient monkeypatch in the test suite silently misses —
    # tests stop mocking the real request and hit the live provider. The
    # interception tests now patch BOTH httpx and httpx2 (guarded import), so
    # 2.x and 3.x stay sealed.
    "openai>=3.19.2,<4",
    "replicate>=1.0.7",
    "langchain>=1.3.2",
    "langchain-core>=1.4.0",
    "langchain-ollama>=1.1.0",

    # `timeout=` aborts catastrophic backtracking inside its C matching loop,
    # which the stdlib `re` cannot (#1240). Present transitively (dateparser,
    # tiktoken) but declared here because it is now a direct runtime import.
    "regex>=2024.11.6",

# Static security analysis config for `bandit -c pyproject.toml -r tg_agent` (#1053).
# The CI step (static-checks) runs it advisory (continue-on-error) for now; this
# scopes the scan to tg_agent/ and skips the test tree. Findings are triaged into a
# skip-list / `# nosec` here before the step is ever made blocking.
[tool.bandit]
exclude_dirs = ["tests"]

# Dead-code scan whitelist (vulture, #1136). vulture auto-reads this section,
# so it applies both to `python -m vulture tg_agent/` and to scripts/code_health.py.
# Every name here is a VERIFIED false-positive — do not delete the code it
# refers to; each entry must say why it is intentionally "unused".
[tool.vulture]
ignore_names = [
    # tg_agent/utils/json.py safe_json_dumps(ensure_ascii=...): intentional
    # call-site-compatibility parameter after the orjson migration (#956) —
    # orjson is always UTF-8, the flag is accepted so existing
    # `safe_json_dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=True)` calls don't break, but has
    # no effect. Removing it would break call sites. See issue #1136.
    "ensure_ascii",
]

# Doc-coverage (interrogate, #1072). scripts/doc_coverage.py and the advisory
# CI step read this. `fail_under` is a SOFT baseline — a ratchet floor that
# surfaces regressions without forcing a docstring-everything sprint. Raise it
# as coverage climbs. interrogate ignores things that don't need a docstring
# (magic/init/nested/private, overloads).
# Ratchet history: 23 (#1072 floor) → 35 (#1134: documented the public-API
# facade — tg_agent/models.py Pydantic models, db.repos bundles, repository CRUD —
# lifting coverage 27% → 40.6%; floor set to 35 to lock in the win with a
# margin below the measured 40.6% so a stray docstring loss doesn't trip the
# gate). Doc-coverage is NOT a CI gate (#1097) — stays a local script.
[tool.interrogate]
fail_under = 35
ignore_init_method = true
ignore_init_module = true
ignore_magic = true
ignore_nested_functions = true
ignore_private = true
ignore_semiprivate = true
ignore_property_decorators = true
ignore_overloaded_functions = true
exclude = ["tests", "scripts", "build", "dist", "site", "mutants"]
verbose = 1

# Mutation testing (mutmut 3.8). Root-caused 07.10.26: stock mutmut is
# incompatible with a FLAT layout whose import package is literally named
# `src` (as this repo's was before the #1448 rename to tg_agent) — it strips a
# `src.` prefix from module names (breaking the trampoline routing and stats
# keys) and asserts against `src.`-prefixed trampoline hits. With the rename
# stock mutmut works again; the strip_src_prefix knob stays until the upstream
# PR (boxed/mutmut, branch fix/strip-src-prefix-knob) lands on PyPI — the fork
# is installed editable from its local checkout. The sandbox ships
# everything tests read outside tg_agent/tests, both at collection time (root
# conftest.py, scripts/) and at run time (.github/workflows/ci.yml,
# docs/reference/*, adk/). data/ is deliberately NOT copied — it holds the
# live DB; sandbox tests run on tmp/in-memory databases. mutmut never prunes
# a stale sandbox (deleted files keep their old copies) — `rm -rf mutants`
# before a rerun.
[tool.mutmut]
source_paths = ["tg_agent"]
also_copy = [
    "conftest.py",
    "scripts",
    ".github/workflows",
    "docs/reference",
    "adk",
    "mkdocs.yml",
    "config.yaml",
    "docker-compose.yml",
]
strip_src_prefix = false
# The fork-isolated serial stats phase pushes the whole suite (~10.7k tests,
# collect-verified 08.10.26) serially through one process; full sandbox runs
# have not completed yet, so the observations are from partial runs: leaky
# leftovers from earlier tests (unclosed sqlite connections, destroyed-pending
# asyncio tasks) get finalized mid-run, and pytest's unraisable AND
# threadexception plugins attribute each to whichever test happens to run
# (seen at 1713 and 3673 green tests respectively) — both plugins are
# disabled for mutation runs; the normal suite still enforces strictness in
# CI. Known cost: a mutant whose only observable effect is a
# broken cleanup path (unclosed connection, uncancelled task) now survives
# silently — the score overstates resource-lifecycle code; such survivors
# need a manual look.
pytest_add_cli_args = [
    "-p", "no:unraisableexception",
    "-p", "no:threadexception",
    "-m", "not mutmut_skip",
]

[project]
name = "prosperity"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Application de gestion des finances personnelles auto-hébergée pour un foyer."
requires-python = ">=3.13,<3.14"
dependencies = [
    "alembic>=1.18.4",
    "asyncpg>=0.31.0",
    "email-validator>=2.2",
    "fastapi>=0.118",
    "ofxparse>=0.21",
    "pwdlib[argon2]>=0.2.1",
    "pydantic>=2.13.4",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.14.2",
    "pyjwt[crypto]>=2.10",
    "python-multipart>=0.0.9",
    "sqlalchemy[asyncio]>=2.0.49",
    "uvicorn[standard]>=0.38",
]

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "pytest>=8.3",
    "httpx>=0.28",
    "pytest-asyncio>=1.3.0",
    "hypothesis>=6.152.9",
    "testcontainers[postgres]>=4.14.2",
    "psycopg2-binary>=2.9.10",
    "factory-boy>=3.3.3",
    "pyyaml>=6.0",
    "coverage>=7.14.0",
    "pytest-cov>=7.1.0",
    "pyright>=1.1.405",
    "ruff>=0.14.0",
    "pre-commit>=4.0",
    "import-linter>=2.3",
    "pytest-xdist>=3.8.0",
    "deptry>=0.25.1",
]

# `deptry` : cohérence des dépendances Python déclarées/importées (S-quality-gate-1/S07).
# `exclude` reprend l'exclusion par défaut de `tests/` (plus `client`, `htmlcov` et les
# caches) — volontairement, pour que DEP004 (une dépendance du groupe `dev` importée
# depuis `backend/` ou `alembic/`) reste détectée ; la contrepartie est qu'une dépendance
# `[project.dependencies]` consommée uniquement depuis `tests/` doit être ignorée en
# DEP002 avec motif (cas `email-validator`).
# `[dependency-groups].dev` (PEP 735) est déjà reconnu nativement comme groupe dev
# par deptry — aucune option supplémentaire n'est nécessaire pour ça.
[tool.deptry]
known_first_party = ["backend"]
# `exclude` REMPLACE la liste par défaut de deptry (qui contient `.git`) : sans `\.git` ici,
# un worktree du cycle (`.git/scd-worktrees/<ticket>/`) est scanné et fait rougir la gate.
exclude = ["\\.git", ".venv", "client", "htmlcov", "tests", "\\.hypothesis", "\\.pytest_cache", "\\.ruff_cache", "\\.mypy_cache", "__pycache__"]

[tool.deptry.per_rule_ignores]
# DEP002 (déclarée mais jamais importée par son nom) : chargées à l'exécution par un
# mécanisme indirect, jamais par un `import` explicite dans backend/alembic/tests.
# - asyncpg : driver SQLAlchemy async résolu depuis l'URL de connexion (`postgresql+asyncpg://`).
# - python-multipart : parsing multipart/form-data fait par Starlette en interne (FastAPI File/Form).
# - uvicorn : serveur ASGI lancé en CLI/entrypoint, jamais importé en Python.
# - email-validator : chargé à l'exécution par pydantic.EmailStr (backend/modules/auth/schemas.py),
#   jamais importé par son nom hors tests/ (exclu du scan).
DEP002 = ["asyncpg", "python-multipart", "uvicorn", "email-validator"]

[tool.uv]
package = false

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
pythonpath = ["."]
testpaths = ["tests"]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
# Session-scoped loop so async tests share the same loop as the session-scoped
# testcontainers/db_engine/db_session fixtures (tests/integration/conftest.py).
# Without this, tests on the default function loop get "attached to a different
# loop" errors from asyncpg resources created on the fixture's session loop.
asyncio_default_test_loop_scope = "session"
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "session"
markers = [
    "e2e: black-box HTTP user-journey tests (committed_client + real Postgres)",
]

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["backend"]
branch = true
# SQLAlchemy's async stack and FastAPI's threaded sync routes both
# require explicit concurrency tracking — without these, route bodies
# and async-backed DB calls report uncovered even when fully exercised
# in tests (the bodies execute in worker threads/greenlets that
# coverage's default tracer doesn't see).
concurrency = ["greenlet", "thread"]

[tool.coverage.report]
show_missing = true
skip_covered = false
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
]

[tool.coverage.html]
directory = "htmlcov"

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py313"
extend-exclude = [".venv", "htmlcov", ".hypothesis", ".pytest_cache", "client"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
# C90 (mccabe, max-complexity=10) : complexité cyclomatique. SIM/RET : idiomes de simplification
# et de retour anticipé. PERF : pièges de performance connus (boucles, comprehensions). PT :
# idiomes pytest (fixtures, raises, paramétrage). W : warnings pycodestyle. PLR déjà couvert par PL.
select = ["E", "F", "I", "UP", "B", "PL", "C90", "SIM", "RET", "PERF", "PT", "W"]
# PGH004 : pas de `# noqa` nu ; RUF100 : pas de `# noqa` mort. Le filet escape-hatches vit ici,
# pas dans un grep CI (cf. runbooks/ci.md § Escape-hatches).
extend-select = ["PGH004", "RUF100"]

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 10

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["backend"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**" = [
    "PLR2004", # 770 remontées : nombres magiques légitimes en test (codes HTTP, effectifs d'échantillon)
    "PT018",   # 53 remontées : assertions composites du patron arrange/act/assert (vérifs liées regroupées)
    "PT019",   # 16 remontées : fixtures `_`-préfixées injectées pour leur effet de bord (setup/teardown), jamais lues
]

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
indent-style = "space"

# Type checker: pyright (cf. P01.3.1) — faster than mypy and better Pydantic v2 support.
# Strict on backend/ (production surface); standard on tests/ where third-party
# libs without stubs (testcontainers, factory_boy) would otherwise drown signal.
[tool.pyright]
include = ["backend", "tests"]
exclude = ["**/__pycache__", ".venv", "htmlcov", ".hypothesis", ".pytest_cache"]
pythonVersion = "3.13"
pythonPlatform = "Linux"
typeCheckingMode = "strict"
extraPaths = ["."]
reportMissingImports = "error"
reportMissingTypeStubs = "warning"
useLibraryCodeForTypes = true
venvPath = "."
venv = ".venv"

[[tool.pyright.executionEnvironments]]
root = "tests"
reportMissingTypeStubs = "none"
reportUnknownMemberType = "none"
reportUnknownArgumentType = "none"
reportUnknownVariableType = "none"
reportUnknownParameterType = "none"
reportMissingParameterType = "none"

    # P1 (ADR-222): ship the governance constitution single-source-of-truth so
    # `graq init` renders the full rulebook into CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/etc. Without
    # this the .md fragments are stripped from the wheel and init silently falls
    # back to the abridged inline copy. Owner-approved (harish, 2026-06-07).
    # V-CR-GOV-INSTALL-P1-NATIVE-001: graq_edit G4 + graq_config_audit could not
    # resolve the worktree path (S-010 class); native edit with recorded approval.
    "graqle/data/constitution/*.md",
    # ed25519 cutover (ADR-215 §5): the Community trust source — PUBLIC licence
    # signing keys so offline installs can verify v2 licences. Public-key-only
    # (the private signer is server-side; keygen.py is excluded below).
    "graqle/licensing/trusted_keys.json",
    # CR-010.R1: the frozen proof spec + its conformance corpus. These MUST ship
    # in the wheel — the whole point is that a third party can implement a
    # conformant verifier from the published schemas + golden vectors alone.
    # Loaded via importlib.resources (never __file__), so they resolve from a
    # zip-imported wheel. Spec version is decoupled from the SDK version.
    "graqle/pct/schema/proof-spec/**/*.json",
    "graqle/pct/schema/proof-spec/**/*.md",
    "graqle/pct/schema/conformance/*.json",
    "graqle/pct/schema/conformance/fixtures/*",
    # CR-010.R3: compliance packs are DATA — a framework is a pack.yaml plus a
    # schema.json, so adding NIST AI RMF / ISO 42001 needs no Python. These MUST
    # ship in the wheel or the packs silently vanish from an installed SDK and
    # only first-party imports keep working. Loaded via importlib.resources
    # (never Path(__file__).parents[N], which resolves elsewhere once installed).
    "graqle/compliance/packs/**/*.yaml",
    "graqle/compliance/packs/**/*.json",
]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["graqle"]
exclude = [
    "graqle/benchmarks/data/*",
    # B3/S2: shapes.ttl excluded from wheel — structural SHACL logic is
    # readable even with opaque URNs; keep it server-side only until ADR-206
    # documents accepted disclosure posture before public PyPI.
    "graqle/governance/shacl/shapes.ttl",
    # WS-C C1 (ADR-BIZ-001): the Community (Apache-2.0) wheel ships WITHOUT the
    # proprietary commercial backends. These live in the source tree but are
    # carved out of the public wheel; the proprietary graqle-studio /
    # graqle-enterprise distributions re-include them. The thin cli/commands/*
    # wrappers ship and degrade gracefully (graqle/cli/_edition_guard.py) when a
    # backend is absent. An import-direction CI gate enforces that no Community
    # module eagerly imports these (lazy-only invariant). scorch + phantom are
    # NON-CORE plugins and intentionally REMAIN in Community (Harish, 2026-06-01).
    "graqle/cloud/*",
    "graqle/leads/*",
    "graqle/studio/*",
    "graqle/server/*",
    # WS-D D-pkg (ADR-BIZ-001): the admin licence SIGNER must not ship in the
    # public Community wheel. keygen.py embeds the legacy HMAC signing secret
    # (its own docstring: "never distribute to end users"); generate_key signs
    # licences. With ed25519 (WS-D) the wheel verifies with a PUBLIC key only and
    # cannot forge, but excluding the signer is belt-and-suspenders — the public
    # artifact carries verification, never issuance.
    "graqle/licensing/keygen.py",
    # WS-F (ADR-BIZ-001): trade-secret calibration internals — TS-1..TS-4
    # implementation details (weights, AGREEMENT_THRESHOLD, J̄ formula, θ_fold
    # derivation, STG production rules). The Community wheel ships the public
    # interface (output scores, status enums) but never the computation internals.
    # The trade-secret wheel gate (scripts/ci/trade_secret_wheel_gate.py) enforces
    # this mechanically on every PR and release build.
    "graqle/governance/calibration.py",
    "graqle/governance/calibration_store.py",
]

[tool.uv]
# Relative `exclude-newer` durations (below) are only understood by uv >= 0.9.17.
# WARNING: this `required-version` guard does NOT protect older uv here. An old
# uv can't parse `exclude-newer = "7 days"`, so it warns and discards the WHOLE
# `[tool.uv]` table - required-version included - then resolves without the
# cooldown and silently rewrites uv.lock (exit 0). The guard only fires when the
# table parses, i.e. on uv that's already new enough. The real guarantee that a
# new-enough uv is present comes from the SessionStart hook
# (.claude/hooks/session-start.sh), which upgrades uv before any sync.
required-version = ">=0.9.17"
# 7-day quarantine on freshly-published packages (supply-chain defense).
exclude-newer = "7 days"

[tool.poetry]
name = "netie"
version = "2.5.0"
description = "Cortex governed agentic engine — answer plane + optional agentic/RAG extras"
authors = ["Open Source"]
packages = [
    { include = "netie" },
    { include = "CortexOS" },
    { include = "packs" },
    { include = "cortex_contract", from = "packages" }
]

# pip resolves [project].dependencies. Do not reintroduce a caret table here —
# it silently capped cryptography at <43 and pillow at <11. See
# tests/packaging/test_dependency_floors.py.

[tool.poetry.extras]
agentic = ["dbos"]
rag = ["sentence-transformers", "qdrant-client", "tantivy"]
full = ["dbos", "sentence-transformers", "qdrant-client", "tantivy"]
dev = ["pytest", "pytest-asyncio", "respx", "ruff", "mypy", "import-linter", "types-PyYAML"]
local-inference = ["llama-cpp-python"]
gpu = ["torch", "llama-cpp-python"]
a2a = ["websockets"]
personality = []
postgres = ["sqlalchemy", "asyncpg", "psycopg"]
agents = ["dbos"]
tokens = ["tiktoken"]
api = []
dms = []

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py310"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "UP", "B"]
ignore = ["E501", "B008"]

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.11"
ignore_missing_imports = true
warn_unused_ignores = true
check_untyped_defs = false
pretty = true
# The contract package is distributed as top-level `cortex_contract`. Without
# this, mypy resolves packages/cortex_contract/*.py as both `cortex_contract.*`
# (the __init__.py walk-up) and `packages.cortex_contract.*` (as a namespace
# package from the root) and refuses to run at all.
mypy_path = "packages"
namespace_packages = false
# A setuptools build/ tree under the package is a *copy* of it, so mypy sees two
# modules named cortex_contract and stops with "errors prevented further
# checking" — exit 2, nothing type-checked, and it reads like an environment
# glitch rather than a disabled gate. Any `pip install -e .` or `python -m
# build` recreates it, so excluding it is the fix; deleting it is not.
exclude = '(^|/)build/'
# Packaging / release infra only — engine modules remain gradually typed.
files = [
    "CortexOS/packaging.py",
    "packages/cortex_contract",
    "scripts/check_versions.py",
    "scripts/export_openapi.py",
    "scripts/export_semantics.py",
]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
pythonpath = ["."]
markers = [
    "corpus_expanded: full paraphrase expansion (slow; set CORPUS_EXPANDED=1)",
]

layeredArchitecture().consideringAllDependencies()

      .layer("Controllers").definedBy("feedback.workshop.application.infrastructure.web.controller..")
      .layer("Services").definedBy("feedback.workshop.application.domain.service..")
      .layer("UseCases").definedBy("feedback.workshop.application.usecase..")
      .layer("Repository").definedBy("feedback.workshop.application.domain.repository..")

      .whereLayer("Controllers").mayNotBeAccessedByAnyLayer()
      .whereLayer("Services").mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Controllers", "UseCases")
      .whereLayer("Repository").mayOnlyBeAccessedByLayers("Services", "UseCases");

classes()
      .that().resideInAPackage("..service..")
      .and().areAnnotatedWith(Service.class)
      .should().haveSimpleNameEndingWith("Service");

[project]
name = "bernstein"
version = "3.22.0"
description = "The open-source governance layer for AI agents. No model in the coordination loop, so replaying a plan reproduces its task graph byte-identically, and run receipts are byte-identical across independent builds. Signed lineage plus an opt-in HMAC audit chain a reviewer checks offline, without rerunning it. Runs Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, and 40+ CLI agents; governs any deliverable from code to research to audit evidence packs. Cluster mode, air-gap deploy."
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
license = "Apache-2.0"
authors = [{ name = "Alex Chernysh", email = "alex@alexchernysh.com" }]
keywords = [
    "ai",
    "agents",
    "orchestration",
    "multi-agent",
    "coding",
    "cli",
    "llm",
    "automation",
    "devtools",
    "deterministic",
    "replay",
    "audit",
    "provenance",
    "lineage",
    "worktree",
]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 4 - Beta",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "Intended Audience :: System Administrators",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: Apache Software License",
    "Operating System :: OS Independent",
    "Operating System :: POSIX :: Linux",
    "Operating System :: MacOS",
    "Operating System :: Microsoft :: Windows",
    "Programming Language :: Python",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3 :: Only",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14",
    "Topic :: Software Development",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Build Tools",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Code Generators",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Quality Assurance",
    "Topic :: System :: Distributed Computing",
    "Typing :: Typed",
]
dependencies = [
    # No ceiling: the route-table walk that the agent task-scope gate compiles
    # its matchers from lives in ``core/routes/route_table.py`` and descends
    # through the ``include_router`` wrappers FastAPI keeps from 0.137 onward,
    # so it resolves the same templates on both sides of that change.
    # ``tests/unit/test_route_table.py`` holds the floor.
    "fastapi>=0.115",
    # Direct floor for the Starlette ASGI layer so the resolved lockfile stays
    # above PYSEC-2026-161 even when pulled through FastAPI or MCP.
    "starlette>=1.0.1",
    "uvicorn>=0.30",
    "httpx>=0.27",
    "cryptography>=50.0.0",
    "pyyaml>=6.0",
    "rich>=13.0",
    "textual>=1.0",
    "click>=8.3.3",
    "openai>=2.36.0",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.13.1",
    "python-dotenv>=1.2.2",
    "setproctitle>=1.3",
    "prometheus-client>=0.21",
    "pluggy>=1.5",
    "mcp>=1.30.0,<2",
    "watchdog>=4.0",
    "opentelemetry-api>=1.41.1",
    "opentelemetry-sdk>=1.41.1",
    "opentelemetry-exporter-otlp>=1.41.1",
    "pillow>=12.3.0",
    "pyfiglet>=1.0",
    "terminaltexteffects>=0.11",
    "websockets>=14.0",
    # SAML XML signature verification. Pure-Python via lxml+cryptography.
    # Required to validate IdP assertions in src/bernstein/core/security/auth.py;
    # enabling SAML without this library installed is a hard error.
    "signxml>=4.0",
    # Hardened XML parser. Used in src/bernstein/core/security/auth.py to
    # parse SAML assertions without expanding internal entities. Mitigates
    # billion-laughs / quadratic-blowup DoS on unauthenticated IdP responses.
    # defusedxml.ElementTree is a drop-in for xml.etree.ElementTree.
    "defusedxml>=0.7.1",
    # OS-keychain transport for the credential vault (release 1.9). Pulls in
    # macOS Keychain / Linux Secret Service / Windows Credential Manager
    # backends. AES-GCM file fallback uses the existing ``cryptography`` dep.
    "keyring>=25.0",
    # Strict per-phase artefact validation in
    # ``src/bernstein/core/orchestration/phase_schemas.py``.  Already pulled in
    # transitively by several deps; promoted to a direct dep so the phase
    # pipeline does not silently degrade if a transitive owner drops it.
    "jsonschema>=4.20",
    # RFC 3161 TimeStampToken ASN.1 parsing for the multi-tenant audit
    # export verifier. Pure-Python, MIT-licensed, ~250KB wheel; ships the
    # ``tsp.TSTInfo`` / ``cms.ContentInfo`` types we need without us
    # hand-rolling a DER parser. Used exclusively by
    # ``bernstein.core.security.rfc3161_verifier``.
    "asn1crypto>=1.5",
    # Canonical CBOR encoding for the COSE_Sign1 (RFC 9052) audit receipt.
    # MIT-licensed; deterministic-encoding mode gives byte-identical receipt
    # replay. Used by ``bernstein.core.security.audit_receipt`` and the
    # standalone ``tools/verify_audit_receipt.py`` verifier.
    "cbor2>=5.6",
    # Pure-Python PDF generation for the EU AI Act Article 12 evidence pack
    # rendered by `bernstein compliance pack`. MIT-licensed, no native deps.
    # Used exclusively by ``bernstein.core.compliance.article12``.
    "reportlab>=5,<6",
    # YAML frontmatter parsing for `bernstein ticket validate` (SDD ticket
    # schema). Lightweight, MIT-licensed; piggybacks on the already-pinned
    # PyYAML for the YAML body. The validator gracefully falls back to a
    # PyYAML-only parser so the dep is not strictly required at runtime,
    # but pinning it here keeps downstream behaviour consistent.
    "python-frontmatter>=1.1",
    # Pulled in transitively by httpx / anyio. Pin directly to >=3.15 so we
    # stay above the CVE-2026-45409 floor regardless of which transitive
    # owner resolves first; pip-audit gates the production closure on this.
    "idna>=3.15",
    # PEP 440 version parsing/comparison. Imported directly at runtime by the
    # ``bernstein doctor`` last-green advisory (``cli/commands/doctor_cmd.py``)
    # and the adapter security-floor / advisory gates
    # (``adapters/security_floor.py``, ``adapters/advisories.py``). Only ever
    # pulled into the lockfile transitively by dev/test tooling (pytest,
    # pip-audit, e2b, ...), so a clean ``uv tool install`` shipped without it
    # and ``bernstein doctor`` crashed with ModuleNotFoundError. Promoted to a
    # direct dependency so the resolver always installs it. Pure-Python.
    "packaging>=24",
    "tzdata>=2024.1",
]

gcs = ["google-cloud-storage>=3.10.1"]
azure = ["azure-storage-blob>=12.20"]
r2 = ["boto3>=1.43.6"]
# Chat-control bridge backends. Enable with:
#   pip install 'bernstein[telegram]'
# Standard Telegram bot integration via long-poll: configure the bot
# token (from @BotFather) and the chat id, no external services.
telegram = ["python-telegram-bot>=22.7"]
# Slack bidirectional driver over Socket Mode. Enable with:
#   pip install 'bernstein[slack]'
# Configure a Slack app with bot scopes (``chat:write``, ``commands``),
# enable Socket Mode, and set ``BERNSTEIN_SLACK_TOKEN`` (xoxb-...) plus
# ``BERNSTEIN_SLACK_APP_TOKEN`` (xapp-...) before invoking ``bernstein
# chat serve --platform=slack``.
slack = ["slack-sdk>=3.27", "aiohttp>=3.9"]
# Discord bidirectional driver over the gateway. Enable with:
#   pip install 'bernstein[discord]'
# Configure a Discord bot application in the developer portal, copy the
# bot token, and set ``BERNSTEIN_DISCORD_TOKEN`` before invoking
# ``bernstein chat serve --platform=discord``.
discord = ["discord.py>=2.4"]
# Microsoft Teams bidirectional driver over the Bot Framework. Enable with:
#   pip install 'bernstein[teams]'
# Register a bot in the Azure Bot Service, copy the app id and password, and
# set ``BERNSTEIN_TEAMS_TOKEN`` (app id) plus ``BERNSTEIN_TEAMS_APP_PASSWORD``
# (client secret) before invoking ``bernstein chat serve --platform=teams``.
teams = ["botbuilder-core>=4.15", "aiohttp>=3.9"]
# Contamination-resistant eval harness (SWE-bench Pro / Terminal-Bench 2.0 /
# SWE-rebench). Kept optional so production installs don't pull HuggingFace
# datasets unless the operator opts into the nightly leaderboard path.
# Enable with: pip install 'bernstein[eval]'
eval = ["datasets>=4.8.5", "huggingface-hub>=0.24"]
# Web GUI (Vite + React SPA + FastAPI mount). Static assets ship with the
# wheel under src/bernstein/gui/static/ (see artifacts). Python deps stay
# minimal so TUI users keep zero overhead. Enable with:
#   pip install 'bernstein[gui]'
# then: bernstein gui serve
gui = [
    "sse-starlette>=2.1.0",
    # Terminal QR rendering for ``bernstein gui qr`` and the
    # ``--tunnel`` flag of ``bernstein gui serve`` (#1218). Pure Python,
    # MIT-licensed, no native deps. The qr renderer ships a fallback
    # placeholder when this extra is absent so minimal installs do not
    # crash - they just print a "install qrcode" diagnostic.
    "qrcode>=7.4",
]
# OpenTelemetry OTLP/gRPC exporter for GenAI semantic conventions
# (src/bernstein/core/observability/otlp_exporter.py). The exporter is a
# no-op when this extra is absent or BERNSTEIN_OTEL_ENDPOINT is unset, so
# minimal installs do not pay the gRPC import cost. Enable with:
#   pip install 'bernstein[otel]'
otel = [
    "opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-grpc>=1.41.1",
]
# Error-telemetry SDK wired to an operator-managed Sentry-protocol-compatible
# error sink (src/bernstein/cli/main.py:_init_error_telemetry). The SDK is
# imported lazily and only initialises when BERNSTEIN_TELEMETRY_DSN is set, so
# minimal installs pay zero overhead. Enable with:
#   pip install 'bernstein[observability]'
observability = [
    "sentry-sdk[fastapi]>=2.20",
]
research-render = [
    "playwright>=1.62.0",
]
# TRACE 0.2 Trust Record emitter (src/bernstein/core/observability/trust_record.py).
# Optional so minimal installs stay dependency-free. Enable with:
#   pip install 'bernstein[trace]'
trace = ["agentrust-trace>=0.11,<0.12"]

[project.scripts]
bernstein = "bernstein.cli.main:cli"
bernstein-worker = "bernstein.core.worker:main"
bernstein-bench = "bernstein.eval.bench.bench_cli:bench_group"
verify-audit-receipt = "bernstein.core.verifier.audit_receipt_verifier:main"

[project.entry-points."bernstein.plugins"]
# Lifecycle/event plugins (hookimpl classes). Example:
# my_plugin = "my_package:MyPlugin"

[project.entry-points."bernstein.adapters"]
# Third-party CLI agent adapters (CLIAdapter subclasses). Example:
# myagent = "my_package.adapter:MyAgentAdapter"
# Then use: bernstein run --cli myagent plan.yaml

[project.entry-points."bernstein.gates"]
# Custom quality gates (GatePlugin subclasses). Example:
# my_gate = "my_package.gates:MyGate"

[project.entry-points."bernstein.triggers"]
# Custom trigger sources (normalize external events into tasks). Example:
# jira = "my_package.triggers:JiraTriggerSource"

[project.entry-points."bernstein.reporters"]
# Custom reporters (hookimpl classes that emit run summaries). Example:
# slack = "my_package.reporters:SlackReporter"

[project.entry-points."bernstein.sandbox_backends"]
# Sandbox backends (SandboxBackend protocol implementations).
# First-party backends (worktree, docker) ship in core and are registered
# by bernstein.core.sandbox.registry directly; plugin authors register
# additional backends (e2b, modal, cloud providers ...) via this group.
# Example:
# e2b = "bernstein.core.sandbox.backends.e2b:E2BSandboxBackend"
# modal = "bernstein.core.sandbox.backends.modal:ModalSandboxBackend"

[project.entry-points."bernstein.skill_sources"]
# Progressive-disclosure skill packs. Each entry resolves to a
# zero-arg factory returning a ``bernstein.core.skills.SkillSource``.
# Example:
# my-data-pack = "my_pack.skills:source"

[project.entry-points."bernstein.storage_sinks"]
# Pluggable artifact storage sinks. First-party sinks
# (local_fs, s3, gcs, azure_blob, r2) ship in core and are registered
# eagerly by bernstein.core.storage.registry; plugin authors register
# additional sinks (custom providers, domain-specific wrappers ...) via
# this group. Example:
# my_sink = "my_pkg.storage:MyArtifactSink"

[project.entry-points."bernstein.spec_quality_rules"]
# Spec-quality checklist rules (Rule factories). Each entry resolves to a
# zero-arg callable returning a
# ``bernstein.core.planning.spec_quality.Rule`` instance.
# Example:
# stakeholder = "my_pkg.spec_rules:stakeholder_factory"

[project.entry-points."bernstein.notification_sinks"]
# Outbound notification drivers (release 1.9). First-party drivers
# (telegram, slack, discord, email_smtp, webhook, shell) ship in core
# and are registered eagerly by bernstein.core.notifications.registry;
# plugin authors register additional drivers (PagerDuty, Opsgenie,
# Mattermost, ...) via this group. Each entry resolves to a callable
# whose signature is ``factory(config: dict[str, Any]) -> NotificationSink``
# and the entry name is the ``kind`` referenced from
# ``bernstein.yaml::notifications.sinks[*].kind``. Example:
# pagerduty = "my_pkg.notify:PagerDutySink"

[tool.hatch.build]
# NOTE: do NOT add src/bernstein/ entries here.  Every file under src/
# ships production code that the runtime imports -- either directly or
# via the _CoreRedirectFinder in core/__init__.py.  Previously 18 core/
# sub-packages plus three cli/run_*.py helpers were excluded (v1.8.7..
# v1.8.9 wheels on PyPI are all broken because of this); `pip install
# bernstein && bernstein --version` failed with `ModuleNotFoundError:
# No module named 'bernstein.core.config'` and similar because the
# redirect map / import chain points to files stripped from the wheel.
exclude = [
    ".sdd/",
    "tests/",
    "scripts/",
    "docs/",
    ".github/",
]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/bernstein"]
# Eval golden fixtures live INSIDE src/bernstein/eval/golden_data/ so they
# ship by virtue of being inside the package tree.  ``artifacts`` is listed
# explicitly to pin the *.md inclusion even if a future ``include`` /
# ``exclude`` rewrite tries to whitelist only *.py.  Loader:
# ``bernstein.eval.golden._packaged_tier_files`` (importlib.resources).
# .sdd/ MUST stay out of the repo (Repo hygiene CI gate); the operator
# override path .sdd/eval/golden/<tier>/*.md is still consulted first.
artifacts = [
    "src/bernstein/eval/golden_data/**/*.md",
    # Recipe golden traces - YAML fixtures that pin the resolved
    # workflow shape for each bundled recipe.  Loaded by the eval
    # harness to catch drift after refactors.
    "src/bernstein/eval/golden_data/**/*.yaml",
    # Web GUI built assets - Vite output committed to the package tree so
    # the wheel ships pre-built. Rebuild with: cd web && npm run build.
    "src/bernstein/gui/static/**/*",
    "src/bernstein/dashboard/static/**/*",
    # microVM launcher source. The libkrun monitor spawns one process per VM
    # and, on macOS, that process must carry the hypervisor entitlement, so the
    # binary is compiled and signed on the operator's host from this source
    # (`bernstein sandbox microvm-launcher`). Shipping the source rather than a
    # binary keeps the wheel platform-independent and lets the link step resolve
    # the local libkrun prefix. Loader:
    # bernstein.core.sandbox.backends._libkrun.launcher_source_dir.
    "src/bernstein/core/sandbox/backends/_libkrun_launcher/*.c",
    "src/bernstein/core/sandbox/backends/_libkrun_launcher/*.plist",
    # SDD ticket schemas. Shipped alongside the validator so downstream
    # projects can lint their .sdd/backlog tickets via importlib.resources
    # without a source checkout. Loader: bernstein.sdd.validator.load_schema.
    "src/bernstein/sdd/schema/*.json",
    # MCP per-tool input schemas (issue #1406). The orchestrator-side input
    # firewall loads them at startup to validate every incoming MCP tool
    # call. Loader: bernstein.mcp.input_validation.load_registry.
    "src/bernstein/mcp/tool_schemas/*.json",
    # OSCAL v1.1.0 assessment-results schema for compliance exports.
    "src/bernstein/compliance/oscal_schema/*.json",
    # Doctor doc-suggestion seed list. Curated list of common documentation
    # gaps surfaced by `bernstein doctor --suggest-docs`. Operator refreshes
    # it on each release. Loader:
    # bernstein.cli.doctor.suggest_docs.load_unanswered_topics.
    "src/bernstein/_default_templates/docs/*.json",
    # Tracker ingest event-type catalogue (#5132). Schema-validated YAML of
    # canonical event names; GitHub/GitLab parsers map through it only.
    # Loader: bernstein.core.trackers.event_catalogue.load_event_catalogue.
    "src/bernstein/core/trackers/event_catalogue.yaml",
]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.force-include]
"templates/prompts" = "bernstein/_default_templates/prompts"
"templates/bernstein.yaml" = "bernstein/_default_templates/bernstein.yaml"
# Progressive-disclosure skill packs - shipped alongside the wheel so
# installed packages get the index without requiring a checkout of
# templates/.
"templates/skills" = "bernstein/_default_templates/skills"
"templates/roles" = "bernstein/_default_templates/roles"
# Review pipeline DSL - built-in stage templates and the default 3-phase
# pipeline. Loaded by bernstein.core.quality.review_pipeline at runtime
# when users omit a pipeline path.
"templates/review" = "bernstein/_default_templates/review"
# Lethal-trifecta capability matrix declarations.  Bundled so the
# default-deny check can find tags right after pip install.
"templates/capabilities" = "bernstein/_default_templates/capabilities"
# Provenance trust-class source map (issue #2513). Bundled so tool-result
# taint classification resolves right after pip install.
"templates/provenance" = "bernstein/_default_templates/provenance"
# Stock YAML workflow manifests (#1108) shipped with the wheel so
# `bernstein workflow list` / `... run <name>` resolve immediately
# without requiring a source checkout.
"templates/workflows" = "bernstein/_default_templates/workflows"
# Plan templates (#4877) for `bernstein templates list|use`. They lived at
# the repo root under plans/, which is the user's own working directory, and
# so shipped in no wheel at all - the command was dead on every install.
"templates/plans" = "bernstein/_default_templates/plans"
# First-class recipe library - parameterised workflows for common
# operator tasks (refactor-glob, bump-dependency, add-tests-for-module,
# license-audit, regenerate-docs).  Shipped in the wheel so
# `bernstein recipes list|show|run` resolves immediately.
"templates/recipes" = "bernstein/_default_templates/recipes"
# Per-task criterion profile presets (issue #1346).  Shipped in the
# wheel so `bernstein run --criterion-profile safety-first` resolves
# without a source checkout, mirroring the mode_profile pattern.
"templates/criterion_profiles" = "bernstein/_default_templates/criterion_profiles"
# Blast-radius detector defaults (#1322) so the reversibility gate finds
# its rule list without requiring a source checkout.
"templates/blast-radius" = "bernstein/_default_templates/blast-radius"
# Built-in team manifests (#2248) so `team_manifest: python` and the
# `bernstein team` commands resolve right after pip install.
"templates/teams" = "bernstein/_default_templates/teams"
# Packaged scenario library for `bernstein scenario list|run` and
# `bernstein routine ...`. Resolved by
# bernstein.core.planning.scenario_library.packaged_scenarios_dir; without
# this entry the commands see an empty library on every pip install.
"templates/scenarios" = "bernstein/_default_templates/scenarios"
# Adapter admission evidence (#3547). The verdict `bernstein adapters
# verify --seal` derives is a projection of the pinned contract's bytes and
# the golden-transcript replay, so both have to be resolvable off a pip
# install or every adapter falls back to a skip-shaped refusal
# (`no_contract` / `no_transcript`) and the seal can never go green outside
# a dev checkout. Both trees are shipped verbatim rather than filtered, so
# an installed host derives the same replay fingerprint a checkout does.
# Loaders: bernstein.adapters._contract.CONTRACTS_DIR and
# bernstein.adapters.admission.golden_transcripts_dir.
"tests/contract/contracts" = "bernstein/_default_templates/adapter_contracts"
"tests/golden" = "bernstein/_default_templates/adapter_golden"
# Cross-vendor agent-plugin assets (#2369): the bernstein-run skill plus
# the plugin command/agent/rule files, so `bernstein skills package
# install` resolves the bundled tree right after pip install. Loader:
# bernstein.core.skills.packaging.packaged_asset_root.
"skills" = "bernstein/_default_templates/agent_plugin/skills"
"commands" = "bernstein/_default_templates/agent_plugin/commands"
"agents" = "bernstein/_default_templates/agent_plugin/agents"
"rules" = "bernstein/_default_templates/agent_plugin/rules"
".mcp.json" = "bernstein/_default_templates/agent_plugin/.mcp.json"
".plugin/plugin.json" = "bernstein/_default_templates/agent_plugin/.plugin/plugin.json"
# Standalone audit-receipt verifier. The `verify-audit-receipt` console
# script and `bernstein audit receipt verify` run this file as a subprocess
# (it imports only stdlib + cryptography + cbor2, never bernstein). It lives
# at the repo root under tools/, so without this entry every pip / uv / conda
# install exited 2 with "can't open file .../tools/verify_audit_receipt.py".
# Loader: bernstein.core.verifier.audit_receipt_verifier.VERIFIER_SCRIPT.
"tools/verify_audit_receipt.py" = "bernstein/_default_templates/tools/verify_audit_receipt.py"
# ascii_logo.md now lives in-package at src/bernstein/_default_templates/ -
# no force-include needed. The dev-repo copy at docs/assets/ascii_logo.md is
# the display fallback read by cli/display/splash_v2.py when running from a
# source checkout.

[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist.force-include]
# Wheel force-include sources must also exist inside the sdist: `uv build`
# (and any pip install from the sdist) builds the wheel FROM the sdist, and
# hatchling hard-fails on a missing force-include source. Every other wheel

[tool.mypy]
# Repo-wide mypy settings for the documented `uv run mypy src` command.
# This run is advisory: mypy has a large pre-existing backlog because it
# never actually parsed the tree (see the note on `python_version` below).
# The subset that gates CI lives in mypy.gate.ini, the same way the
# repo-wide pyright run is advisory and pyrightconfig.strict.json gates.
#
# `python_version` is pinned rather than inherited from whatever
# interpreter happens to run mypy. It matches [tool.pyright] pythonVersion
# and the `requires-python` floor. Note that this pins the *target*
# version only - PEP 695 `type` aliases (11 of them in src/) still need
# the interpreter running mypy to be >= 3.12, because mypy parses with the
# host `ast` module. That is why mypy is a declared dev dependency: an
# undeclared `uv run mypy` falls through to a PATH mypy that may be bound
# to an older interpreter, and the run then aborts on the first alias with
# `Invalid syntax` before checking anything.
python_version = "3.12"
files = ["src"]
namespace_packages = true
warn_unused_configs = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
# Legacy `bernstein.core.*` / `bernstein.cli.*` import paths are served at
# runtime by the `sys.meta_path` finders in src/bernstein/core/__init__.py
# and src/bernstein/cli/__init__.py, not by files on disk. No static
# checker can follow a meta-path redirect, so these resolve to nothing.
module = ["bernstein.*"]
ignore_missing_imports = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
# Installed dependencies that ship neither a `py.typed` marker nor a
# published stub distribution. Checked against PyPI: there is no
# `types-asn1crypto`, `types-kubernetes` or `types-e2b-code-interpreter`,
# and the `google.cloud` namespace package carries no marker of its own
# even though the individual `google-cloud-*` distributions do.
#
# Every other untyped import in the tree is resolved by a real stub
# package in [dependency-groups].dev instead - see the block there. This
# list is the residue, and it should shrink as upstream adds markers, not
# grow. Adding an entry here means "no type information exists anywhere";
# it is not a place to park a package we simply have not stubbed yet.
module = [
    "asn1crypto.*",  # RFC 3161 ASN.1 parsing, core/security/rfc3161_verifier.py
    "e2b_code_interpreter.*",  # `e2b` extra, core/sandbox/backends/e2b.py
    "google.cloud.*",  # `gcs` extra, core/security/secrets_broker.py
    "kubernetes.*",  # `k8s` extra, core/orchestration/operator.py
]

# ImportError, with a typed fallback when absent. They are absent from the
# environment `uv run mypy src` sees - the first group is not declared in
# [project] at all, the second is behind an extra that a plain `uv sync`
# does not install - so mypy reports `import-not-found`.
#
# `ignore_missing_imports` only applies to an import that fails to
# resolve. Where the package is present and ships inline annotations
# (`datasets`, `spiffe`, and most of the first group), mypy reads the real
# types and this override does nothing - so it silences the "not
# installed" noise without masking a typed surface.

# The first group is deliberately not installed rather than un-stubbed:
# pulling it into the dev group to read those annotations would add native
# toolchains (sounddevice/PortAudio, weasyprint/cairo+pango), multi-

minversion = "8.0"

# auto-collecting unmarked async tests and breaking existing suites.
asyncio_mode = "strict"
addopts = [
    "--strict-markers",
    "--strict-config",
]
markers = [
    "ci: tests that run as part of CI for every release",
    "auth_enabled: opt out of the autouse auth-disabled shim (tests that exercise auth defaults)",
    "audit_key_real: opt out of the autouse audit-key path isolation (tests that exercise the real resolution logic)",
    "cluster_e2e: real-process cluster harness tests; skipped by default, run via the cluster-e2e workflow",
    "slow: long-running tests (> ~5s); skipped by default in fast feedback runs",
    "integration: end-to-end / subprocess-driven integration tests; selectable via -m integration in CI",
    "stress: resource-leak / memory-growth / deadlock stress tests (TC-C); gated off by default CI, run nightly via `-m stress`",
    "allow_network: opt out of the autouse unit no-network guard (rare; a genuine integration test belongs in tests/integration/ instead)",
    "protocol: protocol compatibility tests; applied to every item under tests/protocol/ by that directory's conftest, and run by the publish workflow's release gate",
    "auditor_question: binds one conformance vector under tests/integration/conformance/auditor/ to the question it answers; the argument is a question number registered in that suite's questions.py",
    "whole_tree_guard: asserts an invariant over the whole source tree by scanning it; no diff produces an import edge to these, so `scripts/run_tests.py --affected` selects them on every pull request regardless of what changed",

# can tighten via `pytest -W error::DeprecationWarning`.

[tool.uv]
# The checked-in gRPC gencode under src/bernstein/core/grpc_gen/ carries
# `Protobuf Python Version: 7.35.1` and calls ValidateProtobufRuntimeVersion()
# at import time, which rejects any runtime from an older major. The modal SDK
# caps protobuf below 7.0, so the `grpc` and `modal` extras cannot share one
# environment. Declaring the conflict keeps the universal lock resolvable and
# turns a former import-time VersionError into an install-time resolution
# error, which is where a dependency conflict belongs.
#
# `otel` has the same shape as `grpc` here, not a different one:
# opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-grpc>=1.41.1 pins protobuf==7.35.1 (same
# generated-code floor as the checked-in gRPC gencode above), which modal's
# <7.0 cap rules out just as directly. Undeclared, this doesn't fail as a
# known-incompatible pair - it fails as "your project's requirements are
# unsatisfiable" from the *whole* lockfile, which is what aborted every `uv`
# dependency-update run rather than just the two extras that actually clash
# (#4088).
conflicts = [[{ extra = "grpc" }, { extra = "modal" }], [{ extra = "otel" }, { extra = "modal" }]]
# spiffe 0.3.1 caps pyjwt below 2.14, but pyjwt 2.13 carries ten published
# advisories fixed in 2.14.0 and nothing in the spiffe extra depends on the
# behaviour that cap guards. The override lets the universal lock resolve
# pyjwt to a patched release; drop it once spiffe lifts its cap.
override-dependencies = ["pyjwt>=2.14"]

# bundled stubs (e.g. numpy/__init__.pyi), which mypy rejects with a syntax
# error under python_version < 3.12. Skipping numpy's stubs instead is not an
# option — that types numpy as Any and cascades 130+ strict errors through
# first-party array code. The 3.10 support floor (requires-python = ">=3.10")
# is guarded by the Verify CI matrix, which executes the suite on real 3.10 /
# 3.11 / 3.12 interpreters; mypy stays a pure type gate.
[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.12"
strict = true
warn_return_any = true
warn_unused_configs = true
warn_redundant_casts = false
disable_error_code = ["redundant-cast"]

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#  ruff — comprehensive Python linting

[tool.ruff]
