target-version = "py310"
# Frozen surfaces excluded from lint — scheduled for removal in v5.0

  "research/",
]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
  "E",     # pycodestyle errors
  "W",     # pycodestyle warnings
  "F",     # pyflakes
  "I",     # isort
  "B",     # flake8-bugbear — opinionated bug detection
  "C4",    # flake8-comprehensions — unnecessary list/dict comprehension
  "UP",    # pyupgrade — modernize syntax for target Python
  "SIM",   # flake8-simplify — simplifiable constructs
  "PT",    # flake8-pytest-style — pytest best practices
  "RUF",   # ruff-specific rules
  "S",     # flake8-bandit — security checks
  "A",     # flake8-builtins — shadowing built-ins
  "C90",   # mccabe complexity
  "DTZ",   # flake8-datetimez — naive datetime usage
  "T20",   # flake8-print — print() in production code
  "PIE",   # flake8-pie — misc lints
  "PLC",   # pylint convention
  "PLE",   # pylint error
  "PLW",   # pylint warning
  "TID",   # flake8-tidy-imports — banned imports
  "TCH",   # flake8-type-checking — move imports to TYPE_CHECKING
  "PERF",  # perflint — performance anti-patterns
  "FLY",   # flynt — f-string conversion
  "FURB",  # refurb — modern Python idioms
]
ignore = [
  "E402",    # module-level import not at top (needed for conditional imports)
  "S101",    # assert usage (allowed in tests, banned in src via per-file)
  "S311",    # pseudo-random generators (acceptable for simulation seeds)
  "B008",    # function call in default argument (FastAPI Depends pattern)
  "UP007",   # X | Y union syntax (keep Optional for readability in complex signatures)
  "SIM108",  # ternary operator (readability over brevity for scientific code)
  "C901",    # too complex (handled by C90 mccabe with explicit threshold)
  "PLW2901", # loop variable overwritten (common in numeric code)
  "S603",    # subprocess call (needed in scripts)
  "S607",    # partial executable path (needed in scripts)
  "PLC0415", # import-outside-top-level (lazy imports by design for optional deps)
  "RUF002",  # ambiguous-unicode-character-docstring (μM, α, β are scientific notation)
  "RUF001",  # ambiguous-unicode-character-string (same)
  "RUF003",  # ambiguous-unicode-character-comment (same)
  "PLW0603", # global-statement (registry pattern for causal rules, detection config)
  "RUF043",  # pytest-raises-ambiguous-pattern (acceptable in test assertions)
  "PERF203", # try-except-in-loop (necessary for resilient iteration over scenarios)
  "PERF401", # manual-list-comprehension (readability over micro-optimization in scientific code)
  "PLW1510", # subprocess-run-without-check (scripts handle errors explicitly)
  "RUF012",  # mutable-class-default (dataclass fields with default_factory pattern)
  "SIM105",  # suppressible-exception (explicit try/except clearer than contextlib.suppress)
  "PT011",   # pytest-raises-too-broad (acceptable for integration tests)
  "PT012",   # pytest-raises-with-multiple-statements (test readability)
  "PT017",   # pytest-assert-in-except (intentional test pattern)
  "E741",    # ambiguous-variable-name (I, F, H, N are standard in scientific code)
  "S110",    # try-except-pass (intentional for optional features with fail-closed pattern)
  "T201",    # print (used in CLI, scripts, and cognitive functions)
  "E501",    # line-too-long (handled by formatter, allow in complex expressions)
  "A002",    # builtin-argument-shadowing (id= in rule_registry is domain convention)
  "B039",    # mutable-contextvar-default (logging config pattern)
  "S104",    # hardcoded-bind-all-interfaces (API server binds 0.0.0.0 by design)
  "S105",    # hardcoded-password-string (false positive on enum/config field names)
  "S112",    # try-except-continue (rate limiter resilience pattern)
  "SIM102",  # collapsible-if (readability over compactness in gate logic)
  "DTZ003",  # call-datetime-utcnow (UTC usage intentional in timestamps)
  "DTZ005",  # call-datetime-now-without-tzinfo (same)
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"src/**/__init__.py" = [
  "F401",    # unused-import: __init__.py re-exports are intentional public API
]
"tests/**/*.py" = [
  "S101",    # assert is fine in tests
  "S105",    # hardcoded passwords in test fixtures
  "S106",    # hardcoded passwords in test arguments
  "T20",     # print in tests is acceptable
  "PLR2004", # magic values in tests are fine
]
"scripts/**/*.py" = [
  "T20",     # print is expected in CLI scripts
  "S603",    # subprocess calls in scripts
  "S607",    # partial path in scripts
]
"src/mycelium_fractal_net/cli.py" = [
  "T20",     # print is the correct output mechanism for CLI
]
"src/mycelium_fractal_net/__main__.py" = [
  "T20",     # print is the correct output for CLI entrypoint
]
"src/mycelium_fractal_net/integration/crypto_adapters.py" = [
  "B904",    # frozen adapter — exception chaining deferred to v5.0
]
"src/mycelium_fractal_net/experiments/**/*.py" = [
  "T20",     # print for experiment output
]
"src/mycelium_fractal_net/pipelines/reporting.py" = [
  "E501",    # HTML templates contain long lines by nature
]
"src/mycelium_fractal_net/pipelines/scenarios/**/*.py" = [
  "T20",     # print in __main__ blocks
]
"benchmarks/**/*.py" = [
  "T20",     # print for benchmark output
  "S101",    # assert in benchmarks
]

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

[tool.mypy]

    "mycelium_fractal_net.self_reading.*",
]

strict_equality = true

# Frozen / transport / ML modules: errors reported but not blocking

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = [
    "mycelium_fractal_net.model",
    "mycelium_fractal_net.signal.*",
    "mycelium_fractal_net.numerics.*",

# codemem-mcp is a sibling standalone package; see packages/codemem-mcp/pyproject.toml.
# Rationale documented in .claude/dev/active/codemem/codemem-plan.md §3 #1 (Q1 + Q13).
members = ["packages/codemem-mcp"]

[tool.uv.sources]
codemem-mcp = { workspace = true }

[tool.ruff]
# Eval fixtures plant logging/style defects on purpose for the skills to find (ADR-0021).
extend-exclude = [
    "tests/fixtures/evals",
    "tests/fixtures/canary/canary_shell.py",  # why: a deliberate S602; tests/security/test_canary.py scans it explicitly
]

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Logging + comment hygiene (logging-and-comments standard). CI's `touched` job runs
# `ruff check` (via pre-commit) on every file a PR touches (ADR-0018).
# T201 has only an unsafe fix, so `ruff check --fix` reports prints and never deletes them.
extend-select = [
    "LOG",              # logger misuse: Logger() direct, getLogger without __name__, root-logger calls
    "G",                # eager log formatting (G004 = f-string in log call), .warn, exc_info misuse
    "T20",              # print/pprint left in library code
    "BLE",              # blind `except Exception`
    "S",                # flake8-bandit security rules, the Python security gate (M8, ruff-only); incl. S110/S112 silent swallows
    "TRY400", "TRY401", # use logger.exception in except; don't repeat the exception in the message
    "D",                # docstrings, google convention (incl. D417 undocumented Args) (T8)
    "TD",               # TODO format: TODO(owner/issue): text
    "ERA",              # commented-out code
    "RUF100",           # unused noqa: a suppression that suppresses nothing is removed (T8)
    "PGH003", "PGH004", # blanket `type: ignore` / `noqa`: name the code you silence (T8)
    "C901",             # cyclomatic complexity (KISS, T11 §3)
    "PLR0913",          # too many arguments (KISS, T11 §3)
    "W605",             # invalid escape sequence: a SyntaxWarning on Python 3.12+, an error later
]
# Touched files comply in full (D8): CI lints only the files a PR touches, so the
# pre-existing docstring gaps are paid down as files are edited, not all at once.
# PLR2004 (magic values) is deliberately not selected: constants are review-only (T8).
extend-ignore = [
    "D107",  # why: the class docstring documents __init__ args (google style, T8)
    "TD003", # why: wants an issue URL line; it rejects TODO(ADR-NNNN), which TODO001 accepts (T8)
]

[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "google"

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 10  # why: ruff/flake8 default; Ste's T11 §3 ceiling for one function

[tool.ruff.lint.pylint]
max-args = 6  # why: one over ruff's 5 — leaves room for a keyword-only flag (T11 §3)

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# print IS the interface for CLIs (data -> stdout); tests need no docstrings.
"**/cli.py" = ["T20"]
"**/__main__.py" = ["T20"]
"src/aa_ma/forks.py" = ["T20"]  # run as `python -m aa_ma.forks`; stdout is its report
"src/aa_ma/deps.py" = ["T20"]   # run as `python -m aa_ma.deps` (aa_ma_deps helper); stdout is its report
"scripts/**" = ["T20"]
# tests run git/bash on purpose (S603/S607), write tmp fixtures (S108) and assert (S101) — approved M8.2.
"tests/**" = ["D", "T20", "S101", "S108", "S110", "S603", "S607"]

[tool.commitizen]
# Releases are cut by scripts/release.sh (docs/runbooks/release.md): it promotes the curated
# `## Unreleased` CHANGELOG section and the README "Current version" line, then `cz bump`
# updates version_files and commits everything (-a) under an annotated tag. cz never writes
# the CHANGELOG — update_changelog_on_bump=true replaced curated notes with commit subjects
# every release from v0.7.0 to v0.11.0 (lessons L-006/L-008).
name = "cz_conventional_commits"
version_provider = "pep621"
tag_format = "v$version"
update_changelog_on_bump = false
annotated_tag = true
bump_message = "bump: version $current_version → $new_version\n\n[ad-hoc]"
version_files = [
    "VERSION:__version__",
]
# uv.lock records the project version; re-lock after cz writes version_files so the -a
# commit (and the tag) carry a consistent lock. release.sh refuses to push otherwise.
pre_bump_hooks = ["uv lock --quiet"]

# --------------------------------------------------------------------
# pytest (M1 Task 1.13)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------
# The `perf` marker gates the performance-budget suite at
# `tests/perf/test_budgets.py`. Default test runs skip it (via the
# `addopts` filter below); run it locally with `-m perf` (CI does not run it).
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
markers = [
    "perf: performance-budget gates (codemem M1 Task 1.13). Skipped by default; run with `-m perf`.",
    "slow: long-running property tests (codemem M2 Task 2.4 roundtrip — 100 examples). Skipped by default; run with `-m slow`.",
]
# tests/fixtures/evals/ holds eval-case fixture repos (ADR-0021), not this repo's tests.
addopts = "-m 'not perf and not slow' --ignore=tests/fixtures/evals"

[dependency-groups]

    "hypothesis>=6.0",         # M2 property-based round-trip tests (Step 2.4)
    "import-linter>=2.0",      # M1 layer-boundary enforcement (Step 1.11)
    "commitizen>=4,<5",        # scripts/release.sh; pinned <5 (cz 5 removes --files-only and may change bump flags). Was only on PATH via a conda env (L-015).
    "ruff>=0.4",
    "tiktoken>=0.7",           # codemem-token-benchmarks M2: external tokenizer for cross-tool normalization
    "mcp>=1.29.1,<2",               # codemem-benchmark-fairness-v2 M2a.1: explicit dev dep for jCodeMunch stdio MCP round-trip in scripts/bench_codemem_vs_aider.py (already transitive via fastmcp; declared explicitly per L-055).

    "pip-audit>=2.10.1",       # code-conventions-impact M8.4: CI deps job (uv audit is experimental in uv 0.12.3, A6)
]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# setuptools : déclare tous les packages pour que pip install -e . fonctionne
# et que conftest.py n'ait plus besoin de manipuler sys.path.

where = ["."]
include = [
    "common*",
    "core*",
    "database*",
    "dataIntegrityEngine*",
    "event_sentiment*",
    "screener*",
    "selector*",

    "risk_management*",

# Phase C / S14 — mutation testing scope (mutmut)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

paths_to_mutate = "risk_management/,execution_engine/,corporate_actions/"
runner = "pytest -x -q --no-cov"
backup = false

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ruff — linter rapide (remplace flake8 + isort + pyupgrade)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py312"
line-length = 120

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",    # pycodestyle errors
    "W",    # pycodestyle warnings
    "F",    # pyflakes
    "I",    # isort
    "UP",   # pyupgrade
    "B",    # flake8-bugbear
    "C4",   # flake8-comprehensions
    "SIM",  # flake8-simplify
]
ignore = [
    "E501",   # line too long (géré par line-length)
    "B008",   # do not perform function calls in default arguments
    "SIM108", # ternary vs if/else (lisibilité)
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/*" = ["S101"]  # assert autorisé dans les tests

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# mypy — vérification statique des types
# (config complète dans mypy.ini pour compatibilité IDE)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.12"
ignore_missing_imports = true

requires-python = ">=3.11"
keywords = ["agents", "governance", "llm", "ai"]

    "Development Status :: 3 - Alpha",

    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries",
]

# Provider SDKs live in adapter packages (axor-claude, axor-openai, axor-openrouter).

# symmetric HMAC signer needs nothing. Install this only for asymmetric A2A trust.

    "cryptography>=42.0",
]

    "pytest>=8.0",
    "pytest-asyncio>=0.23",
    "pytest-cov>=5.0",

]

[tool.uv]
default-groups = [ "dev" ]
# Docs: https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/settings
add-bounds = "major"

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py310"
line-length = 88
[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [ "ALL" ]
ignore = [
  "ANN",    # Type hints related, let mypy handle these.
  "ARG",    # Unused arguments
  "CPY001", # Copyright notices
  "D100",   # Module docstrings
  "D104",   # Package docstrings
  "D105",   # Magic method docstrings
  "D106",   # Nested class docstrings, such as Meta
  "D107",   # __init__ docstrings
  "D212",   # Multi-line summaries may start on the second line
  "D404",   # First word of the docstring
  "D405",   # Section name capitalization
  "EM101",  # "Exception must not use a string literal, assign to variable first"
  "EM102",  # "Exception must not use an f-string literal, assign to variable first"
  "PD",     # Pandas related
  "Q000",   # For now
  "SIM105", # "Use contextlib.suppress({exception}) instead of try-except-pass"
  "TRY003", # "Avoid specifying long messages outside the exception class"
]
# Migrations are special
per-file-ignores."**/migrations/*" = [ "D", "RUF012" ]
# Sphinx specific
per-file-ignores."docs/source/conf.py" = [ "D", "INP001" ]
# Allow private member access for Registry
per-file-ignores."eav/registry.py" = [ "SLF001" ]
per-file-ignores."test_project/**" = [ "D" ]
# pytest is even more special
per-file-ignores."tests/*" = [
  "D",       # Tests are named for what they check
  "INP001",  # "Add an __init__.py"
  "PLR2004", # "Magic value used in comparison"
  "PLW0108", # "Lambda may be unnecessary" - used with assertRaises
  "PT009",   # "Use a regular assert instead of unittest-style"
  "PT027",   # "Use pytest.raises instead of unittest-style"
  "PT030",   # "pytest.warns match parameter" - broad warnings intentional in tests
  "S101",    # "Use of assert detected"
  "SLF001"  # "Private member accessed"
]

external = [ "WPS" ]
flake8-implicit-str-concat.allow-multiline = false

pydocstyle.convention = "google"

    "C4", # flake8-comprehensions
    "C90", # mccabe complexity (includes C901: too complex)
    "UP", # pyupgrade
]

    "E501",  # line too long - line-length checks disabled globally
    "B008",  # do not perform function calls in argument defaults
    # py314 (PEP 649/749) modernization deferred from #748 to #988; remove these when it lands.
    "UP037",  # quoted annotations (420 sites); safe to unquote only with runtime-resolver review
    "UP043",  # unnecessary default type args
]

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 11

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]

"tests/**/*" = ["B011"]
"docs/**/*" = ["F821", "F841", "F811", "B904", "E402"]
# Codacy's containerised PyLintPython3 uses a pre-3.12 parser and fails to parse PEP 695 type
# parameter lists ("Parsing failed: expected '('"). Keep the TypeVar spelling used by the
# repo's other 12 generics until that runtime catches up. See #784.
"server/tests/support.py" = ["UP047"]
"server/main.py" = ["E402"]  # Reason: Imports must come after load_dotenv() to ensure env vars are loaded before any modules that depend on them are imported

# Based Pyright (IDE / CLI): scope checks to this repo; do not analyze stdlib sources
# or dependency trees under .venv. If you still see diagnostics on
# pyenv-win/.../Lib/*.py, that file is outside the project: close it and set the
# interpreter to this workspace's .venv.
[tool.basedpyright]
pythonVersion = "3.14"
venvPath = "."
venv = ".venv"
# Repo root on path so scripts/*.py can import the top-level `server` package (same as runtime sys.path).
extraPaths = ["."]
# Scope: server/** only (prod + tests). Mirrors `files = ["server"]` under [tool.mypy].
# A no-argument `basedpyright` run -- which is what the pre-commit gate and CI run -- checks
# exactly this set, so the baseline in .basedpyright/baseline.json stays meaningful. See #784.
include = ["server"]
# `# type: ignore[code]` is a mypy comment. basedpyright honours a bare `# type: ignore` by
# suppressing EVERY rule on that line and ignoring the mypy rule code, so 372 such comments
# under server/ were blanket-laundering Any findings. Rule-specific `# pyright: ignore[rule]`
# is the only suppression this project accepts, and it must carry the justification comment
# enforced by scripts/lint_pyright_suppressions.py. See #784.
enableTypeIgnoreComments = false
exclude = [
    "**/.venv",
    "**/node_modules",
    "**/__pycache__",
    "**/.git",
    "**/htmlcov",
    "**/.mypy_cache",
    "**/.pytest_cache",
    "**/.ruff_cache",
    "**/graphify-out",
    "**/graphify",
]

    "sqlfluff>=4.2.0", # SQL linting and formatting; >=4.1.0 CVE-2026-46373, >=4.2.0 CVE-2026-46374

# ===================================================================
# Ruff (Linter + Formatter)
# 核心代码质量工具，集成了数十种工具，速度极快。
# 负责：代码风格检查、自动格式化、导入排序、坏味道重构等。
# ===================================================================
[tool.ruff]
required-version = ">=0.6.0"
# 设置与 Black 兼容的行长。
line-length = 88
# 指定你的项目支持的最低 Python 版本。
target-version = "py313"

# 指定 Ruff 需要检查的源代码和测试目录。
src = ["packages", "apps/backend", "scripts", "tooling"]

# 全局排除不需要检查的文件和目录。
exclude = [
    ".bzr",
    ".direnv",
    ".eggs",
    ".git",
    ".hg",
    ".nox",
    ".pants.d",
    ".ruff_cache",
    ".svn",
    ".tox",
    ".venv",
    "__pypackages__",
    "_build",
    "build",
    "dist",
    "node_modules",
    "venv",
    "scripts/learning",
]

cache-dir = ".ruff_cache"
respect-gitignore = true
force-exclude = true

# --- Ruff Linter (检查器) 配置 ---
[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",
    "F",
    "W",
    "C90",
    "I",
    "N",
    "UP",
    "B",
    "A",
    "C4",
    "SIM",
    "PTH",
    "PLC",
    "PLE",
    "PLR",
    "PLW",
    "RUF",
    "D",
    "PT",
    "ANN",
    "S",
    "T20",
]

ignore = [
    "B008",   # 允许函数调用作为默认参数（FastAPI Depends）
    "N803",   # 函数参数命名：第三方库适配（numpy 矩阵变量等）
    "N806",   # 函数内变量命名：数学/科学计算常量（X, XtX, CONVERGENCE_TOL 等）
    "N818",   # DittoException 基类命名是设计选择
    "RUF002", # 中文标点符号
    "RUF003", # 中文注释标点符号
    "D203",   # 与 Black 冲突
    "D212",   # 与 Black 冲突
    "D100",   # 模块必须有文档字符串
    "D107",   # __init__ 文档字符串
    "D400",   # 文档字符串句号结尾（中文不适用）
    "D415",   # 文档字符串首行标点
    "D401",   # 祈使语气
    "PT011",  # pytest.raises match 参数
    "SIM105", # contextlib.suppress
    "SIM117", # 嵌套 with 语句
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]

# Protocol 接口方法用 ``...`` 省略体是标准惯例，D102 不适用

[tool.ruff.lint.pylint]

[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]

# flake8-tidy-imports: 禁止特定 API 导入
[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports.banned-api]
"pandas".msg = "Use polars instead"

# ===================================================================
# BasedPyright (类型检查) - Pyright fork，更严格的默认设置
#
# 策略：standard 打底 + 核心目录 strict
# 优势：
#   1. 避免全仓 strict 导致的噪音爆炸
#   2. 核心业务逻辑获得最严格检查
#   3. 边缘模块保持灵活性
#   4. 更多诊断规则默认启用，更好的 AI coding 支持
# ===================================================================
[tool.basedpyright]
pythonVersion = "3.13"
pythonPlatform = "All"
stubPath = "typings"

# 显式指定 uv 管理的虚拟环境，确保 VS Code 扩展和 CLI 都能正确定位
venvPath = "."
venv = ".venv"

# 核心：standard 模式打底（比 basic 严格，比 strict 宽松）
typeCheckingMode = "standard"

# 源码目录（tests 用独立配置 pyright.tests.json）
include = ["packages/**/src", "apps/backend/src"]

# 排除目录（tests 用独立配置）
exclude = [
    "**/__pycache__",
    "**/node_modules",
    ".venv",
    "build",
    "dist",
    "tests",
    "**/tests",
]

# VS Code 体验：tests 打开也不出红黄线（诊断被抑制）
ignore = [
    "tests",
    "tests/**",
    "**/tests/**",
    "packages/*/tests/**",
    "apps/backend/tests/**",
    # MarketQueryService: multi-line error message uses implicit string concatenation
    # (已迁移至 services/)
]

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 关键：核心目录提升到 strict 模式
# 这些是最值钱的代码，值得最严格的检查
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
strict = ["packages/**/src"]

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 规则微调：让 Ruff 管风格，Pyright 专注类型
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Ruff 已经管了这些
reportUnusedImport = "none"
reportUnusedVariable = "none"

# 第三方库 stub 不完整时的处理
reportMissingTypeStubs = "warning"

# 检测不必要的 type: ignore 注释
reportUnnecessaryTypeIgnoreComment = "error"

# 检测隐式字符串拼接
reportImplicitStringConcatenation = "error"

# 对于 standard 模式下的 Unknown 类型，降级为 warning
# 这样编辑器里能看到黄线提醒，但不会阻塞 CI
#reportUnknownMemberType = "warning"
#reportUnknownArgumentType = "warning"
#reportUnknownVariableType = "warning"

# 私有成员访问（测试和内部模块可能需要）
#reportPrivateUsage = "warning"

# 告诉 Pyright 源码根目录（解决 import 路径问题）
extraPaths = [
    "packages/platform/src",
    "packages/kernel/src",
    "packages/data/src",
    "packages/features/src",
    "packages/analysis/src",
    "packages/strategy/src",
    "packages/portfolio/src",
    "packages/risk/src",
    "packages/execution/src",
    "packages/backtest/src",
    "packages/application/src",
    "apps/backend/src",
]

# ===================================================================
# Pytest (测试框架)
# ===================================================================
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
minversion = "7.0"
testpaths = ["packages/*/tests", "apps/backend/tests"]
python_files = ["test_*.py"]
python_classes = ["Test*"]
python_functions = ["test_*"]
pythonpath = [
    ".",
    "packages/platform/src",
    "packages/kernel/src",
    "packages/data/src",
    "packages/features/src",
    "packages/analysis/src",
    "packages/strategy/src",
    "packages/portfolio/src",
    "packages/risk/src",
    "packages/execution/src",
    "packages/backtest/src",
    "packages/application/src",
    "apps/backend/src",
]

filterwarnings = ["error", "ignore::UserWarning", "ignore::DeprecationWarning"]

markers = [
    "unit: Mark test as a unit test",
    "integration: Mark test as an integration test",
    "e2e: Mark test as an end-to-end test",
    "slow: Mark test as slow running (skip with -m 'not slow')",
    "serial: Mark test that must run serially",
    "capacity: Mark scheduler-capacity slow-lane test (dedicated CI job)",
    "snapshot: Mark test that uses inline-snapshot (must run serially)",
    "pit: Mark test as Point-in-Time validation (no future data leak)",
    "sandbox_live: Physical OCI sandbox acceptance requiring the approved runtime",
    "cli_test: CLI tests that disable observability auto-reset",
]

log_cli = true
log_cli_level = "INFO"
asyncio_mode = "strict"

# pytest-timeout 兜底防挂死；合法慢测试打 slow/capacity 标记进慢车道，不调大此值
timeout = 600

addopts = [
    "-ra",
    "-v",
    "--import-mode=importlib",
    "-n", "auto",           # 默认并行运行
    "--dist", "loadfile",   # 同文件测试串行（避免 snapshot 冲突）
    "--strict-markers",
    "--strict-config",
    "--durations=10",       # 报告最慢的 10 个测试
]

# ===================================================================
# Coverage
# ===================================================================
[tool.coverage.run]
branch = true
patch = ["subprocess"]
source = [
    "apps/backend/src/ditto_apps",
    "packages/agent/src/ditto_agent",
    "packages/analysis/src/ditto_analysis",
    "packages/application/src/ditto_application",
    "packages/backtest/src/ditto_backtest",
    "packages/data/src/ditto_data",
    "packages/execution/src/ditto_execution",
    "packages/features/src/ditto_features",
    "packages/kernel/src/ditto_kernel",
    "packages/platform/src/ditto_platform",
    "packages/portfolio/src/ditto_portfolio",
    "packages/risk/src/ditto_risk",
    "packages/strategy/src/ditto_strategy",
]
omit = ["**/generated/**", "**/tests/**"]

[tool.coverage.report]
precision = 2
show_missing = true
skip_covered = false
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "def __repr__",
    "def __str__",
    "raise AssertionError",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
    "@(abc\\.)?abstractmethod",
    "@overload",
    "class .*\\bProtocol\\):",
    "if self\\.debug:",
]
fail_under = 0
partial_branches = ["pragma: no branch", "if TYPE_CHECKING:"]

[tool.coverage.html]
directory = "htmlcov"

[tool.commitizen]

tag_format = "v$version"
update_changelog_on_bump = true
changelog_incremental = true

    "mypy>=1.10.0",
    "import-linter>=2.0",
    "respx>=0.21.0",
    "aiosqlite>=0.20.0",  # in-memory SQLAlchemy backend for unit/integration tests
]

[project.scripts]
cyberdyne-backend = "cyberdyne_backend.main:main"

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/cyberdyne_backend"]

# ── pytest ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
# Default test run skips integration tests so CI stays offline. Use
# `just test-integration` to opt in.
addopts = "-m 'not integration'"
markers = [
    "unit: Unit tests (no I/O, no real HTTP, no DB)",
    "integration: Adapter-level tests that cross a process boundary",
]

# ── coverage ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Gate only the hexagonal core (domain + application) at 90% — adapters
# are exercised by integration tests instead, same shape as the rest of
# the Cyberdyne stack. The whole tree is still imported when tests run,
# but coverage only counts the layers we care about gating.
[tool.coverage.run]
source = [
    "src/cyberdyne_backend/domain",
    "src/cyberdyne_backend/application",
]
omit = ["**/__init__.py"]
branch = true

[tool.coverage.report]
fail_under = 90
show_missing = true
skip_covered = true
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if TYPE_CHECKING:",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
]

# ── ruff ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py312"
extend-exclude = ["alembic/versions"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "F",   # pyflakes
    "E",   # pycodestyle errors
    "W",   # pycodestyle warnings
    "I",   # isort
    "B",   # flake8-bugbear
    "UP",  # pyupgrade
    "N",   # pep8-naming
    "SIM", # flake8-simplify
    "RUF", # ruff-specific
]
ignore = [
    "E501",  # line length — handled by formatter
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**" = ["N802", "N806"]  # allow test function naming flexibility

# ── mypy (strict) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.12"
strict = true
mypy_path = "src"
packages = ["cyberdyne_backend"]
plugins = ["pydantic.mypy"]
exclude = ["alembic/versions"]

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "tests.*"
disallow_untyped_defs = false
disallow_incomplete_defs = false

# reportlab ships no type stubs.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "reportlab.*"
ignore_missing_imports = true

# openpyxl ships no type stubs.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "openpyxl.*"
ignore_missing_imports = true

# yt-dlp ships no type stubs.
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "yt_dlp.*"
ignore_missing_imports = true

name = "omnibase_core"

description = "ONEX Core Framework - Base classes and essential implementations"
authors = [
    {name = "OmniNode.ai", email = "contact@omninode.ai"}
]
license = { text = "MIT" }
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
keywords = [
    "onex",
    "framework",
    "architecture",
    "dependency-injection",
    "base-classes",
    "infrastructure",
    "event-driven",
    "error-handling",
    "node-architecture"
]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 4 - Beta",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3 :: Only",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries :: Application Frameworks",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries :: Python Modules",
    "Typing :: Typed"
]
dependencies = [
    "pydantic>=2.12.5,<3.0.0",
    "pyyaml>=6.0.2,<7.0.0",
    "dependency-injector>=4.49.1,<5.0.0",
    "deepdiff>=8.0.0,<10.0.0",
    "click>=8.3.1,<9.0.0",
    # OMN-15688 (2026-08-04): floor raised to 50.0.0 to clear two HIGH CVEs that
    # Trivy flags on the omninode-runtime image at cryptography 48.0.1 --
    # CVE-2026-69247 (PKCS#7 EnvelopedData decryption exposes a Bleichenbacher
    # oracle through distinguishable errors, fixed 50.0.0) and CVE-2026-69249
    # (duplicate self-signed intermediates cause exponential path-building,
    # fixed 49.0.0). The previous <50.0.0 ceiling made the fixed release
    # unreachable, blocking every runtime candidate rebuild (omnibase_infra
    # build-workspace-candidate-runtime.yml run 30878868464).
    # Platform consequence, decided 2026-09-30: the floor stays. PyPI ships no
    # macOS x86_64 wheel for cryptography 50, so on Intel macOS uv builds it from
    # source, which needs a Rust toolchain and OpenSSL 3 (brew install openssl@3
    # rust, OPENSSL_DIR=$(brew --prefix openssl@3)). Intel macOS is a supported
    # from-source platform, documented in the public Supported Platforms guide
    # and exercised by the nightly install canary. Lowering the floor to get
    # wheels would reopen both CVEs above, so it is not an option.
    "cryptography>=50.0.0,<51.0.0",
    "jsonschema>=4.25.1,<5.0.0",
    "httpx>=0.27.0,<1.0.0",
    "blake3>=1.0.8,<2.0.0",
    "ruamel-yaml>=0.18.0",
    "tree-sitter>=0.25.2,<0.27",
    "tree-sitter-python>=0.25.0,<0.26",
    "pathspec>=0.12.1",
]

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/OmniNode-ai/omnibase_core"
Repository = "https://github.com/OmniNode-ai/omnibase_core"
Documentation = "https://github.com/OmniNode-ai/knowledge_base"

[project.scripts]
onex = "omnibase_core.cli.cli_commands:cli"
# Backward-compatibility alias (renamed from 'omni-agent' to 'onex' in v0.3.0)
omni-agent = "omnibase_core.cli.cli_commands:cli"
# Dev/test runtime host CLI (Phase 1 MVP - LocalHandler only)
# WARNING: For development and testing ONLY, not for production use
omninode-runtime-host-dev = "omnibase_core.cli.cli_runtime_host:main"
# OMN-19405 (typed work ledger T5): the read CLI; folds the JSON-lines ledger at
# ONEX_WORK_LEDGER_PATH and answers one query. Exit 0 CLEAR, 3 HELD/FOUND, 2 UNDECIDED.
onex-work-ledger = "omnibase_core.nodes.node_work_ledger_state_compute.runtime_work_ledger:main"
check-local-paths = "omnibase_core.validation.validator_local_paths:main"
check-github-token-env-reads = "omnibase_core.validation.validator_github_token_env_reads:main"
# OMN-20918 (OCC retirement S8): the imperative contract guard moved from onex_change_control;
# reads the caller's own allowlist and refuses one that gains a path against the merge base.
check-imperative-contracts = "omnibase_core.handlers.handler_imperative_contract_guard_cli:main"
# OMN-19998: refuse a dependency on a repository at the same or a higher layer of
# the declared order, through any channel; every repository runs it via
# .github/workflows/dependency-direction.yml and the pre-commit hook.
check-dependency-direction = "omnibase_core.handlers.handler_dependency_direction_cli:main"
# OMN-19998: version drift at source. Refuse a floor raise on a sibling registry
# package ahead of the registry consumers that install it, and a job the merge
# queue runs that pull request CI skips; every repository runs both via
# .github/workflows/version-drift.yml and the pre-commit hooks.
check-version-floor-consumers = "omnibase_core.handlers.handler_version_floor_consumers_cli:main"
check-merge-queue-parity = "omnibase_core.handlers.handler_merge_queue_parity_cli:main"
# OMN-19998: CI runners are for private repositories only (RULING 2026-10-16T07:07:09Z).
# Refuse a public repository adding a job whose runs-on is, or can resolve to, a
# self-hosted label, against the shrink-only baseline shipped in the package; every
# repository runs it via .github/workflows/version-drift.yml and the pre-commit hook.
check-public-runner-placement = "omnibase_core.handlers.handler_public_runner_placement_cli:main"
# OMN-19998: internal siblings resolve from dev merge tags, never a release, sha or branch.
check-internal-sibling-pins = "omnibase_core.handlers.handler_internal_sibling_pins_cli:main"
# OMN-14401: reject config/registry YAML files declaring duplicate ids over a
# non-unique key (checked registries are config-as-data via a manifest file).
check-duplicate-registry-ids = "omnibase_core.validation.validator_duplicate_config_ids:main"
# OMN-13293 (G1): the same local-paths check executed as a COMPUTE node over the
# in-memory event bus (two-transport seam; Kafka backend in CI). Proven
# equivalent to check-local-paths on the G1 corpus + 6999-file shadow-bake.
check-local-paths-compute = "omnibase_core.nodes.node_local_paths_check_compute.runtime_local_paths_check:main"
# OMN-13294 (G2): hardcoded private-IP (RFC1918) scanner, same COMPUTE/bus seam.
# Generated by node_generation_consumer and corpus-accepted.
check-private-ip-compute = "omnibase_core.nodes.node_private_ip_check_compute.runtime_private_ip_check:main"
# OMN-13497: no-faked-boundary scanner (bans hand-written fakes/stubs of the
# inference/routing/dispatch boundary), same COMPUTE/bus seam. Generated by
# node_generation_consumer and corpus-accepted. Lands report-only.
check-no-faked-boundary = "omnibase_core.validation.no_faked_boundary.runtime_no_faked_boundary:main"
# OMN-13480 (G2, SEA-dogfood): the TODO-marker scanner names its own subject tokens here.  # onex-allow-todo-marker OMN-13480 reason="describes the marker scanner; not agent-left unfinished work"
# scanner, same COMPUTE/bus seam. Generated by node_generation_consumer against the
# live model and corpus-accepted on the first attempt.
check-todo-fixme-marker-compute = "omnibase_core.validation.todo_marker.runtime_todo_marker:main"
# OMN-13509 (G2, SEA-dogfood): sibling pin-hygiene scanner (blocks off-dev-line
# omnibase-core/spi/compat git pins), same COMPUTE/bus seam. Generated by
# node_generation_consumer against the live model and corpus-accepted on the first
# attempt; git ancestry resolved at the EFFECT boundary. PR-time sibling of the
# deploy-time OMN-12977 guard.
check-pin-hygiene-compute = "omnibase_core.validation.pin_hygiene.runtime_pin_hygiene:main"
# OMN-13480 (G2 residual, SEA-dogfood): hardcoded localhost/loopback URL scanner
# (blocks http(s)://localhost / http(s)://127.0.0.1 literals — the loopback
# endpoints url-authority's public-https-literal rule excludes), same COMPUTE/bus
# seam. Generated by node_generation_consumer against the live model and
# corpus-accepted.
check-localhost-url-compute = "omnibase_core.validation.localhost_url.runtime_localhost_url:main"
# OMN-13294 (G2, SEA-dogfood): hardcoded onex.* topic-string scanner (blocks
# pasted onex.<a>.<b>.<c> topic literals that should be contract-declared), same
# COMPUTE/bus seam. Generated by node_generation_consumer against the live model

check-hardcoded-topic-compute = "omnibase_core.nodes.node_hardcoded_topic_check_compute.runtime_hardcoded_topic_check:main"
# OMN-13569: doc-content COMPUTE validator (blocks local-environment traces +

cli = ["psutil>=7.2.1"]
kafka = ["aiokafka>=0.12.0,<1.0.0", "confluent-kafka>=2.12.0,<3.0.0"]
cache = ["redis>=5.0.0,<9.0.0"]
metrics = ["prometheus-client>=0.21.0,<1.0.0"]
sql-parser = ["sqlglot>=26.0.0,<31.0.0"]
# OMN-15789: omnibase_core.event_bus.testing ships real pytest fixtures
# (event_bus_substrate / fidelity_event_bus_substrate) so downstream repos
# can import and extend them by name (see that package's module docstring).
# Declared as its own extra rather than folded into a consumer's existing
# dev dependencies -- pytest/pytest-asyncio become a real import-time
# dependency of that one submodule, so the wheel metadata says so honestly.
testing = ["pytest>=8.4.0", "pytest-asyncio>=1.4,<2"]
full = ["omnibase-spi>=0.20.2", "psutil>=7.2.1", "aiokafka>=0.12.0,<1.0.0", "confluent-kafka>=2.12.0,<3.0.0", "redis>=5.0.0,<9.0.0", "prometheus-client>=0.21.0,<1.0.0", "sqlglot>=26.0.0,<31.0.0", "pytest>=8.4.0", "pytest-asyncio>=1.4,<2"]

[dependency-groups]

    "pytest>=8.4.0",
    "pytest-asyncio>=1.4,<2",
    "mypy>=1.19.1",
    "pyright>=1.1.408",
    "ruff>=0.14.13,<0.18.0",

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/omnibase_core"]

# OMN-18033: the gitignore-baseline spec is repo-root governance data, but the
# validator that reads it is propagated to downstream repos and runs there from
# an isolated pre-commit environment, where architecture-handshakes/ does not
# exist. Ship the one source file inside the wheel rather than copying it into
# twelve repos that would then drift.
[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.force-include]
"architecture-handshakes/gitignore-baseline.yaml" = "omnibase_core/data/gitignore-baseline.yaml"

[tool.hatch.build]
# Include YAML contract files in the wheel for PyPI installs (OMN-6484)
# and the generated feature-flag catalog JSON (OMN-7776).
artifacts = [
    "src/omnibase_core/**/*.yaml",
    "src/omnibase_core/feature_flags/feature_flag_catalog.json",
]

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py312"
line-length = 88
exclude = [
    "**/archived/**",
    "**/archive/**",
    "**/__pycache__/**",
    "**/site-packages/**",
    "tests/fixtures/validation/exports/syntax_error.py",  # Intentionally invalid for testing
    "tests/fixtures/validator_parity/release_identity",  # Data corpus of deliberately invalid pyproject.toml files: ruff parses every nested pyproject.toml it walks past
]

[tool.ruff.format]
# Use black-compatible formatting (ruff format is a drop-in replacement for black)
quote-style = "double"
indent-style = "space"
skip-magic-trailing-comma = false
line-ending = "auto"

[tool.mypy]
# Strict mode enables: warn_return_any, warn_unused_configs, disallow_untyped_defs,
# disallow_incomplete_defs, check_untyped_defs, disallow_untyped_decorators,
# no_implicit_optional, warn_redundant_casts, warn_unused_ignores, strict_equality, and more
strict = true
plugins = ["pydantic.mypy"]
python_version = "3.12"
mypy_path = "src"
namespace_packages = true
explicit_package_bases = true

# Third-party libraries without type stubs
[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "jsonpath_ng.*"
ignore_missing_imports = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "sqlglot.*"
ignore_missing_imports = true

[tool.pydantic-mypy]
init_forbid_extra = true
init_typed = false
warn_required_dynamic_aliases = true
warn_untyped_fields = true

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
pythonpath = ["src", "."]
python_files = ["test_*.py", "*_test.py"]
python_classes = ["Test*"]
python_functions = ["test_*"]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "function"
markers = [
    "unit: Unit tests that test individual components in isolation",
    "integration: Integration tests that test multiple components together",
    "slow: Tests that take a long time to run (>1s)",
    "smoke: Quick smoke tests for basic functionality",
    "performance: Performance and benchmark tests",
    "cache: Cache-related tests",
    "nodes: Node architecture tests",
    "validation: Validation framework tests",
    "flaky: Marks tests as flaky and allows reruns (from pytest-rerunfailures)",
    "timeout: Timeout for individual tests using pytest-timeout plugin (e.g., @pytest.mark.timeout(60))"
]
addopts = [
    "--strict-markers",
    "--strict-config",
    "-ra",
    "--tb=short",
    "-n4",  # Limit parallel workers to prevent OOM (was: auto)
    "--timeout=60",  # Prevent hanging tests (60s per test)
    # OMN-15977: signal-based timeout, NOT thread-based. pytest-timeout's
    # thread method spawns a watcher thread that fires SIGKILL-equivalent only
    # when the GIL is released -- a CPU-bound pure-Python loop holding the GIL
    # continuously (e.g. a runaway regex/compute path) never yields, so the
    # watcher thread never gets scheduled and the "timeout" never fires. This
    # was the unkillable-CPU config behind two 2026-08-12 runaways (46min,
    # 53min) that a health-tick had to SIGKILL manually. Signal method
    # delivers SIGALRM, which interrupts at the next Python bytecode boundary
    # regardless of GIL contention -- it can actually kill a CPU-bound loop.
    "--timeout-method=signal",

    "--dist=loadgroup",  # Group tests by @pytest.mark.xdist_group for better control
    "--reruns=2",  # Auto-retry failed tests twice (handles flaky tests)
    "--reruns-delay=1",  # 1 second delay between reruns
]
filterwarnings = [
    # === Deprecation Warning Capture (OMN-199, Phase 7) ===
    # Display deprecation warnings during test runs so developers can address them
    # before v0.5.0 when these will become errors
    "default::DeprecationWarning",
    "default::PendingDeprecationWarning",
    # Suppress asyncio "Task was destroyed but it is pending!" warnings
    # These are expected during test cleanup when fixtures cancel pending tasks
    # The cleanup fixtures (event_loop_cleanup, cleanup_service_tasks) properly
    # cancel tasks, so these warnings are cosmetic and don't indicate real issues
    "ignore:.*Task was destroyed but it is pending.*:RuntimeWarning",
    # NOTE: "coroutine was never awaited" warnings are NOT suppressed
    # These indicate real bugs where async functions were called but never executed
    # If you encounter this warning, FIX the test by properly awaiting the coroutine
]
# Memory optimization notes:
# - Limited to 4 workers to prevent OOM on machines with 16GB RAM
# - Use --timeout to prevent hanging tests accumulating memory
# - Use --dist=loadscope to group tests by module (reduces import overhead)
# Test execution strategies:
#   Fast iteration: -n 2 --timeout=30
#   Full suite: -n 4 --timeout=60 (default)
#   CI/Large machines: -n 8 --timeout=120
#   Debug single test: -n 0 (disable xdist)
#
# Intelligent test selection with pytest-testmon:
#   Run only affected tests: uv run pytest --testmon
#   Reset testmon database: uv run pytest --testmon-noselect
#   Disable testmon: uv run pytest --testmon-off
#   Note: .testmondata file is gitignored and stores test dependencies

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["src/omnibase_core"]
omit = [
    "*/tests/*",
    "*/archived/*",
    "*/archive/*",
    "*/__pycache__/*",
    "*/site-packages/*"
]
branch = true

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = [
    "pytest>=8.0.0",
    "pytest-asyncio>=0.23.0",
    "pytest-cov>=4.1.0",
]

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["backend"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
pythonpath = ["backend"]
testpaths = ["backend/tests"]
python_files = ["test_*.py"]
python_classes = ["Test*"]
python_functions = ["test_*"]
markers = [
    "unit: Unit tests (fast, no external dependencies)",
    "integration: Integration tests (may require external services)",
]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "function"

[tool.uv.sources]
secretkeeper = { path = "../SecretKeeper/sdk/python" }

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "pytest>=8.0.0",
    "pytest-asyncio>=0.23.0",
    "pytest-cov>=4.1.0",
    "types-requests>=2.32.4.20260107",
    "pyright>=1.1.390",
    "import-linter>=2.11",
]

name = "roost"
dynamic = ["version"]

authors = [

]

]

]

]

]

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/lowkeylabs/roost"
Repository = "https://github.com/lowkeylabs/roost"
Issues = "https://github.com/lowkeylabs/roost/issues"

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = [
    "ruff>=0.6.9",
    "pre-commit>=3.7.0",

    "pytest-cov>=7.0",
    "pyright>=1.1.400",
    "import-linter>=2.3",
    "grimp>=3.11",
]


[project.scripts]
# provide three different names for the CLI entry point
roost    = "owlroost.cli._main:cli"
roost-audit = "owlroost.tools.audit:main"

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling", "hatch-vcs"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

# -------------------------------
# Hatch configuration
# -------------------------------

[tool.hatch.version]
source = "vcs"

[tool.hatch.version.raw-options]
version_scheme = "guess-next-dev"
local_scheme = "node-and-date"


[tool.hatch.metadata]
allow-direct-references = true

[tool.hatch.build]
include = [
  "src/owlroost/conf/**/*.yaml",
]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/owlroost"]



# -------------------------------
# Ruff configuration
# -------------------------------

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py312"
line-length = 100
fix = true

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",   # pycodestyle errors
    "F",   # pyflakes
    "W",   # pycodestyle warnings
    "I",   # import sorting (isort replacement)
    "B",   # flake8-bugbear
    "UP",  # pyupgrade
]
ignore = [
    "E501",  # line length handled pragmatically
    "UP038",
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"__init__.py" = ["F401"]

# -------------------------------
# Ruff formatter (optional but enabled)
# -------------------------------

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
indent-style = "space"
skip-magic-trailing-comma = false
line-ending = "auto"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
minversion = "8.0"
addopts = "-ra --ignore=tests_v1"
testpaths = ["tests"]
pythonpath = ["src"]
python_files = ["test_*.py"]
console_output_style = "progress"

# -------------------------------
# Flexible load of local owl-planner for concurrent development
# -------------------------------
## Use when needing to point to local code.
#[tool.uv.sources]
#owlplanner = { path = "../owl-planner", editable = true }

# -------------------------------
# Coverage
# -------------------------------

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["src/owlroost"]

[tool.coverage.report]
skip_empty = true
show_missing = true

omit = [
    "tests/*",
    "tests_v1/*",
]


# -------------------------------
# Pyright
# -------------------------------

[tool.pyright]
include = ["src", "tests"]

pythonVersion = "3.12"
typeCheckingMode = "basic"

reportMissingImports = true
reportMissingTypeStubs = false

# -------------------------------

imports = true
packages = true

ontology = true

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E", "F", "W",      # pycodestyle, pyflakes
    "I",                # isort
    "UP",               # pyupgrade (enforces the modern type hints CLAUDE.md asks for)
    "B",                # bugbear
    "C4",               # comprehensions
    "SIM",              # simplify
    "RUF",              # ruff-specific
    "ARG",              # unused arguments
    "PTH",              # pathlib
    "PIE", "N", "ERA",  # misc, naming, commented-out code
    "T20",              # no stray prints outside CLI surfaces
    "DTZ",              # naive datetimes (the app reasons in Chicago calendar days)
    "BLE",              # blind except
    "C901", "PLR0911", "PLR0912", "PLR0913", "PLR0915",  # size ceilings (see below)
    "FURB", "PERF",
]
ignore = [
    "E501",    # the formatter owns line length; what remains is long strings and URLs
    "SIM108",  # a ternary is not always clearer
    "SIM905",  # word lists written as one "...".split() string read better than a list literal
]
# Newsletter text uses typographic quotes and dashes; console output uses the info sign.
allowed-confusables = ["–", "‘", "’", "ℹ"]
# DS: tools/lint/check_docstrings.py, so ruff accepts `# noqa: DSNNN`.
external = ["DS"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
# Tests: mock signatures, fixture datetimes, factories with many fields.
"tests/*" = ["ARG001", "ARG002", "DTZ001", "DTZ005", "T20", "PLR0913"]
# CLI surfaces: printing is the job.
"utils/*" = ["T20"]
"tools/*" = ["T20"]
"ingest/email/process_emails.py" = ["T20"]
"ingest/scraper/process_scraped_newsletters.py" = ["T20"]
"notifications/process_notification_queue.py" = ["T20"]
"notifications/weekly_notification_queue.py" = ["T20"]
"notifications/test_matcher.py" = ["T20"]
# Library modules that use print as logging. This list only shrinks: moving one to `logging` removes its line.
"ingest/email/email_parser.py" = ["T20"]
"ingest/scraper/newsletter_scraper.py" = ["T20"]
"notifications/digest_data.py" = ["T20"]
"notifications/rule_matcher.py" = ["T20"]
"processing/llm_client.py" = ["T20"]
"processing/llm_processor.py" = ["T20"]
"processing/weekly_report_generator.py" = ["T20"]
"shared/utils.py" = ["T20"]
# Pydantic fields use these aliases; a `type` statement makes a TypeAliasType,
# which Pydantic turns into a named schema reference instead of the plain type.
"models/types.py" = ["UP040"]
# One-shot maintenance scripts, ratcheted separately from the product.
"utils/calculate_token_costs.py" = ["C901", "PLR0912", "PLR0915"]
"utils/migrate_topics.py" = ["C901", "PLR0912", "PLR0915"]
"utils/cost_report_generator.py" = ["PLR0915"]

# Budget ceilings, not contracts: lower them freely, never raise them.
# Each sits at today's worst function, named in its comment; walk them down by
# splitting that function. tests/unit/test_lint_budgets.py holds them in place.
[tool.ruff.lint.mccabe]
max-complexity = 21   # ingest/email/email_parser.sanitize_content

[tool.ruff.lint.pylint]
max-args = 8          # analytics/terms.compute_distinctive_terms, compute_rising_terms
max-returns = 9       # processing/weekly_report_generator.generate_weekly_topic_report
max-branches = 21     # ingest/email/email_parser.sanitize_content
max-statements = 65   # notifications/process_notification_queue.process_digests


[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["analytics", "config", "ingest", "models", "notifications", "processing", "prompts", "shared", "tools", "utils"]

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["."]
omit = ["tests/*", "tools/*", ".venv/*", "samples/*", "migrations/*"]
branch = true

[tool.coverage.report]
precision = 1
# Erosion backstop, not a target: raise it as coverage rises, keep ~2 pts under.
fail_under = 59
exclude_also = ["if TYPE_CHECKING:", "if __name__ == .__main__.:", "raise NotImplementedError"]

[project]
name = "punt-quarry"
version = "3.4.0"
description = "Extract searchable knowledge from any document. Expose it to LLMs via MCP."
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.13"
license = "MIT"
authors = [
    { name = "Punt Labs" },
]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 4 - Beta",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Topic :: Text Processing :: Indexing",
]
dependencies = [
    "pymupdf>=1.25.0",
    # 0.34.0 is the first release carrying create_index(column, config=...);
    # every earlier version raises TypeError on the call db/schema.py and
    # db/optimizer.py make, so a resolver landing below this floor produces an
    # artifact that imports cleanly and fails at the first index build.
    "lancedb>=0.34.0",
    "tokenizers>=0.20.0",
    "huggingface-hub>=0.26.0",
    "pydantic>=2.0.0",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.0.0",
    # 0.133.0 is the first fastapi that drops its own starlette ceiling
    # (starlette>=0.40.0, unbounded); every earlier release caps starlette below
    # 1.3.1 and so cannot coexist with the secure floor below.
    "fastapi>=0.133.0,<1.0.0",
    "typer>=0.15.0",
    "rich>=13.0.0",
    # Floor is 2.x: the stdio server imports MCPServer from mcp.server.mcpserver,
    # which exists only in mcp 2.x (FastMCP was removed in 2.0). A 1.x install
    # satisfies the range and then fails at import, so the floor must exclude it.
    "mcp>=2.2.0,<3.0.0",
    # 1.3.1 is the first release patched against all five advisories open here:
    # the request.form() DoS and StaticFiles UNC SSRF (high), the Host-header and
    # HTTPEndpoint getattr issues (medium), and request.url.hostname poisoning.
    # No ceiling: the previous <1.0.0 is what made these unfixable by a version
    # bump at all, and fastapi -- which owns far more starlette surface than we
    # do -- carries none. uv.lock is the reproducibility mechanism.
    "starlette>=1.3.1",
    "uvicorn>=0.32.0",
    "websockets>=13.0",
    "pyarrow>=18.0.0",
    "numpy>=1.26.0",
    "Pillow>=10.0.0",
    "python-docx>=1.1.0",
    "tree-sitter>=0.23.0",
    "tree-sitter-language-pack>=0.5.0,<1.0.0",
    "rapidocr>=3.6.0",
    "onnxruntime>=1.18.0",
    "opencv-python-headless>=4.8.0",
    "openpyxl>=3.1.0",
    "python-pptx>=1.0.0",
    "beautifulsoup4>=4.12.0",
    "markdownify>=0.14.0",
    "pathspec>=0.12.0",
    "ultimate-sitemap-parser>=1.8.0",
    "pyyaml>=6.0.0",
    "cryptography>=46.0.0",
    "httpx>=0.27.0",
    # Floor and cap both verified (Copilot, PR #503 round 3): this repo
    # subclasses watchdog's PRIVATE internals (Inotify._add_dir_watch/
    # _add_watch, InotifyBuffer.__init__, InotifyEmitter.on_thread_start --
    # see quarry/daemon/inotify_prune.py, inotify_prune_chain.py), and that
    # subclassed surface was verified only against the installed 6.0.0 (the
    # CI pin test, test_pins_the_watchdog_internals_this_module_subclasses,
    # never ran against an older release). The floor was previously >=4.0,
    # which was ALSO wrong independent of a naming issue Copilot separately
    # caught: fs_watchdog.py imports UnsupportedLibcError unconditionally,
    # but that class is named UnsupportedLibc (no "Error" suffix) through
    # watchdog 4.0.2, the last 4.x release -- confirmed by downloading and
    # inspecting watchdog/utils/__init__.py at 4.0.2 ("class
    # UnsupportedLibc(Exception)") versus 5.0.0 ("class
    # UnsupportedLibcError(Exception)"), so 4.x/5.x resolving under the old
    # floor would have crashed at import time. 6.0.0 is both the version
    # with the correct name AND the only version this module's private
    # internals dependency is verified against, so the floor and the cap
    # meet at the single release actually tested: 6.0.0 is currently
    # watchdog's latest release, so this pin resolves to exactly what CI
    # runs. A future watchdog release bumping either bound is a deliberate,
    # re-verified dependency update, not an automatic one.
    "watchdog>=6.0,<7",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = [
    # 0.15.8 is the first ruff whose S603 stops flagging a subprocess call
    # with fully literal argv (bisected: 0.15.7 flags hooks.py:139, 0.15.8
    # does not).  Below it the repo cannot be green on any single source
    # state: the older ruff demands a `# noqa: S603` there and the newer
    # one rejects that same directive as unused (RUF100).
    "ruff>=0.15.8",
    "mypy>=1.18.1",
    "pyright>=1.1.0",
    "pytest>=8.4.2",
    "pytest-asyncio>=0.23.0",
    "pytest-cov>=6.0.0",
    "pytest-timeout>=2.3.0",
    "types-PyYAML>=6.0.0",
    # Enforces the DES-031 I1 client/engine package boundary (make check-imports).
    "import-linter>=2.0",
]
# Eval-only. NEVER a core dependency, NEVER a dependency of `make check` or any
# CI job. ranx pulls Numba/llvmlite (a C-JIT stack, not pure Python); it must
# stay quarantined here so a compiler-less install of quarry proper is never
# blocked. `make eval` runs `uv sync --extra eval`; nothing else needs it.
# Verified 2026-07-04: resolves + installs + imports on CPython 3.13.5 with
# numba 0.66.0 / llvmlite 0.48.0 wheels (no compiler required).
#
# numpy skew: ranx -> numba caps the resolved numpy to <2.5, so `uv.lock` (and
# thus CI, which installs the locked env) tests against numpy 2.4.6, while the
# shipped wheel and `make test-wheel` resolve numpy 2.5.x unconstrained. This is
# safe — the numpy 2.x C-ABI is stable across 2.4/2.5, so embeddings and search
# behave identically; only the eval harness pins the older numpy.
eval = [
    "ranx>=0.3.20",
]

reportUnknownParameterType = false
reportUnknownVariableType = false

description = "legoESM atmosphere component: hydrostatic/nonhydrostatic/shallow-water dynamical cores (FV3 cube, spectral, SFNO, MPAS) + physics (radiation, convection, turbulence, microphysics, gravity-wave drag)."
readme = "README.md"
license = { text = "MIT" }
requires-python = ">=3.11"
authors = [{ name = "Pierre Gentine" }]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 3 - Alpha",
    "Intended Audience :: Science/Research",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering :: Atmospheric Science",
]
# Depends ONLY on the substrate (legoesm-core) — NOT on the other Earth-system
# components, NOR on the coupler/driver/training above it.  Both invariants are
# machine-enforced by the import-linter contracts ("Earth-system components are
# independent of each other" + "Components must not import the coupler, driver,
# or training"), which is what lets `pip install legoesm-atmosphere` run standalone.
dependencies = [
    "legoesm-core~=1.0.0",
    "jax>=0.5.3",
    "jaxlib>=0.5.3",
    "numpy>=1.26",
    "equinox>=0.11",
    "pyyaml>=6.0",
]

# Optional heavy feature reaching UP into the ML layer.  The BASE atmosphere
# imports only legoesm-core (verified: `import legoesm.atmosphere` does not pull
# ml), so the component stays standalone; this extra declares the install path
# for the SFNO/U-Cast neural dynamical cores + ML physics parameterization, which
# import the neural primitives at top level:
#   atmosphere.dynamics.{sfno_sw,sfno_pe,ucast_pe} and
#   atmosphere.physics.ml_parameterization
#   -> legoesm.ml.{sfno,ucast,normalization,channel_packing,conservation,physics.*}
# Install with `pip install legoesm-atmosphere[ml]`.  These component->ml edges
# are baselined in import-linter contract #3.
[project.optional-dependencies]
ml = ["legoesm-ml~=1.0.0"]

[tool.uv.sources]
legoesm-core = { workspace = true }
legoesm-ml = { workspace = true }

# This component PROVIDES the FV3 shallow-water barotropic dycores that the ocean
# component's barotropic solver resolves BY NAME through
# legoesm.registry.SW_BAROTROPIC_REGISTRY (importlib.metadata entry points — NOT a
# static import).  Declaring them here means installing legoesm-atmosphere makes
# the ocean reuse the SAME shallow-water dycore (zero duplication) without either
# component importing the other.
[project.entry-points."legoesm.sw_barotropics"]
fv3sw = "legoesm.atmosphere.dynamics.shallow_water_fv3_cdgrid:_build_fv3sw_barotropic_model"
fv3edge = "legoesm.atmosphere.dynamics.shallow_water_fv3_cdgrid:_build_fv3edge_barotropic_model"

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling>=1.32.4", "hatch-vcs>=0.5"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[project]
name = "terok-executor"
description = "Single-agent task runner for hardened Podman containers"
readme = "README.md"
license = "Apache-2.0"
authors = [
    {name = "Jiri Vyskocil", email = "jiri@vyskocil.com"},
]
maintainers = [
    {name = "Jiri Vyskocil", email = "jiri@vyskocil.com"},
]
keywords = ["podman", "containers", "agent", "ai", "coding-agent"]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 3 - Alpha",
    "Environment :: Console",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "Intended Audience :: System Administrators",
    "Operating System :: POSIX :: Linux",
    "Programming Language :: Python",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Quality Assurance",
    "Typing :: Typed",
]
requires-python = ">=3.12,<3.15"
dynamic = ["version"]
# Dependency pins follow the policy in AGENTS.md ("Dependency Pinning &
# pyproject.toml Hygiene").  Keep the dependency list comment-free.
dependencies = [
    "terok-sandbox @ https://github.com/terok-ai/terok-sandbox/releases/download/v0.7.0a1/terok_sandbox-0.7.0a1-py3-none-any.whl",
    "terok-util>=0.4.0,<0.5.0",
    "ruamel.yaml==0.19.1",
    "Jinja2~=3.1",
    "tomli-w~=1.2",
    "prompt-toolkit~=3.0",
    "pydantic~=2.13",
    "rich~=15.0",
    "agent-client-protocol==0.12.1",
]

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://terok-ai.github.io/terok-executor/"
Repository = "https://github.com/terok-ai/terok-executor"
Documentation = "https://terok-ai.github.io/terok-executor/"
Issues = "https://github.com/terok-ai/terok-executor/issues"
Changelog = "https://github.com/terok-ai/terok-executor/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md"
Security = "https://github.com/terok-ai/terok-executor/security/policy"

[project.scripts]
terok-executor = "terok_executor.cli:main"

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "pre-commit>=4.0",
    "ruff>=0.16,<0.18",
    "bandit>=1.7",
    "docstr-coverage>=2.3.2,<3",
    "complexipy>=6.0.1",
    "vulture>=2.12",
    "reuse>=6.2.0,<7",
    "tach>=0.35.0,<0.36",
    "mypy>=2.1.0,<3.0",
    "import-linter>=2.13",
]
test = [
    "pytest>=9.1.1",
    "pytest-cov>=4.0",
    "pytest-timeout>=2.0",
]
docs = [
    "properdocs>=1.6.7",
    "mkdocs-material>=9.7.6",
    "mkdocstrings[python]>=0.26",
    "mkdocs-gen-files>=0.5",
    "mkdocs-literate-nav>=0.6",
    "mkdocs-section-index>=0.3",
    "mkdocs-terok~=0.8.0",
]

[tool.uv]
default-groups = ["dev", "test"]

[tool.hatch.metadata]
allow-direct-references = true

[tool.hatch.version]
source = "vcs"
fallback-version = "0.5.1a1"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/terok_executor"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
python_files = ["test_*.py"]
python_classes = ["Test*", "*Tests"]
python_functions = ["test_*"]
addopts = "-v --tb=short"
markers = [
  "needs_podman: requires podman on the host",
]

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py312"
line-length = 100
src = ["src", "tests"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
  "E",      # pycodestyle errors
  "W",      # pycodestyle warnings
  "F",      # pyflakes
  "I",      # isort
  "B",      # flake8-bugbear
  "C4",     # flake8-comprehensions
  "UP",     # pyupgrade
  "SIM",    # flake8-simplify
]
ignore = [
  "E501",   # line too long (handled by formatter)
  "B904",   # raise from in except
  "SIM102", # nested if statements
  "SIM105", # contextlib.suppress vs try/except/pass
  "SIM108", # use ternary operator
  "SIM117", # nested with statements
]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**" = ["E402"]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["terok_executor"]
combine-as-imports = true

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
indent-style = "space"
docstring-code-format = true

# Static type checking -- see `make typecheck`.
# ``resources/`` is excluded entirely: it holds container-side scripts and
# bundled agent assets that aren't part of the host-side import graph
# (``resources/toad-agents/`` isn't even a valid Python package name).
[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.12"
files = ["src/terok_executor"]
exclude = "src/terok_executor/resources/"
ignore_missing_imports = true
check_untyped_defs = true
warn_unused_ignores = true
warn_redundant_casts = true
warn_unreachable = true
no_implicit_optional = true
strict_equality = true
disallow_untyped_defs = true
disallow_incomplete_defs = true
pretty = true
show_error_codes = true

# ``resources/`` holds container-side scripts (run inside task containers, not
# part of the host import graph -- the same reason mypy excludes it).  Tests
# exercise them by path-loading (``SourceFileLoader``), which coverage.py can't
# attribute, so they report 0%; omit them rather than chase phantom misses.
[tool.coverage.run]
omit = ["*/terok_executor/resources/*"]
